## 2026-08-05 [product]: The contingent pay-gate is retired and its construct test relocated; H-BuildRightThing splits. **The event channel and the ICP widening are filed PROPOSED-PENDING-CONTACT, not applied.** **UNTESTED.**

> **CORRECTION, same day — applied after an adversarial segmentation review.** As first written, this entry **applied** an `active-market-focus` move (co-founder pairs → "teams with many developers") and an `active-channel` move (direct-first → event-led) on **deductive grounds only**: send-capacity arithmetic and the Min Principle. That violates the slot-move gate recorded 2026-07-29 [product] — a `SINGLE-VALUE` slot moves only on *"a named human and a date… collected since that slot last moved"*, and its anti-laundering clause covers anything that changes who the next outreach targets. **Worse, the identical move was already refused:** 2026-07-29 Decision 2 filed *"engineering teams ~10-50"* as **PROPOSED-PENDING-CONTACT** because *"the reasoning is deductive and the one qualifying datum does not support it."* This entry re-proposed it under a different label without citing the refusal or supplying the missing datum. **Both slot moves are hereby demoted to PROPOSED-PENDING-CONTACT.** What remains *applied* below: items 4, 5 and 6 — the pay-gate retirement (which *executes* the 2026-07-24 fixed-price-install decision rather than moving a slot), the -Sell/-Cause split (`hypotheses.md` is a bet-list, not a single-valued slot), and the ladder/diagnose-free-treat-paid principle. **Review findings that must be answered before either slot moves — none engaged in the original entry:**
> - **"Large orgs have already bought process"** (2026-07-29, same entry) and the 2026-07-22 ADR-sourcing rejection — *"a team publishing numbered ADRs… has already built a decision protocol; they are among the least likely buyers."* Engineering is the function with the **most** installed comprehension-verification machinery (code review, PR gates, ADRs, retros), so widening toward developers moves **toward** the substitute. The canvas already names closed-loop readback as *"the closer relative for the work domain."*
> - **The Min Principle is being over-applied.** "Joint comprehension ≤ min" plus "min degrades with N" does not yield "bigger teams are better customers" — that needs three further premises (the degradation is felt *and attributed to understanding*; it is not already handled; someone with budget owns it). All three have counter-evidence here. And the cited articles themselves file the monotonic decay as an **unsolved defect** (`a29`: heckler's-veto at scale; `a39`: *"conservative to the point of uselessness"*), while the community-Min is recorded unsolved (2026-07-24). The only field datum on a dev team records the instrument **breaking at 6–7 people** (H-ProtocolSpreadsWithoutTool).
> - **`product↔team lead` is adjacent to a pair already rejected on the merits** — H-SalesProductAlignment, rejected 2026-07-26 for reproducing the buyer≠subject friction plus an interest conflict verification can surface but not resolve. Not mentioned in the original entry.
> - **The employment-asymmetry bound was scoped as delivery-only risk *because the free audit was solo 1:1*.** Making `team lead↔developer` the **entry** pair moves the asymmetry onto the sale. That scope bound was never re-derived.
> - **Buyer ≠ sufferer:** *"in a 10-50 product company the buyer is a VP Eng or CTO while ICs feel the pain — cost-insulation, an existing disqualifier"* (2026-07-29). Co-founder pairs were chosen partly *because* buyer and subject coincide by consent.
> - **The canvas's second, independent rationale does not generalize.** Beyond the theory-of-change argument this entry addressed, `lean-canvas.md` grounds the co-founder pair on *"reference network of 2 (no regression to the mean)"* — a property that **weakens monotonically with team size**, i.e. the widening's own mechanism attacks it.
> - **"Bigger market" is asserted, never sized** — `lean-canvas.md` §Market Size → Active focus is *"UNTESTED, unsized."* And the longer sales cycle was accepted without re-deriving the standing *"fail 90-day hard ceiling."*
> - **The stronger alternative is already written down with a verbatim buyer quote and is unused** — 2026-07-29: *"the sharper qualifier is a **trigger, not a headcount** — teams whose throughput outgrew their coordination process,"* interviewee verbatim *"if you're shipping 5 times the things… the process breaks."* Testable question: *"did your shipping rate change faster than how you plan?"* It is acute rather than chronic (the canvas: *"chronic pain rarely opens a budget line. Acute, dated events do"*), it carries attested buyer language where **"rework" is unattested — 0 of 30 competitor heroes, 0 of 3,671 transcript lines** — and it supplies the STATE layer the ICP-5 was proven insufficient without.
>
> **Process consequence:** the gate's own enforcement is the failure. `/docs-strategy-update` Gate 2 greps for a literal `LOCKED:` marker; this gate is recorded in `decisions.md` prose and carries none, so the grep returned "0 matches" and read as permission. **Either the 2026-07-29 gate gets `LOCKED:` markers at the three slots, or Gate 2 must grep `PROPOSED-PENDING-CONTACT` / `slot is frozen` as well.** `[FOUNDER DECISION]` — and until it exists this will recur, because it just did.

**Context:** A long GTM session that started from the founder's stated blocker — *"I don't see how it makes any commercial sense long term, and I don't want to be in a rat race"* — and worked backwards through the arithmetic rather than forwards from the offer. Three things fell out, and a fourth (a stale hand-off) had been sitting unreconciled for 12 days.

**Decision:**

1. **Cold 1:1 outreach is retired as the front door — on send-capacity, not on economics.** With the founder's own rates (2% answer × 25% call × 25% report × 30% install = 0.0375% compound), 3 installs need ~8,000 messages. Automated sending makes the €/hr *flat* across response rates, so the response rate is a **feasibility** threshold, not an economic one. LinkedIn's ~100/week connection cap (approximate, unverified this session) turns 8,000 into ~80 weeks; a one-quarter deadline would require a ~12% reply rate. **LinkedIn becomes a sourcing surface only; email is the send channel if cold runs at all.**
2. **The front door is a free 1-to-many discussion event, fishbowl format.** Poll positions → argue without the protocol → argue with it → reflection. 2–4 people speak, everyone votes. Breakouts are rejected at the free tier (unobservable, unorchestrable with strangers) and moved behind the paywall. Rationale for fishbowl over breakouts is Bicchieri, and it is the project's own H-NormFlip: norms install through **observed** compliance, so a fishbowl produces *"everybody saw that everybody saw"* while ten private breakouts produce ten private experiences and no common knowledge. Corroborated by an existing field learning — [theory-of-change.md](theory-of-change.md) 2026-03-29: *"Events demonstrate; conversion happens when participant brings it home."*
3. **The ICP widens from co-founder pairs to teams with many developers**, entering via cross-functional pairs (team lead↔developer, product↔team lead), not founders. Argument is the Min Principle already filed as `a29`/`a39`: joint comprehension is bounded by the **minimum**, not the average, so it degrades mechanically with team size — bigger teams carry more of the pain and less of the self-diagnosis. Co-founder pairs have the highest stakes *per* decision but the fewest decisions and the smallest rework surface. Trade accepted: bigger pain and bigger market, bought with a longer sales cycle. **The event door stays open to anyone; only the message targets narrowly** — "anyone who works with AI" is the absence of a targeting criterion, not a criterion.
4. **The contingent pay-gate is retired and its construct test relocated.** The gate conflated two questions and priced one to test the other — *does the construct exist* (do teams carry important unsurfaced gaps?) versus *will they pay* — which is precisely why it put delivery risk on the founder. Applying the 2026-07-24 supersession that was never reconciled. **The construct test moves off the price and onto measurement:** (a) **prevalence** — the live event poll (*"how many times last quarter did you rebuild something after discovering you'd understood the decision differently?"*), free, n grows weekly; (b) **surfacing** — at each install, record whether the gap that surfaced was one the team **did not already know about**. Founder's own objection accepted: a self-reported rebuild count validates nothing about the *mechanism*, so it is a **qualifier that routes people, not evidence**.
5. **H-BuildRightThing splits.** It fuses two claims with different test horizons: **-Sell** (people buy against the rework problem statement — testable now, by the event and the first sales) and **-Cause** (unverified understanding is what *causes* the rework — testable only after installs accumulate). Writing them apart removes a fake test instead of replacing it with another one.
6. **Ladder: free event → paid event (bring one person) → team install; paid intro hour for the unqualified.** Replaces the €300 "gap audit," which was unpriceable because it had no market comparable — the founder had to invent the value, defend it, and guess at WTP, which is the mechanical reason he could not tell whether it was worth €300. Workshop tickets and coaching hours both have comparables. Governing line unchanged from 2026-07-24: **diagnose free, treat paid** — so the 30-min scoping call is free and nobody ever pays to describe their own need. All prices `[FOUNDER DECISION]`.

**Falsifier:** (a) fewer than ~15 registrations from 2,000 cold emails (<0.75%) ⟹ cold email cannot fill a room; revert to platform-supplied audience (Luma/Eventbrite) or warm-only. (b) Event attendees consistently report 0–1 rebuilds ⟹ the prevalence claim under H-BuildRightThing-Sell is weak and the problem statement is aimed at a symptom the target does not have. (c) Installs only ever surface gaps the team already knew about ⟹ H-BuildRightThing-Cause fails on the surfacing leg. (d) If the program (pairs) does not sell, the 1-to-many funnel is **worse** than 1:1 on every axis except content residue — the event's entire arithmetic advantage lives in the program price, not in the install path.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) **Reduce the target from 3 installs to 1** — makes LinkedIn viable at 5%+ and cuts an 80-week program to 11 weeks, but the founder rejected it on the grounds that the point is a scalable motion, not an answer. (b) **Hybrid physical/online events** — rejected on a product-specific ground, not logistics: in-room attendees hold side-channel information online attendees cannot verify, so the format contradicts the demonstration it exists to run. Chiang Mai physical stays a separate event, not a hybrid arm. (c) **An agent auto-answering LinkedIn messages** — it automates 13 of 140 hours, changes the calendar by zero (the cap binds, not reply time), risks ToS on the account holding the warm network, and hands away the first 160 objections, which are the data. Agent-drafts / founder-sends survives. (d) **Questionnaire as a pre-call disqualifier** — already rejected as P989 (2026-07-15); the two-party variant is worse and filters when the bottleneck is volume. (e) **Three CTAs from stage** — rejected as stacked; accepted as *segmented*, one spoken primary with three-way routing in the follow-up.

**Consequences:** `hypotheses.md` H-BuildRightThing needs the pay-gate test replaced and the -Sell/-Cause split written; `lean-canvas.md` §Customer Segments (the seed–A co-founder-pair "Who") and the page-lead CTA (*"Free alignment audit / contingent POC as the only CTA"*) are stale; `goals.md` still carries the contingent-POC core outcome and the €1500 floor. **`theory-of-change.md` "explains why the co-founder pair is the natural first market" is now a stale label, NOT a contradiction** — its own argument (long-loop, high-stakes coordination with delayed feedback and invisible error) generalizes to dev teams *more strongly*, so the reasoning survives the ICP widening and only the market label needs updating. H-WorkshopFormat has been `Active P1 / "first workshop imminent"` since **2026-04-02** with **zero workshops run**, so its transform-if (`<10% conversion after 3 workshops`) has never been reachable — the denominator is 0. `/align` is redefined by the founder as **transcript → letter**, not two-forms → three-numbers; it lives at the paid event and the install, **not** as a free-event CTA, because handing a stranger a tool to use with an absent third party recreates the exact condition behind the letter's R₀≈0 result.

**Open — the R₀≈0 datum is contested and was NOT resolved here.** The founder states most of the 18 letters were never sent and those that were mostly got completed. Two readings survive: the **denominator** was wrong (`0/18` should have been `0/N_sent`), or the **definition** was doing the work (the metric counted *async, unprompted* completions, which a nudged completion correctly excludes). One query settles it — of the 18, how many were delivered, how many recipients filled their side, and how many did so with no founder prompt. The number is referenced in `lean-canvas.md` ×5, `hypotheses.md` ×4, and `progress.md` ("Killed 2026-06-02"); the coach-channel pivot it triggered was already demoted 2026-07-03, so the live exposure is limited. `[FOUNDER DECISION]` on whether to run the query.

## 2026-08-05 [process]: Cross-skill references rot silently — inline the borrowed steps instead

**Context:** While building `/problemify`, the design called for referencing `/dd:frame`'s Steps 3–5 (A→B→obstacle, 5-why) rather than restating them, per Reference Over Duplication. A hostile reviewer challenged whether a cross-skill *step* reference is even executable. Grepping the referrers settled it: `/dd:frame-analyze` is cited in `build/pick-flow/SKILL.md:50,161`, `build/reproduce/SKILL.md:357`, and `docs/decisions.md:11448` — but the command's actual name is `dd:frame` (`dd/frame-analyze.md:2`). **Four dead references to a command that never existed under that name, none caught by any gate.** Nothing tests that a `/skill-name` mentioned in prose resolves.

**Decision:** Reference Over Duplication does **not** extend to instruction-level references between skill files. A skill may cite another skill as *related* (routing, "use X instead"), but must **inline** any steps it needs the agent to execute. Reversed the `/problemify` design mid-build and inlined ~10 lines.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Reference by step number — strictly worse than by name: `dd/frame-analyze.md` is v2.0.0 from a frame+analyze merge, so its numbering already shifted once and any insertion renumbers silently. (b) Fix the four dead references now — real automation debt, but out of scope for this session; recorded here rather than scope-crept.

**Consequences:** The general form: a reference is safe when a *human reading it* is the consumer, and unsafe when an *agent executing it* is. Two further hazards this surfaced: the referenced file carries constraints the referrer doesn't want (`dd/frame-analyze.md:194` forbids evaluating whether an obstacle is real, which contradicts `/problemify`'s core move) and the agent has no precedence rule between the two. **Status: proposed** — no mechanical check exists that skill-name references resolve; a lint over `/[a-z:-]+` mentions against the skill registry would catch all four.

**References:** [problemify](~/.claude/commands/slava/think/problemify.md) · [pick-flow](.claude/commands/slava/build/pick-flow/SKILL.md) · [skills.md](.claude/rules/skills.md)

## 2026-08-05 [process]: A skill covering 75% of a requested one is a routing failure, not a green light to fork

**Context:** The founder asked for `/problemify` (formulate A→B→obstacle, 5-why the obstacle, offer alternative problem formulations), noting he had "asked this many many times." `/create-skill`'s duplication check found `/dd:frame` already does A→B→obstacle (Step 3), structural root cause with cited evidence (Step 4), 5-why (Step 5), and a source registry — ~75% of the ask, and documented as a standalone entry point. This is the second instance in three days of proposing to build what already ships (`/goal`, 2026-08-03).

**Decision:** Built a thin sibling rather than extending `/dd:frame`, on one specific ground: `dd/frame-analyze.md:194` forbids evaluating whether an obstacle is real — it must "name them as hypotheses" for the downstream conjecture agent. `/problemify`'s core move is *rendering a verdict* on the stated obstacle. Extending would have given one skill two contradictory postures about whether it may judge. `/dd:frame` stays the pipeline phase; `/problemify` is the standalone verdict, chat-only, terminating in an act.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Extend `/dd:frame` — rejected on the contradiction above, plus its standalone mode emits a T-numbered file, scoring criteria, and a note-for-conjecture-agent, all wrong weight mid-conversation. (b) Build as originally specced — would have silently replaced `/dd:frame`, since global `CLAUDE.md:85-86` registers `think:falsify` and `think:adversarial-review` but **zero `/dd:*` skills**, so the registered sibling wins every routing contest.

**Consequences:** The founder's felt need recurring "many many times" while a 75%-covering skill sat unused is evidence of a *discoverability* failure, not a missing tool — which is why the new skill is thin and heavily cross-referenced rather than another full pipeline. Two registry gaps remain open: `/dd:*` is absent from global `CLAUDE.md`, and `think/route.md:40` is stale (lists `/create-prd`, `/design-audit`; omits all `/dd:*` and `/adversarial-review`). **Status: proposed** — both need the `/slava:maintain:claude-md` gate, not a direct edit.

## 2026-08-04 [product]: The field adopter dropped the score because his team never agreed to it — an unconsented-condition failure, not a measurement failure

**Context:** The 2026-07-14 field datum (unsolicited practitioner, sustained tool-free use, dropped the sealed-bid score) has been cited repeatedly — including by me, twice this session — as evidence that *the number gets discarded in the wild*, feeding the open "is the number load-bearing" sub-bet under H-PopperianIncrement. **The founder offered a candidate explanation, and flagged it himself as a conjecture rather than a finding:** the practitioner's team members never accepted the protocol, so he may have been imposing the number on non-consenters. **The practitioner was never asked why he dropped it.** Whether a consenting team would also drop it is equally unobserved. Both branches are open.

**Decision — hold the datum as ambiguous rather than as evidence against the number, and record the ambiguity where the bet lives.** The prior reading ("the number gets discarded in the wild") asserted a cause nobody checked; the consent reading is a *second* candidate cause, not a replacement finding. What changes is the confidence, not the direction: this datum is **too confounded to move the number sub-bet either way**, and the cheapest resolution is one question to the practitioner. Pending that, it joins two other cases pointing the same direction: the founder's own CPA dyad (agreed → sustained, useful, energy-costly, continues) and unprompted strangers (not agreed → rejected as intrusive, sometimes as *robotic*). Read together, the three are corroboration of **philosophy.md §2 scope condition 2** — nothing in paraphrasing supplies the will to start paraphrasing; the pre-commitment does — which the 2026-08-03 Gottman pass had already judged *"the one bound that is independently supported and not an anomaly-absorber."* **Rejected alternative:** continuing to file it under "the number is contested." That framing survived three retellings because nobody asked why he dropped it, and it was quietly recruiting a consent failure as measurement evidence.

**Consequence for the unit of spread.** If agreement is the load-bearing part, then the transmissible unit is the **agreement**, not the question — and "did they ask 0–10" is the wrong success metric, because it is the component most likely to be dropped exactly where consent is absent. Corrected metric split, after the founder caught the first version as circular ("if install = CPA signed and signing ends a paid install, it measures compliance"): **persistence** = the installed pair runs it on a live decision with the founder absent and it is still happening at ~4 weeks (what the install can prove; H-ProtocolTransfers' actual falsifier); **transmission** = the practice reaches someone never onboarded (the R₀ number, never above zero). **And transmission must be instrumented to count** — the founder's objection is correct: an untracked second-degree adoption is unobservable, so the only countable forms are a signed agreement or a letter created by an un-onboarded author. *This is the first non-decorative argument for the product surface: not a front door (falsified, R₀≈0 — H-LetterAsProduct) but the **telemetry** that makes R₀ measurable at all.*

**Also corrected here:** hypotheses.md rendered the practitioner's report as a quoted **"zero rework"** he did not literally say (he said nothing comes back for rework). Flagged as an open `/docs-strategy-update` job in [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-28 and unfixed since; now paraphrased with the correction noted inline.

**Falsifier:** run the protocol with a team that *has* pre-agreed and they drop the number anyway ⟹ the consent explanation is wrong and the number genuinely is the weak component. **Second falsifier:** a signed agreement or an authored letter appears from someone never onboarded, and the practice around it turns out not to include the paraphrase check ⟹ the agreement is not the transmissible unit either.

**Evidence grade:** n=1 re-read, founder-supplied, **UNTESTED** — the consenting-team case has never been observed.

**References:** [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-ProtocolSpreadsWithoutTool (evidence row — where the re-reading is recorded) · [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-17 [product] (the original split) · 2026-07-28 (the misquote flag) · [philosophy.md](philosophy.md) §2 scope condition 2 · `content/articles/a48_the-user-who-dropped-the-numbers.md`.

## 2026-08-04 [product]: "Gap" needs a criterion or it is a house style — 18 candidates prune to 3, and Weaver failing the test is the better outcome

**Context:** Conversation-analysis window 2026-08-03→04 (2 CP-relevant conversations). Two independent conversations on consecutive days flagged the same hazard in the project's habit of naming each thinker-conjecture a *Gap*: **three instances is where a genuine pattern and a rhetorical template become indistinguishable from outside** — "someone will notice the shape before they evaluate the content, and the template reading is cheaper for them than the pattern reading." `lean-canvas.md` §Channels holds a live plan for **18** such events. **Evidence grade: conversation-sourced, n=0, UNTESTED** — no field data in this window; nothing below has been read in primary.

**Decision 1 — adopt a 3-part criterion for what counts as a gap.** All three required: (a) the framework's central result has a precondition involving mutual understanding; (b) the author left that precondition unspecified; (c) without it, the result weakens or fails. Applying it: **Aumann strongest** — common knowledge is an *explicit premise* of the theorem, not a buried presupposition, so the claim is "your stated antecedent is never satisfied," which is formal and checkable. **Popper strong.** **Deutsch moderate** (in-principle claim, so "no stopping rule" is a consequence rather than an oversight). Pinker moderate, Edmondson plausible, Locke weaker. **Bicchieri and Ostrom are not gaps at all.** Recommendation carried into the canvas: **three gap articles maximum**; everything else is event material, where repetition is a feature.

**Decision 2 — Weaver fails criterion (b), and that is the stronger position.** The claim we were about to make — *Level B was named in 1949 and never operationalized* — **will not survive contact with the literature**: Bar-Hillel & Carnap 1952 (with Floridi's veridicality repair), Juba & Sudan 2008, the 6G semantic/goal-oriented communication programme that cites Weaver's Levels B and C as its literal charter and has been funded since ~2021, and the cloze procedure (Taylor 1953) descending from Shannon's 1951 guessing experiments. Weaver also did not merely name the level — he proposed a *semantic receiver* and *semantic noise*, and asserted Shannon's math would generalize upward, which Shannon himself warned against in the 1956 "Bandwagon" editorial. **Since Weaver said outright he was not solving Level B, we cannot claim discovery — we can claim to have filled a stated open problem, which is cleaner and far less contestable. Rejected alternative:** claiming the Weaver Gap as a third or fourth gap. **The reframe that survives, and does more work:** *every operationalization of Level B installs a third party who already knows the answer* — a logician holding state descriptions, a designer holding the task metric, an examiner holding the key, a confederate knowing the referent. Remove the omniscient third party and Level B has no instrument. Falsifiable in the right direction (produce a two-party no-referee instrument to defeat it) and structurally identical to the Min Principle. **Bound:** Weaver's Level B as phrased is one-directional (sender intent vs receiver uptake); a joint quantity bounded by the weaker of two self-reports sits between B and C, so claiming Level B outright mislocates what we have.

**Decision 3 — the Popper Gap / Deutsch Gap pair is a definitions-layer fact, because "stopping rule" now names three different constructs.** Popper Gap = **whether a given test counts** (failure mode: false confidence — you think you were tested and weren't). Deutsch Gap = **when to stop testing** (failure mode: misallocation — quitting on something soluble, or persisting on something that isn't). They compose **one way only**: fixing the Popper Gap is a precondition for the Deutsch Gap being answerable, not the reverse. The object is stated as *when to accept divergence with a specific person as final* — a stopping rule over a **social** process with a counterparty who can be queried — **not** "when to abandon a research programme," which invites an easy objection and collides with the programme-level stopping rule in P1026. Third construct already in `definitions.md` §Problem-Statement Clarity: when a *builder* stops seeking clarity and acts. **Rejected alternative:** philosophy.md — that doc holds the epistemological foundation and testable conjectures; a naming collision is glossary work, and §Problem-Statement Clarity already performs exactly this disambiguation against the Verification Threshold.

**Correction recorded — a misgraded anomaly reached the founder and would have reached an article.** The 2026-08-02 conversation presented the Munich Marital Study as *"well controlled… a well-controlled study, in your exact domain, with a negative result"*, concluded *"the burden is on you now"*, and recommended making scored-vs-performed verification the top hypothesis on that basis. **This project verified the opposite the following morning** (2026-08-03 entry below, adversarially reviewed by five hostile reviewers): Munich/Hahlweg is **not cited in the 1998 paper**, the comparison groups are **non-randomized, self-selected non-participants**, and this project **declines to bank that evidence in either direction**; `philosophy.md` §2 scope condition 3 grades the same comparison "UNTESTED, weakest of the three." The conversation was still open after the correction landed. **The recommendation survives on other grounds** — `decisions.md` 2026-08-03 [process] already moved H-PopperianIncrement to the front of the scientific test queue as the rival-discriminator against P1026 rival (a), `[FOUNDER DECISION on priority]` still open — **but the warrant does not, and the warrant is what would have gone into the article.** Both new a-specs carry an explicit do-not-repeat flag. Noted for the record: the same conversation correctly warned that "it escalates now but de-escalates later" is a degenerating move — an auxiliary absorbing an anomaly with no novel prediction — while the anomaly it urged absorbing was itself misgraded.

**Also rejected this pass (the against-argument winning):** (a) filing a new hypothesis for "measure predicted-vs-actual paraphrase accuracy and perceived resolvability in groups reporting stuck" — hypotheses.md holds 42 UNTESTED blocks with none promoted; this belongs in P1026's **Novel-prediction field** on H-PopperianIncrement, the field P1026 exists to introduce. (b) Adding the omniscient-third-party reframe to the canvas — it is a sharper articulation of a structural claim already recorded three times (a9 "Aumann's missing instrument", a35 "black-boxes meaning-verification", a29 Min Principle); routed to content instead. (c) Recording Gottman's "~69% perpetual problems" figure against the founder's in-chat aggregation claim (*"a relationship is a collection of successes/failures on all the small matters"*) — `philosophy.md` §2 **already** forbids the aggregation claim (*"the postulate claims active listening makes falsification possible, not that it improves outcomes"*), so the doc is right and no edit is needed; and the figure is secondary-source Gottman framing, which is exactly the class that cost an adversarial pass on 2026-08-03.

**Falsifier (Decision 1):** publish the three surviving gap articles and a reader or reviewer identifies the form as a template anyway — or, inversely, a pruned candidate (Edmondson, Locke, Pinker) is independently argued by someone else as a genuine gap of this shape ⟹ the criterion is either not sufficient or is cutting real claims, and the three-maximum constraint drops.
**Falsifier (Decision 2):** someone produces a two-party, no-referee instrument for Level B ⟹ the third-party observation is wrong and the Weaver line loses its payload.
**Falsifier (Decision 3):** the two gaps turn out to compose in both directions — a case where knowing when to stop testing changes whether a given test counts ⟹ the one-way composition is wrong and they are one construct, not two.

**Consequences:** `definitions.md` §Problem-Statement Clarity gains the gap pair + the three-stopping-rules disambiguation; `lean-canvas.md` §Channels "Future: Conjecture-Event Series" gains the criterion and a second, distinct risk (the *form* discounts the real claims — separate from the already-recorded "preparation becomes its own refinement loop"). Articles filed: `content/articles/a64_the-stopping-rule-nobody-specified.md` (ARC-4, the Deutsch Gap), `content/articles/a65_three-gaps-not-eighteen.md` (ARC-1, the criterion + the pruning); `a35` enriched with the Aumann interpretation-layer diagnosis. **Unresolved and surfaced separately:** the contingent-POC pay-gate named in the 2026-08-03 [process] entry as the programme's progressivity discriminator was superseded by the 2026-07-24 fixed-price-install decision, whose reconciliation hand-off was never run — `goals.md`, `hypotheses.md` H-BuildRightThing, and `lean-canvas.md` still carry the contingent framing. `[FOUNDER DECISION]`, not resolved here.

**References:** [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-08-03 [product] (the Gottman research pass this corrects against) · 2026-08-03 [process] (P1026 rigor layer; H-PopperianIncrement priority) · 2026-07-24 [product] (fixed-price install — the unreconciled supersession) · [philosophy.md](philosophy.md) §2 scope conditions · [features/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md).

## 2026-08-03 [product]: Flip rate exists in prod and already discriminates — but the corpus has 6 reader flips, and the binding constraint is the missing second position, not verification cost

**Context:** A session on "fitness of ideas" proposed a chain — score stories by flip rate → expose an API → run a challenge where authors compete to produce flips → flips build author reputation. Before designing any of it, the corpus was measured on **prod** (read-only, REST + anon key), scoped to the `#understanding` / `#misunderstanding` / `st1–st9` system-tagged points. Three assumptions held going in; the data broke two.

**What the measurement found** (29 points, 349 `point_position_history` rows, Mar–Jul 2026):

1. **Verification friction is not what blocks flip data.** **0 of 349** position-history rows carry a `session_id` — every recorded position change in the project's history happened *outside* a `/live` clarity session. The stated worry ("a second position requires me to run a session") is false for position capture; the story is delivered in writing by the letter, and the re-take can be in-product.
2. **The chapter form is already enforced, in `system_tags`.** `misunderstanding` = anti-point, `understanding` = point, shared `st{n}` = the pairing (`p630_system_tags.sql`). It was assumed unenforced and therefore unusable as a denominator; it is neither.
3. **22 valence flips, but 16 came from one account** — the account that is `first_validator_id` on every point, i.e. the author (author identity per the 2026-04-24 [technical] entry). That is curation, not reading. **Reader flips: 6, from 4 readers.**
4. **Zero chapter completions.** No reader has ever flipped *both* halves of one `st`-chapter. The designed unit (anti-point A→D **and** point D→A) has not completed once.
5. **The real bottleneck is the second position.** 57 of 196 user-point threads ever received one; 14 of 33 users ever took a second position on anything. Nothing brings a reader back to re-take a position after the story.
6. **Flip rate already discriminates, weakly.** Reader-only: 6 flips / 36 re-take threads ≈ 17%, clustering on `st1` and `st5`; `st2` produced **0 flips across 8 re-takes**; 15 of 20 re-taken points produced nothing. This supports the founder's own objection-turned-insight — *not every story should flip, only good ones* — which is the metric working, not an argument against it.

**Decision:** **Postpone** the fitness function, the challenge/competition, the public API, and the P685 / P687 revival. A reputation economy denominated in a unit with n=6 and zero completions is not fundable by this evidence. **Build instead:** the post-story position re-take in the letter reading flow — the single gate every downstream idea sits behind.

**Alternatives rejected:** *Reduce verification cost first* (the session's opening premise) — rejected on the data: the cheap half of the loop is already cheap, already sessionless, and already running at volume, and it still yields almost no flips. *Run a hackathon / community challenge now* — rejected: a challenge is a scoring mechanism and there is no scoreable denominator yet. *Design a new measurement system* — rejected: `point_positions` + `point_position_history` have existed since `20260204_stories_points_calibration.sql`; the finding required a read, not a build.

**Consequences:** The next spec is the post-story re-take, and it carries a clean falsifier: if second-position rate rises and flips still do not appear, "good stories flip" is false and the fitness function dies for a real reason rather than for lack of data. If flips appear, P685 (Badge to GIVE — the non-monetary attractor for people who want to spread the practice) and P687 (clarithon / intra-cohort competition, already filed 2026-04-10) come off the shelf with a denominator. **Hand-off needed:** this bears weakly on **H-LegibilityVsCost** — the cost-binding arm is disfavoured by observation 1, but n=6 makes it suggestive, not evidence; route the `hypotheses.md` edit through `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`, do not write it here.

**Method caveats (stated so the numbers are not over-read):** `strongly_`/`somewhat_` variants were bucketed into agree/disagree and `unsure` excluded, so a "flip" is any agree↔disagree crossing in time order — a user correcting a misclick counts. Per-point n is 1–4; only `st2`'s 0-for-8 is individually informative. Read via the anon key, so any RLS-hidden rows are excluded.

**References:** `supabase/migrations/20260204_stories_points_calibration.sql` (`point_positions`, `point_position_history`) · `supabase/migrations/20260403120000_p630_system_tags.sql` (chapter encoding) · [definitions.md](definitions.md) §"Position Flip vs Interpretation Flip" · `features/p685_badge_propagation_vision.md` · `features/p687_post_flip_journaling.md` · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-LegibilityVsCost · this log 2026-04-24 [technical] (author identity via `first_validator_id`)

## 2026-08-03 [product]: The standard objection to paraphrasing was never a test of paraphrasing — and the harder problem it hid is a design constraint, not a concession

**Context:** Researched the claim that Gottman "proved active listening ineffective." Findings below were produced by a research pass, then **adversarially reviewed by five hostile reviewers before any of it was committed** — the review overturned four of my own claims, and this entry records the corrected version. Provenance matters here: the first pass declared the primary paper unreadable because `pdftotext` returned zero bytes on a scanned PDF, and wrote around it with honesty caveats. The paper was readable the whole time via page-image rendering. **A caveat is not a substitute for reading the source**, and the caveat would have shipped a 10x error with a disclaimer attached.

**What the primary actually says** (Gottman, Coan, Carrere & Swanson 1998, JMF 60:5-22, `10.2307/353438` — read this session):
- Observational, not a trial. 130 newlyweds, 6-year follow-up, a **15-minute lab conflict discussion** (topic selected with an experimenter), seven process models tested, active listening among them.
- Active-listening sequences "occurred infrequently for all couples, **totaling approximately 4 seconds out of 900**" (p.13) — i.e. **~0.44% of the discussion, in seconds of airtime**. The widely circulating "4.4%" is a decimal-shift error in secondary sources; do not repeat it.
- The paper does use the word: marital therapy "needs to **abandon the active listening model**" (p.20). That is its language, not the critics'.
- **The construct-validity admission that matters most** (p.17): the authors' own coders applied the validation code "exclusively for what Duncan and Fiske (1977) had called *listener backchannels*" — head nods and brief vocalizations. **They measured nodding, not paraphrase.**
- **The Munich/Hahlweg study is NOT cited in the 1998 paper.** Verified against the full reference list (pp.21-22): "Hahlweg" appears only as an *editor*. Munich is cited in Gottman's **2000 reply**. An earlier draft attached it to the 1998 paper — a citation error inside the very argument that criticizes citation practice.

**Decision 1 — record the correction, do not build a case on it.** The inference from a rare, non-predictive, backchannel-coded behavior to "abandon the intervention" does not hold, and was formally rebutted in the same journal (Stanley, Bradbury & Markman 2000, `10.1111/j.1741-3737.2000.00256.x`; Gottman replied, `...00265.x`; Hafen & Crane 2003 documents it unresolved). Gottman's prediction models separately failed to replicate in an independent sample (Kim, Capaldi & Crosby 2007, `10.1111/j.1741-3737.2006.00343.x` — note an earlier draft carried PMID 17375729, which is an unrelated paper; do not reuse it). **Rejected alternative:** citing the Hahlweg EPL follow-ups (dissolution 27.5% vs 52.6% at 11 years; 5% vs 26% at 25 years) as counter-evidence. Both have **non-randomized comparison groups of self-selected non-participants** — self-selection plausibly produces the whole effect — and the 25-year study found **no significant relationship-quality difference** on Locke-Wallace despite the divorce gap. Banking them would be the mirror image of the error being criticized. Also corrected: the 11-year EPL cohort was **married**, not premarital, and the comparison groups are described as non-participants, not as having "declined."

**Decision 2 — Gottman-Rapoport is prior art, scoped to its market.** Gottman's current conflict intervention gates persuasion on paraphrase: *"No one can engage in persuasion until both of you can state your partner's position to your partner's satisfaction"* — CP's mechanic including the speaker-as-arbiter move. **Cite it; never pitch paraphrase-before-proceeding as a discovery.** Recorded in hypotheses.md (H-TherapistRetention Shoulders) and lean-canvas.md. **Rejected alternative:** treating it as closest prior art *generally*. It is clinician-mediated, romantic-dyad, validation-mandatory — wrong for the team wedge. The work-domain equivalent is **closed-loop readback / the two-challenge rule** (crew resource management), which was already in hypotheses.md as a source of countable corpses and went unrecognized as prior art for months.

**Decision 3 — H-PopperianIncrement's control arm is specified by MECHANIC, not brand.** Must contain paraphrase-to-satisfaction + postponed persuasion, minus the number, minus refutation conditions, minus agreement-decoupling. **Rejected alternatives:** generic "active listening" (too weak — beating Rogerian reflection proves nothing) and Gottman-Rapoport-as-such (unadministrable to a seed-A product team; a control arm you cannot run on your own ICP is not a control arm). **Falsifier:** CP ties the mechanic-matched control ⟹ the claim narrows to "CP instruments what these protocols do by feel" — a measurement claim, not a Popperian one.

**Decision 4 — H-ComprehensionTrust's battery becomes a mediation design, WITHOUT inheriting the couples literature's pessimism.** Bradbury & Bodenmann 2020 (`10.1146/annurev-clinpsy-071519-020546`) report that changed behavior does not mediate treatment effects and that durable communication change "has not been documented"; Lavner et al. 2016 (`10.1111/jomf.12301`) find both causal arrows weak. **Rejected alternative (my own first draft):** "CP inherits this problem in full." It does not. That failure is observer-coded behavior to self-reported satisfaction over multi-year lags; CP's mediator is speaker-adjudicated paraphrase accuracy over weeks, and our own closeness-communication-bias evidence predicts the reverse arrow runs the *opposite* way. **Also rejected:** the flattering claim that a small operator can do what large trials cannot. At n=10 the pilot is underpowered for a mediation test; what it can do is validate a non-self-report accuracy measure and size a real study. `[FOUNDER DECISION: who codes accuracy]` — under the current Min architecture the mediator is a participant self-report collected by the vendor, which reinstates the "seller as judge" problem.

**Decision 5 — teach-back softening REVERTED.** An earlier edit today softened theory-of-change.md's explain-back row using couples evidence. Wrong: teach-back is comprehension-accuracy to readmissions, objective referent, weeks-long lag, and nothing in the couples corpus bears on it. The softening also hit one row while leaving its sibling ("45-60% fewer readmissions | Healthcare RCTs") untouched 18 lines above — the caveat-to-one-sibling failure. The mediation caveat now lives once, scoped, in §Evidence Gaps. **Being wrongly pessimistic is still being wrong.**

**Decision 6 — philosophy.md §2 scope conditions are recorded as UNTESTED predictions with falsifiers, not as boundaries.** The adversarial review judged the first version against p1026's own anti-degeneration criteria and it failed on every count: content-reducing, anomaly-matched 1:1, ex-post, no novel prediction. Two of the three bounds also, read literally, disqualified H-BuildRightThing's own pilot. **Rule adopted:** a scope condition that cannot state its falsifier gets deleted, not recorded.

**Decision 7 — asymmetric-skepticism correction.** The self-selection scalpel had been applied to exactly one citation (EPL — the one whose acceptance would embarrass a vendor) and withheld from every favorable one. Corrected for the sharpest case: **Kluger et al. 2023 measures _perceived_ listening, a self-report**, and our own hard core predicts perceived listening is inflated exactly where the real gap is largest — while lean-canvas.md separately attacks the field for resting on self-report. Kluger is now tagged: evidence the *construct* matters commercially, never evidence that verified comprehension produces outcomes. **Deferred:** the same audit for Hawkins 2008 (developer allegiance, self-report outcomes), teach-back readmissions, Google Aristotle, Gallup. Also noted and not fixed: "programs help modestly, reliably" understates the floor — the same review reports d≈0.09 in a 6,298-couple RCT and a trial where skills-trained newlyweds did not beat couples told to watch and discuss movies.

**Deliberately NOT recorded:** Simpson, Ickes & Blackstone (1995) / Simpson, Orina & Ickes (2003), on empathic accuracy reducing felt closeness when a partner's thoughts are relationship-threatening. Assessed from search summaries only; paradigm is romantic jealousy with unestablished transfer to work dyads; effect size and replication unchecked. Recording it would be the failure named in `.claude/rules/epistemic.md` gate 9. It is also **not new to us** — `content/articles/a24_when-common-knowledge-hurts.md` already holds this concession with a deciding-variables table, so if verified it is a *citation for a24*, not a new hypothesis. Founder's framing, recorded: **CP is not radical honesty.** It does not require always verifying understanding; it asks you to reveal the gap in *your own* understanding, and even that is declinable if you say why. The nearer relative is radical *psychological safety*, which is a different thing.

**Consequences:** hypotheses.md (H-TherapistRetention Shoulders, H-ComprehensionTrust, H-PopperianIncrement), lean-canvas.md (Current Alternatives, both boxes), philosophy.md §2, theory-of-change.md (Outcomes + Evidence Gaps; §What We Uniquely Do reverted), features/p1026 (pointer only; registry still needs a work-domain rival row), and `content/articles/a63_the-critic-who-built-a-paraphrase-gate.md` (framing inverted — leads with convergence, not with the critique).

## 2026-08-03 [product]: Intuition fails in a second direction — withheld content, held out of the canvas pending a 2nd instance

**Context:** Pitch-copy work (2026-07-31) surfaced a suppression mechanism the docs do not carry. The documented failure of comprehension-intuition is that it tells you you *have* been understood when you haven't. The founder supplied the inverse: intuition also tells you the other person **won't** understand you — so you don't say the thing at all. That guess is never tested either, and unlike the first failure it **leaves no trace to inspect**: gaps accumulate with nothing to audit later, and by the time anything surfaces the accumulation *is* the problem. Founder-originated — it is the mechanism in his own co-founder split, and it replaced (not refined) an earlier AI framing of that split as "answering questions the other never asked", which he rejected.

**Paired sharpening — the symmetry, which is a positioning constraint rather than phrasing.** Not *"your intuition is worse than theirs"* but: when backgrounds diverge, **neither** side's read is evidence any more. You can't rely on their sense that they understood you; they can't rely on yours. Both instruments fail at once, and they fail quietly — nothing signals it happened. This is what makes the conclusion non-insulting: nobody's judgment is being called poor, the instrument simply doesn't reach across the gap.

**Decision:** the mechanism is **distinct, and is NOT written into lean-canvas §Problem yet.** Recorded here with a promotion trigger instead.

**Distinctness ruling (this was the question put to the gate).** §Problem now carries four separate suppression triggers, and they fire at different points in the sequence: (1) **ask-suppression** — "I'll be judged slow/incompetent if I ask you to paraphrase" (self-sealing illusion, 2026-05-19); (2) **post-parking withholding** — once agree-to-disagree is the expected endpoint, people preempt because surfacing just gets parked (2026-07-11); (3) **defense-under-attack** — the target of a live complaint attacks back rather than empathizes (philosophy.md scope conditions, 2026-08-03); (4) **this one** — pre-emptive content-withholding on anticipated non-comprehension, upstream of all three, because nothing is ever surfaced at all. Not a re-description.

**Why it is held out of the canvas anyway.** n=1, retrospective, founder self-report, sourced from a copy-iteration conversation in a window where **zero tests ran**. `hypotheses.md` currently carries 42 `UNTESTED` blocks with none promoted or pruned this cycle (Gate 4 erosion WARN). Writing a fourth untested mechanism into §Problem in the same week the programme adopted a rigor layer against exactly that accumulation would be the move [P1026](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md) was specced to restrain. Routing, not refusal — recording is never blocked, and the founder confirmed this placement.

**Promotion trigger:** a **second independent instance** — someone other than the founder reporting that they withheld content because they predicted it wouldn't be understood. The outreach campaign is the plausible source. On instance 2, promote to lean-canvas §Problem alongside the other three triggers, cross-linked so they are told apart on the page.

**Falsifier:** subjects who report withholding content on anticipated-non-comprehension grounds show the same downstream gap accumulation as subjects reporting only the ask-suppression pattern ⟹ the two are not distinct in effect and this collapses into the self-sealing illusion.

**Evidence grade:** **UNTESTED, n=1**, retrospective and self-reported — stated by the founder as his reading in hindsight, explicitly not as a finding.

**References:** [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §Problem (self-sealing illusion · agree-to-disagree) · [philosophy.md](philosophy.md) scope conditions · [process-learnings.md](process-learnings.md) 2026-07-27 data point 1

## 2026-08-03 [product]: Elicitation wording and the permission line are two separate levers on Min honesty — keep the comprehension question

**Context:** A 2026-07-31 conversation proposed replacing the protocol's comprehension question (*"how much do you think you understand my intended meaning, 0–10?"*) with a clarity question (*"how clear do you think I was?"*). The reframe demonstrably unsticks people, and the reason is real: it flips who pays the face cost. A low number stops being a confession about the listener and becomes a report about the speaker. It was raised as a breakthrough. Separately, the same window produced a permission line — *"I'm fine with a low number, that's what tells me where to be clearer"* — which is already written into pitch copy and will ship with the outreach campaign whether or not it is recorded here.

**Decision:** Reject the wording swap; adopt the permission line as a distinct, separately-tested lever. Friction and accuracy are controlled by different levers, so there is no trade to make: keep the comprehension question as the measured variable and move the face-work into the permission line and the repair request (*"can you explain back what you think I meant, so I can see where I was unclear?"*).

Three grounds for rejecting the swap, all conjectural: (1) clarity has no ground truth — clarity is attributed to a message relative to one listener, comprehension is a state inside that listener, and the protocol's target is the second; (2) what a listener can actually rate is apparent well-formedness, i.e. the fluency heuristic, which is exactly what inflates the comprehension illusion — so the clarity wording is predicted *more* vulnerable to false highs, and the self-concealment conjecture says the top of the scale is the dangerous case; (3) *"you weren't clear"* is the standard polite carrier for *"I don't accept your point"*, so disagreement leaks into the number and contaminates the misunderstanding-vs-disagreement partition (bears on H-DisagreementDecomposition). A further bound: the disclosure premise may invert with a friend, mentor or client, where a low number becomes a criticism rather than a confession — so the reframe may be a local optimum for the population it was informally tried on.

Two constraints on the permission line: it is a promise, not a framing — the **first low number received is the actual calibration event**, and if the facilitator's face does anything, every subsequent number inflates and stays inflated; and it is said once at the open, since repeated it becomes ritual.

**Falsifier:** alternate the two wordings across the next batch of sessions, run the paraphrase round, and score the paraphrase independently of the rating. If the clarity wording is both easier to answer *and* worse at predicting paraphrase failure, a diagnostic was traded for a social lubricant. Second falsifier, for the permission line: rooms that get the permission line but no facilitator-first score produce as many honest low numbers as rooms that get both ⟹ the demonstration is decoration and the grant does the work (touches H-NormFlip and a51).

**Novel prediction (per the P1026 forward-only format, same-day):** the permission line produces an **asymmetric, floor-specific** effect — it lowers reported comprehension at the bottom of the scale without moving the top, so measured variance increases *downward* and the accuracy gain concentrates in low-comprehension events. The rival affect-first / psychological-safety programme predicts a uniform warmth effect (safety raises disclosure generally, across the scale). A second novel prediction discriminates the wordings: clarity ratings will track message-fluency measures rather than paraphrase accuracy, while comprehension ratings track paraphrase accuracy weakly but non-zero — a dissociation the "it's all just social comfort" account does not predict.

**Evidence grade:** UNTESTED, n=0, conversation-sourced (2026-07-31). Zero tests ran in the source window; all four source conversations were pitch/copy iteration. The predicted ranking of wordings is **conjecture, not finding** — "people answer it more easily" is adoption, not validation.

**Design note:** the falsifier above already satisfies requirement (a) of the same-day mediation correction on the H-ComprehensionTrust battery — comprehension accuracy measured as its own variable, independently of the outcome.

**References:** [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-AffectiveHonesty · `content/articles/a59_who-pays-the-face-cost.md` · `content/articles/a51_the-facilitator-should-fail-first.md` (2026-08-01 enrichment) · [features/p1026](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md)

## 2026-08-03 [process]: The project is an explicit Lakatosian research programme — rigor layer specced (P1026)

**Context:** A Lakatos framing session asked what the programme's hard core and protective belt are. hypotheses.md already encodes the negative heuristic verbatim ("mechanism transformation, not project abandonment"), but the structure was implicit: no written hard core (belt-hit vs core-hit classification happens ad-hoc at each refutation), no rival-programme tracking (no rational persistence/abandonment criterion), and a progress metric — "hypotheses falsified per unit time" — that measures activity, not progress: a degenerating programme (each pivot ad-hoc, accommodating only the anomaly that killed its predecessor) would look identical to a progressive one on the current scoreboard. Lakatos's criterion is corroborated *novel predictions*, which no format field captures.

**Decision:** Adopt the frame explicitly; P1026 specs the rigor layer. (1) `docs/research-programme.md`: numbered hard core with per-element evidential-status labels; the negative heuristic stated *separately* (a core element saying "refutations hit the belt" would immunize itself); rivals registry seeded with four (affect-first listening / coordination tooling / AI-mediated alignment / the affinity-trust null programme); progressivity ledger; generalized stopping rule ("no novel prediction corroborated within N tests or M months → the pivot cadence itself is the anomaly"). (2) hypotheses.md forward-only format: a **Novel prediction** field (falsifiers guard against dogmatism; novel predictions guard against degeneration — distinct disciplines, we had 100% coverage of the first and 0% of the second), a programme tag (business|scientific|both), and a **core-adjacent** flag — first applied to H-WTP-Pain (revelation reframe), whose ad-hoc budget is ONE auxiliary (dyad pre-screening); if revelation stays unreliable on pre-screened dyads, that is a core-hit review, not another belt patch. (3) `/slava:maintain:programme-health` skill: one verdict (progressive/stagnating/degenerating) + one recommendation, invoked by /monthly and after transform-triggers; adoption-time novelty audit instead of pre-named successors (successor framings historically arrive only *after* falsifying evidence lands — legitimate per Lakatos's discovery-vs-justification distinction; rigor applies at adoption, not conception).

The draft core survived one adversarial-critique round with major corrections: three of five drafted elements were belt-in-costume ("reliably" imported the open P0 question into the core; the three-criteria taxonomy carries a published falsifier and two revisions; "irreducibly interpersonal" is a dated design constraint under active contest), and the two never-questioned core commitments were missing precisely because they had never been questioned — **speaker authority** (the speaker is the sole arbiter of being-understood; the whole measurement stack presupposes it) and **the human relationship as the unit of intervention**. K1–K6 draft + open founder decisions (D1 wording; D2 truth-measurement layer: core vs explicit aspiration — silence would shrink the mission without recording it; D3 stopping-rule N/M) live in the P1026 appendix.

**Alternatives rejected:** JSON/schema for hypotheses (the bottleneck is discipline, not machine-readability; would break grep/diff/human ergonomics); hosting the core in philosophy.md (it holds the boldest *testable* conjectures — Asymmetric Conversion, ITT/RITT — and mixing protected with testable content is the confusion being removed); separate business/scientific hypothesis files (several hypotheses are both; a tag suffices).

**Consequences:** July 2026's six wedge re-cuts are currently *unclassifiable* (rapid heuristic exploration vs degenerating patching) — the discriminator is whether the newest adjustment (H-BuildRightThing's contingent-POC pay-gate, a genuine novel prediction) gets corroborated, which raises the pilot's evidential importance. H-PopperianIncrement is annotated as the rival-discriminator against the strongest rival (affect-first listening) and moves toward the front of the scientific test queue `[FOUNDER DECISION on priority]`. Citation discipline recorded: the literature-proven *components* (illusion of transparency, speaker overestimation of being understood, closeness-communication bias) are citable as proven; the recursive *composite* ("illusion of recursive understanding") is our own conjecture extending Pinker — never "proven by cognitive science." Article a62 filed (idea; depends on P1026 shipping so it can cite the doc, not a conversation). **UNTESTED** whether the rigor layer changes behavior rather than adding ceremony — falsifier: two /monthly cycles with an empty progressivity ledger and no health-check verdict acted on.

**References:** [features/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1026_research_programme_rigor_layer.md) · [content/articles/a62_our-startup-as-a-lakatosian-research-programme.md](../content/articles/a62_our-startup-as-a-lakatosian-research-programme.md) · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) · [philosophy.md](philosophy.md) · [theory-of-change.md](theory-of-change.md)

## 2026-08-03 [product]: the rating submit is present-and-disabled on every surface — `/meet` matched the letter instead of inventing a rule (P1024)

**Context:** P1024 shipped `/meet`'s understanding step with the submit button **absent** until a number was picked, on a reading of P955's "no dead controls" checklist item. UAT rejected it on consistency grounds: the letter reading flow renders the same `ComprehensionRatingCard` with its submit visible-and-disabled from the first frame, so two surfaces using one component disagreed about when the button exists.

**Decision:** the card's own built-in submit is used everywhere. It renders from the first frame and is disabled until a rating is chosen. `/meet` no longer supplies its own button; the `hideSubmit` prop introduced by P1024 was removed (`/meet` was its only consumer). Two properties beyond consistency: the button announces that a step remains after the number, and the docked bar stops changing height mid-step (measured 330px → 330px), so the certificate no longer reflows under the reader at the moment they tap.

**Alternatives rejected:** keep absence and change the letter to match — rejected, the letter is the shipped, higher-traffic surface and its behaviour was never reported as a defect. Also rejected: widening the shared component with a per-surface flag, which is what `hideSubmit` already was.

**Consequences:** `initialValue` was added to `ComprehensionRatingCard` — without it a rating restored from storage left the row unhighlighted while the host's state said a number was given, and the submit read disabled next to an apparently-empty row. It is uncontrolled after mount (remount to re-seed). A comment in `letter-prediction-walk.tsx` asserting the card "has no controlled/initial-value prop" was falsified by this and corrected in place.

**References:** [features/done/2026-06-10/p1024_meet_agreement_and_understanding.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1024_meet_agreement_and_understanding.md)

## 2026-08-03 [process]: "deterministically blocked by the p955-gate" is written unconditionally in the visual-QA checklist, but the gate only covers fixtured surfaces (P1024)

**Context:** while implementing P1024 I asserted — in a code comment, in the spec, and in a test comment — that the "submit must be absent, never disabled" rule was *enforced by the p955-gate*. It was not. The gate (`src/tests/p955-gate.test.ts`) renders only its own fixture, never `MeetingTermsPage`, and matches primaries by the class names `btn-primary | bg-primary | variant-primary | action-primary | data-variant="primary"`. `/meet` uses `bg-[#002B5C]` and the letter `bg-[#0044CC]`, so neither surface was ever in the matcher's reach. The letter has been rendering a disabled submit under this "enforced" rule the whole time.

**Decision:** record the correction and treat the per-surface coverage model as the operative fact. decisions.md 2026-06-27 [process] already states coverage grows one fixture at a time — the gap is that `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md` restates two checklist items with an unconditional "deterministically blocked by the p955-gate", which reads as global enforcement at the point of use.

**Alternatives rejected:** adding a `/meet` fixture as part of P1024 — out of scope for a change-request and it would have masked the general problem, which is the phrasing, not this one surface.

**Consequences:** the visual-qa.md phrasing needs qualifying ("blocked by the p955-gate **on fixtured surfaces**"). That is a `.claude/rules/` edit and therefore goes through `/slava:maintain:claude-md` — **not applied here**, flagged for the founder. General form: a checklist item that names its own enforcement mechanism should name the mechanism's scope, or it converts a written norm into a believed-mechanical one. Epistemic gate 7 ("exercise a gate's failure path before trusting it") already covers gates you author; this is the consumer-side case — a gate you *cite*.

## 2026-07-31 [technical]: a cross-origin embed's `load` event is not "the visitor can see it" — and nothing above `#root` can cover the pre-mount window (P1017)

**Context:** `/intro` (the primary CTA's destination, a bare Google Calendar embed) rendered blank while loading. The first fix put a loader overlay on the iframe, keyed to `onLoad`. Every test passed. Measured afterwards against the **real** embed on a cold load, that fix covered roughly half the blank time and introduced a second gap of its own. Four distinct windows exist, not one: HTML→React ~85ms, React→lazy chunk ~302ms, chunk→`onLoad` ~5.5s, and **`onLoad`→Google's picker actually painting ~1.6s**. The last one is the trap: `onLoad` fires when the iframe *document* loads, but a client-rendered embed paints well after that, so unmounting the loader at `onLoad` hands the visitor a fresh blank screen at the highest-intent moment.

**Decision:** Three parts. (1) **`onLoad` means "document arrived", never "content is visible"** — for any client-rendered cross-origin embed, treat it as the start of a further wait, not the end. Cross-origin gives no paint signal, so the overlay *fades* rather than unmounting, releasing `pointer-events` immediately so a calendar that IS ready is never trapped behind a spinner. (2) **The pre-React window cannot be covered by any app-level loader** — `#root` is empty until React's first render, so the loader must be inline in `index.html` (no extra request; neither the CSS nor the JS bundle has arrived). It hides itself with pure CSS on `#root:not(:empty)` — no JS timer, nothing for `main.tsx` to remember. Its fade is load-bearing, not decorative: `ClarityPageLoader` deliberately stays invisible for its first 300ms (anti-flash), which almost exactly matched the 302ms chunk window, so an instant hide handed off into a fresh gap. FCP 88–104ms → 20–24ms. (3) **A timing constant tuned on one connection is a latent bug.** A fixed 2200ms post-load fade covered the gap on a fast link and would have missed by ~7s on slow 3G, because a slow client makes Google's render slower too. Derive it instead: `clamp(embedFetchDuration × 0.45, 2200ms, 12000ms)` — how long the embed's own fetch took is an already-measured proxy for this visitor's connection, and the render scales with the same conditions.

**Alternatives rejected:** A fixed post-load delay (calibrated to one connection — the defect above). Clearing the loader at `onLoad` (the measured second blank window). Rendering the shell inside `#root` and letting React replace it (couples the fix to React's container-clearing behaviour instead of a CSS rule that cannot race). Bundle-size work to "make it faster" — measured, our own code is **384ms of a ~7.6s wait (5%)**; the embed is 95%, so even deleting the entire 246KB-gzip entry chunk caps out at ~380ms. A `preconnect` to Google showed **no measurable effect** (inside run-to-run noise — the host had warm DNS/TLS and the wait is Google's server work, not handshake); kept as two cheap hints with the null result written into the comment rather than a claim that wasn't demonstrated.

**Consequences:** Any future embed of a client-rendered third party inherits all four windows. The still-open failure mode: a *blocked* embed (ad blocker, corporate CSP) never fires `onLoad` at all, so none of this engages and the spinner runs indefinitely — tracked as P1023, which needs a founder decision on fallback copy.

**Falsifier:** A cold load at any throttling profile shows a blank content area at any sampled moment between navigation and the calendar painting → the coverage model is wrong, not merely mistuned.

**References:** [index.html](../index.html), [intro-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/intro-page.tsx), P1023 (blocked-embed fallback), 2026-04-11 [technical] (ClarityPageLoader anti-flash)

## 2026-07-31 [process]: a stubbed route cannot verify a loading-state fix — the stub makes the bug zero by construction (P1017)

**Context:** P1017's canary intercepts `calendar.google.com` and holds the response open, which is a legitimate way to make an inherently racy load window deterministic — the real window is a few hundred ms of network luck. 8/8 passed, a code review ran, a blind visual-QA subagent ran. All of it missed a ~1.6s blank window that a single cold load against the real embed exposed immediately. **Cause: `route.fulfill` returns a document that is complete the instant it loads**, so the gap between `onLoad` and the third party's client-side paint is exactly zero in the test and ~1.6s in reality. The test could not fail. Separately, "verified" had been reported for work where every assertion and screenshot used a stub — the mechanism was proven, the experience was not.

**Decision:** Two rules. (1) **A fix to a loading/perceived-performance state requires at least one measurement against the real third party before it is called verified.** Stubs verify the mechanism (does the overlay mount, does it cover the box, does it clear); they cannot verify the timing they flatten. State explicitly which of the two a run covered — "tests pass" is evidence for the mechanism only. (2) **Blank-detection needs an instrument, not eyeballing.** Sampling the PNG byte size of a clipped content region is a dependency-free, self-calibrating proxy: a flat blank area compresses to ~1440B, the loader to ~3000B, real content to 30–35KB. It turns "is the screen empty" into a countable assertion — the slow-3G run reported **99 samples, 0 blank frames, min 2980B**, which is falsifiable in a way a screenshot review is not.

**Alternatives rejected:** Pixel-diffing via an image library (needs a new dependency for a question byte size already answers). Trusting the visual-QA subagent's screenshots (it reviewed stub-state captures and could only assess what the stub produced — it correctly found real layout issues and still could not see this one). Adding a real-network assertion to the canary itself (makes CI depend on Google's uptime and latency; the measurement belongs in verification, not the gate).

**Consequences:** The `/verify` step for anything touching load/perceived performance should include one throttled real-dependency run. The measurement scripts for this live in the session scratchpad, not the repo — if this recurs a third time, that is the signal to make the byte-size sampler a checked-in tool rather than re-authoring it.

**Falsifier:** A stub-only canary catches a real-dependency timing regression that no real-network run was needed to find → the stub was not flattening the window after all.

**References:** [e2e/p1017-reproduce.spec.ts](../e2e/p1017-reproduce.spec.ts), 2026-07-15 [process] (a capture that skips the reveals photographs a blank page), `.claude/rules/epistemic.md` gate 7

## 2026-07-30 [technical]: A page puts content in the shared nav via an out-of-flow slot + portal — and a fallback that renders identical markup leaves the primary path untested (P1016)

**Context:** `/terms` renders the nav `compact`, which strips every nav link, the CTA and the hamburger. The result was a 64px bar holding one logo, with the page's own level-track sitting on a second 44px row directly beneath it — two rows of chrome above a document, for content that fits in one. The founder's annotated screenshot pointed at exactly that empty band.

**Decision:** `SimpleNavigation` renders a permanent, **absolutely-positioned** slot (`id="nav-center-slot"`, exported as `NAV_CENTER_SLOT_ID`); a page that wants content in the nav row `createPortal`s into it. Absolute positioning is the load-bearing choice, not a styling preference: the slot takes no part in the nav row's flex layout, so on the ~30 routes that portal nothing its presence **cannot** shift the logo or the right-hand group. A `flex-1` slot would have been simpler to write and would have put every other route's nav geometry at risk.

**Verified, not assumed.** The claim "this affects no other page" is exactly the kind that reads as obviously true and ships a regression. Before/after measurement on `/`, `/terms-of-service` and `/founder` at 1280px: nav height 80, logo width 146 at left 32, right-group width and left position — identical to the pixel in every case. Narrowest-width clearance measured too: at 320px the logo ends at x=40 and the first track label starts at x=72.

**The subtler finding — the fallback masked the feature.** The page keeps an in-body sticky track for the case where the nav isn't mounted (chrome-free embed, renamed slot). That fallback renders **the same markup with the same test-ids**, so every existing assertion — three radios, correct labels, terms swap on select, keyboard nav, accept/lock — passed identically whether the portal worked or silently degraded. The entire point of the change was untested by a green suite. Fixed by anchoring one assertion to `[data-nav="main"]` plus a certificate-top-offset check, and the failure path was exercised: with the slot id deliberately broken the test exits 1.

**Generalises:** any graceful fallback whose output is indistinguishable from the primary path converts that path into dead-but-green code. The test must assert the property the fallback *cannot* satisfy — here, DOM location — not the behaviour both share. This is epistemic gate 7 applied to a fallback rather than to a gate.

**Consequences:** `NAV_CENTER_SLOT_ID` is now shared API — renaming it silently degrades `/terms` to the second-row layout, and the e2e test is what makes that loud. Note the `logoOnly` early-return branch of `SimpleNavigation` has **no** slot; unreachable for `/terms` today (it routes `compact`), and the in-body fallback covers it, but it is the one remaining gap if that routing ever changes.

**References:** `src/app/components/layout/simple-navigation.tsx`, `src/app/pages/meeting-terms-page.tsx`, `e2e/p1016-meeting-terms.spec.ts`, [.claude/rules/epistemic.md](../.claude/rules/epistemic.md)
