## 2026-07-29 [process]: Record the non-recording — six proposed doc edits, zero applied, and why that was correct

**Context:** A `/claude-conversations-to-cp` run over three 2026-07-28 conversations. Content was filed and committed (a56, a57, a58 new; a39, a55 enriched — commit `50765dbe`). **Six strategy-doc edits were proposed and none were applied.** The founder's response to the proposal surface was: *"its a bit too much… i dont know how to answer… creates huge amount of confusion and cognitive dissonance."* The session then drifted past the sync into problem-statement work, which was the more valuable half of the evening and added **zero new evidence**.

**Decision:** Write nothing to the strategy docs, deliberately, and record the non-recording instead. Every finding below is **reasoned, not observed**. Writing them into `hypotheses.md` / `lean-canvas.md` would convert argument into apparent evidence — the failure named in the 2026-07-27 `[process]` entry ("An objection is a conjecture, not a refutation"), one level up: there it was the *buyer* that moved on arguments, here it would be the *docs*. **This is not withholding on "wait until validated" grounds** (epistemic gate 8): the findings are recorded here, now, labelled UNTESTED, with the transcript pointer that makes them recoverable in full.

**Distinct from last week.** On 2026-07-27 scope was cut because the proposals were *wrong*. This week the proposals may well be right; the **volume** was wrong. Different failure, same outcome — and the second one is the skill's, not the founder's. **Process fix for the next run:** lead with judgment (what matters, what is accepted or rejected and why), never with a diff. A decision surface is not a deliverable when the reader cannot hold it.

**The unrecorded findings — all UNTESTED, all reasoned, none observed:**
1. **The problem is triage, not misunderstanding.** Verification is expensive; people allocate it by *felt uncertainty*; felt uncertainty barely tracks where gaps actually are (r=.178, already in lean-canvas). Not solution-shaped — it would hold if ClarityPledge did not exist. **Converges independently with the same-date `[product]` entry "Detection may be the product; verified understanding is the remedy"**, which reached it from a founder interview rather than from reasoning. Two routes, one conclusion — the closest thing to corroboration this week produced.
2. **Two-gate qualification.** Arbiter-failure (fuzzy intent / delayed feedback / concentrated stakes) **AND** a live counterpart with skin in it. Consequence: the solo free audit in [goals.md](goals.md) can *reveal* but cannot *deliver* — it is a diagnostic teaser, not the product.
3. **Detection is unilateral; remedy is bilateral.** Explains the 2026-07-16 stranger encounter, the reactive-deployment hazard, and the lean-canvas "motivated Person B" precondition as one fact. **Corollary:** if the remedy needs two, the sale needs two in the room — which disqualifies champion-buys-for-others and any buyer standing outside the dyad.
4. **"If they agree they don't want to verify" is the law of the category, not a sales obstacle.** Demand for verification is *inversely* correlated with need for it: agreement is the strongest felt-certainty signal, and felt certainty barely tracks comprehension.
5. **Diverging opinions is an anti-signal** — visible divergence does not need the instrument. **Repeating is a retrospective trace**: valuable as the countable artifact in a sale, useless as a triage signal, because it reports a gap that already cost.
6. **A root cause nobody attributes to is, commercially, a theory.** Selling the *cure* requires installing a causal model first, which is education and the most expensive sale there is. Selling the **diagnostic** does not — you are paid to find out whether the cause is there.

**Also recorded — a founder constraint is not a market conjecture.** *"Reaching out in order to be paid is work I won't do"* legitimately bounds acceptable GTM and needs no test. What needed a test was the conjecture that rode in alongside it — that L&D / psychological-safety buyers hold an attribution-free budget, self-flagged in-conversation as one-hour-old reasoning. **Filing the two together is what let the buyer relocate a fifth time in two weeks.** Separate them at intake.

**Alternatives rejected:** applying the six edits unreviewed (converts reasoning into doc-grade evidence); applying the "safe" two and deferring four (the split would be arbitrary — none was tested); deferring the record entirely to a rested day (gate 8 — the findings would survive only in a transcript nobody re-reads).

**Consequences:** No strategy-doc edits pending from this session. The four uncaptured proposals (badge-as-empirical-expectation-generator testable with cardstock · transfer falsifier + the spontaneous-vs-assisted scope bound · the process data point · the sampling-bias catch) live in `.private/claude-conversations-to-cp-last-run.txt` and can be re-proposed one at a time when something is tested. **No spec, no follow-up task** — deliberately.

**Falsifier:** if within ~4 weeks any of findings 1–3 is acted on and produces a result, it earned a doc entry and this deferral cost time. If none is acted on, not recording them was correct and cheap.

**References:** session transcript `~/.claude/projects/<project-encoded-path>/1b91fc0d-50d2-45fd-a9d8-433191e5248b.jsonl` · `.private/claude-conversations-to-cp-last-run.txt` (full run record) · [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-27 `[process]` · the same-date `[product]` entries from the parallel founder-interview session · `content/articles/a56`, `a57`, `a58`

## 2026-07-29 [product]: The unit under test is the authored problem definition, not the pain — and it has never been accepted

**Context:** A founder interview was analyzed against the run card. The first formulation of the result was "no evidence the pain is solve-worthy," which the founder corrected: that phrasing presupposes the pain is already known and only needs sizing. You never observe pain; you observe whether **a formulation you authored gets accepted.** Assuming you already know the pain is the same illusion the product exists to catch — the instrument applied reflexively.

**Decision:** Restate the standing problem as **"no problem definition I authored has been accepted as solve-worthy."** Acceptance is **behavioral, not verbal**: the counterpart supplies an **unprompted instance from their own past, with a cost attached.** Verbal agreement is worth zero (this interviewee agreed to a great deal and bought nothing). Corollary recorded from the review: across ~6 founder interviews the wedge was re-cut 4 times (07-01 solo builder → 07-14 key hire → 07-20 team-internal), so **no single definition has been tested more than ~twice** — nothing converged because nothing was repeated. And because delivery failed in most of those interviews, **no definition has been falsified; they were untested.** "Nothing works" and "nothing was tested" look identical from the outside and have opposite implications.

**Also decided — the two-pains split.** "Building the wrong thing" conflates two pains with opposite perception profiles. *Customer-wrongness* ("nobody wanted it") is retrospective, invisible in-flight, and needs a reveal — the interviewee stated it flatly and volunteered that it cannot be sold. *Agreement-wrongness* ("that's not what we discussed, and I deleted it") is felt within days, was volunteered unprompted 28 minutes earlier by the same person, and has a unit: **deleted/reworked developer-days.** H-BuildRightThing is *worded* for the second and *named* after the first, and the name is what reaches the buyer.

**Alternatives rejected:** "no pain found" (presupposes we know the pain); "the instrument is untested on skeptics" (presupposes a problem exists and asks only whether the cure lands); treating the interviewee's sustained GTM critique as evidence (he is not the buyer for the market he was theorizing about, and it arrived after both parties had agreed he was not a customer); a `.private/` problem-definitions log written this session (deleted — unapproved freeform prose, see the [process] entry below).

**Consequences:** Doc edits are **needed but not made here** — hand off to `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` for `hypotheses.md` (H-BuildRightThing naming caution) and any `lean-canvas.md` §UVP consequence. **Live consequence to decide:** `origin/main` carries a landing hero *"Your team agreed. And built the wrong feature."* — first clause is the accepted half, second clause is the rejected half. `[FOUNDER DECISION]`. Rework rate is a candidate outcome metric and the pay-gate for a contingent POC; it is the only quantity in the corpus that is measurable, already-resented, and downstream of misalignment.

**Falsifier:** offer the agreement-wrongness formulation, in the counterpart's own words, to 3 in-ICP founders with the instrument actually run. If none supplies an unprompted instance, the definition is wrong rather than the delivery. Separately: ask 10 seed–A technical founders cold and unframed — *"in the last 30 days, how many developer-days went into something you then deleted or reworked because it wasn't what was agreed?"* ≥6 producing a number unprompted = the pain is felt; ≥6 needing the concept explained = both halves need a reveal and the wedge's premise fails.

**References:** the 2026-07-29 founder dossier + dated analysis in `.private/docs/business/founders/` · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-BuildRightThing · H-WTP-Pain 2026-06-18 (don't qualify on self-reported need)

## 2026-07-29 [product]: Detection may be the product; verified understanding is the remedy

**Context:** The same interview produced a structural observation. The interviewee was the strongest ICP-5-criterion-5 exemplar in the series — someone who had already self-diagnosed the problem and paid for help — and still perceived no live gap. If anyone inside a dyad were going to perceive one and reach for help, it is that profile. **They didn't, because perception is the broken part** — so selecting for *will* does not rescue it. Separately: they denied having any high-stakes decisions, then named a real one **seconds later** when asked directly *"what would be high-stakes for you?"* — after nine minutes at the start of the call had failed to install the term "high-stakes matters" at all.

**Decision:** Record the reframe as an open direction: **the asymmetric capability is detecting the high-stakes matters the parties are blind to; verified understanding is the remedy applied afterwards.** We have been selling the remedy, and nobody perceives a need for a cure to a problem they cannot see — which is the interviewee's own *"nobody raises their hand"* objection stated from the inside. **This also explains a real gap: [definitions.md](definitions.md) states "stakes is the gate" (§Verification Threshold) and contains no definition of high-stakes** — three incidental mentions, no entry. The architecture's gate was never defined because the product was framed as the remedy.

**Alternatives rejected:** auditing the *business model* and disagreeing with it (reopens the 2026-07-07 authority problem — but note the distinction that rescues a narrow version: authority is needed to be *right*, not to *disagree*, and the protocol verifies comprehension **before** the dispute, so a disagreement where we might be wrong is better material than one where we are right); a multi-agent alignment architecture with a governance layer, sketched this session and **not pursued** — it does not touch the untested claim, and reaching for it is the documented overintellectualization pattern (expanding scope when facing uncertainty).

**Consequences:** If detection is the product, `definitions.md` needs a **high-stakes** entry — that is a `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` job, not this one. Sequential consent (*"this looks high-stakes to me because X"* → accept/decline → *"here's what I'd do"* → accept/decline) becomes the honest delivery shape, because with no definition of stakes on our side the classification is genuinely joint work rather than us grading them. **Two consents, not one:** confirming a decision is expensive says nothing about whether we should be in the room. Do not prefill our position on their stakes.

**Falsifier:** run the extraction on a foreign corpus and check whether it surfaces high-stakes items the subject missed live. A manual pass on this transcript found two (an undecided sprint with a 48h deadline; the release bet). If an automated pass finds neither, or only surfaces items the subject already tracks, the detection claim fails and the reframe dies.

**References:** [definitions.md](definitions.md) §Verification Threshold ("stakes is the gate") · `.private/docs/business/customer-dev-lessons.md` 2026-07-07 (audit the capacity, not the business model) · the 2026-07-29 dated analysis in `.private/docs/business/founders/`

## 2026-07-29 [process]: `/align` already exists — the blocker is an unfinished run, not a missing design

**Context:** The session spent significant effort designing an agent that would extract decisions, assumptions and problem statements from a meeting transcript and assign each a stake. That is `/align` v1.7.0, built 2026-07-13 (see this log's entry for that date): Stage-1 detection emits classified cards with `type` (decision/assumption/hypothesis/problem-statement/reasoning) · `stake` · `content` · `source` · verbatim `evidence`, stakes are a magnitude in time **and** money, and the loop halts at a **1→2 gate where the user confirms or corrects the quantified stake.** The sequential-consent mechanism reasoned out from scratch this session **is that gate.** The design was re-derived rather than looked up.

**Decision:** Treat the blocker as **execution, not design.** `/align` has been run on exactly one subject (the founder himself, coaching-pivot decision, ~3–6 months ≈ €18–36k) and that run is **still stuck mid-loop at enrichment→open-questions.** Steps 4–5 of the loop have never been closed once, by anyone. **Close that run before offering the loop to anyone else** — otherwise we are selling a loop we have never finished. Then run the extraction on a foreign corpus as a read-only internal test.

**Also decided — letter direction: the author must have the context.** A letter cannot be authored on someone's behalf about their own business from a corpus that does not contain it. The interview corpus is ~8,700 words about his business and ~8,600 words of him advising us, so enrichment ("harvest already-answered material from the corpus") has almost nothing to work with on his side. Rejected in the same pass: a letter *from* us *to* him about our GTM — high stakes for us, none for him, therefore unjustified. **A confirmed stake card is what a letter is about, and it is his letter, to his cofounder** — the dyad we are not a member of.

**Consequences:** Next-session task is a read-only `/align` run on the full transcript, **not hand-cut** — a real meeting would not be, so cutting it tests an easier problem than the real one. The real test is whether the extraction separates his high-stakes matters from his commentary on our GTM. **Unbuilt and named:** the two-party leg (letter → cofounder → two-sided min → divergence). `/align` was designed for one person on their own corpus. The stake-correction step currently has no home except a live conversation with us present — a known n=1 constraint, not solved.

**Falsifier:** if the extraction labels our positioning problems as his high-stakes items, the detector cannot distinguish subjects and needs the corpus scoped before it is usable.

**References:** decisions.md 2026-07-13 [process] (`/align` brought to minimum-executable bar) · `features/p1003_three_minute_alignment_audit_funnel.md`

## 2026-07-29 [process]: A post-solution founder is a disqualifier that reads as a strong fit

**Context:** The interviewee scored high on ICP-5 — including a rare, hard pass on criterion 5 — and was **not in a buying state**, having already found, paid for and installed a working substitute a short time earlier, on their own initiative, with a reported step-change in outcome. Neither too-early nor too-late but **freshly cured** — and the recently-cured are the most articulate people alive about the pain, having just paid someone to name it. A full interview was spent discovering what two pre-screen questions would have surfaced.

**Decision:** Add **post-solution insulation** as a pre-screen disqualifier (gate G3, trigger + slack): *"When did you last change how you and your cofounder make decisions together — and did you pay anyone for it?"* A change inside ~6 months = deprioritize, **regardless of how well they articulate the pain. Articulacy about the pain and willingness to pay are anti-correlated in the recently-cured.** Also name the competitor explicitly: **a human coach with both founders in a room**, self-initiated from inside the dyad, delivering in weeks. That competitor was absent from the strategy docs and it won this account before we arrived. Note the targeting consequence: **nothing in the account connected the purchase to a hire — accumulated strain connected to it**, so scraping for hiring signals may target the wrong event.

**Also recorded — the interview's own process failures, since all three prior anti-patterns recurred:** the falsifier was **never run** (the 0–10 mechanic was described six times and executed on the subject zero times); the interview **inverted at 01:20:47** and the flip was purchased with a verdict of health (*"you're fine"* → *"if you want my opinion…"* eighteen seconds later), after which ~70 of 156 minutes were the interviewee advising on our GTM; a live gap the subject volunteered unprompted was converted into a hypothetical and closed inside 20 seconds; and **zero commitments of any kind were asked.** Root cause identified: **there was nothing to hand him except the explanation** — no dated room, no artifact — so every pull had nowhere to go. Mitigating correction: leading a witness *toward* "you don't need this" is the safe direction (it risks a false negative, not a false positive), so the leading-question critique is weaker than first scored.

**Alternatives rejected:** pursuing him as a customer (no pain, has a substitute, teaches us nothing); sending him an unsolicited extraction of his own business (a confidently mislabelled list is the authority problem at its worst); a costless homework assignment paired with a gift — the physical habit-token handed over at 02:30:45 inverted reciprocity and contaminated every later signal, and it asked him to **self-detect high-stakes moments, which is the exact capability he had already said he lacks.**

**Consequences:** Pre-screen edit is a `discovery-questions.md` change (not a gated strategy doc) — apply separately. Next interviewee should be filtered on **a live undecided decision with a date, and no coach** — never on "do you have a pain," which reliably returns no. **Open governance item:** recording consent was never established on tape. Confirm it before any further use of that material, and offer the subject the transcript — the one costless reciprocity still available. Per-subject detail is held in `.private/docs/business/founders/` and must not be restated in this public log.

**References:** the 2026-07-29 founder dossier in `.private/docs/business/founders/` · `.private/docs/business/discovery-questions.md` (G3) · `.private/docs/business/customer-dev-lessons.md` (the three prior logged interview anti-patterns) · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-FounderWince state layer

## 2026-07-29 [technical]: A service that returns `[]` on failure is a defect wherever the caller renders an empty state (P1011)

**Context:** Sentry `JAVASCRIPT-REACT-2F`. A laptop wakes from sleep; the first Supabase fetch fails because the network isn't up yet, so the auth token never refreshes; ~3s later the inbox poll goes out with the stale token and PostgREST rejects it (`PGRST303`). `getInboxItems` caught that error, logged it, and `return []`. The caller could not distinguish that from a genuinely empty inbox, so a user who *had* letters was shown **"No letters or responses yet."** The bug was invisible for as long as it existed because the swallow made it look like correct behaviour — the empty state rendered without error.

**Decision:** Failure and emptiness must be distinguishable **at the service boundary**. `getInboxItems` now throws via `throwDbError`; the caller owns the distinction and renders a third state — last-known-good list plus a muted "can't reach the server, retrying" notice — reserving the error state for a failure with nothing already on screen. Suppression behaviour is unchanged: `throwDbError` routes through `logDbError` first, so blips and `PGRST303` still never reach Sentry.

The P710 contract test that asserted *"returns empty when RPC errors (does not throw)"* was **deliberately inverted**, with the reason recorded at the assertion. That test encoded the defect as a guarantee.

**Corollary (found in code review of this very fix, and the more valuable half of this entry):** adding a second `await` inside an existing `try` silently gives the new call the old block's failure semantics. The first cut set the "list loaded" flag at the *end* of the try, after a secondary explain-back-counts fetch. A failure in that secondary call therefore ran the shared `catch` with the flag still false and tore down an already-rendered list into the full-page error screen — **this same bug class, reintroduced one layer deeper, inside the fix for it.** Rule: when a fix adds a call inside an existing `try`, either set success flags at the point success is actually observable, or give the new call its own `try`. Mutation-proven: restoring the old ordering fails exactly one test.

**Alternatives rejected:** Keeping `return []` and having the caller infer failure from a separate error flag — two sources of truth for one condition, and the empty state still wins the race on first paint. Leaving the P710 test untouched and adding a parallel one — the two would assert contradictory contracts.

**Consequences:** Applies to any service function whose caller renders an empty state; ~150 `logDbError` call sites use the `return []`/`return 0` shape, so this is a pattern to apply on contact, not a sweep. Not verified in a live browser — `/letters` is auth-gated and the stale state needs an induced mid-session network failure; unit-tested only.

**References:** [src/app/data/letters-service.ts](../src/app/data/letters-service.ts) (`getInboxItems`), [src/app/components/letters/inbox-tab.tsx](../src/app/components/letters/inbox-tab.tsx), [features/done/2026-06-10/p1011_sentry_noise_and_stale_jwt_empty_inbox.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1011_sentry_noise_and_stale_jwt_empty_inbox.md)

## 2026-07-29 [technical]: Coded transients cannot route through `isNetworkBlip`, and `throwDbError`'s type-based suppression does not cover them (P1011)

**Context:** `PGRST303` ("JWT expired") is a transient wake-from-sleep artifact — the next 15s poll succeeds unaided — so it belongs suppressed. The obvious home looked like `isNetworkBlip`. It isn't: `network-blip.ts:64` returns false for **any** error carrying a `code`, and `PGRST303` legitimately carries one. PostgREST really did reject the token; the blip is *upstream* of it.

**Decision:** Suppress `PGRST303` at the `logDbError` choke point, beside the P913 `42501` branch — rung 2 of the noise ladder (2026-07-15), which line 3147(d) already assigns this class to. Extension-thrown errors (`chrome-extension://`, `ext:`, `<name:bootstrap>` frames) go to rung 3, a frame-based `beforeSend`, since the message is a bare TypeError string a real bug could produce verbatim. Both drops leave a `db-error-suppressed` / `sentry-event-suppressed` breadcrumb.

**Known gap, recorded because it is currently masked by luck:** `throwDbError`'s docstring promises Sentry drops "by TYPE" via `NetworkBlipError`. That promise **does not extend to coded transients** — `isNetworkBlip` is false for them, so the throw is a plain `Error` that `dropNetworkBlipRethrow` will not filter. Nothing leaks today only because the single `PGRST303` caller catches it. Before adding a `throwDbError` call site that lets the rejection escape to the global handler, give the coded-transient class its own error type.

**Alternatives rejected:** Widening `isNetworkBlip` to admit coded errors — it would swallow genuine coded DB failures, which is the whole reason for the `code` short-circuit. A `beforeSend` *message* filter — rejected in P883, re-rejected in P990, for the reason both named: a real error sharing the message shape dies with it. Repairing the refresh path rather than suppressing — an earlier attempt at this was **dead code**: `auth-js` already refreshes with a 90s margin and `_getAccessToken()` re-checks at request time; it was reverted after review disproved the premise.

**Consequences:** The extension filter keys on the **last frame of the last exception value** — last frame because `stripSentryFramesAndReverse` puts the throw site last (an extension monkey-patching `fetch` sits mid-stack on real app errors); last value because `exception.values` holds one entry per `Error.cause` link, and keying on any value would discard an app error wrapping an extension cause. Both narrowings mutation-proven. Fails toward reporting on stacks deeper than `STACKTRACE_FRAME_LIMIT` — accepted, uninstrumented.

**References:** [src/lib/sentry-filters.ts](../src/lib/sentry-filters.ts), [src/app/data/db-error-logger.ts](../src/app/data/db-error-logger.ts), [src/lib/network-blip.ts](../src/lib/network-blip.ts), 2026-07-15 [technical] (noise ladder), 2026-03-07 [technical] (P483+P488 — `#error=access_denied` is the expired-magic-link redirect)

## 2026-07-27 [product]: Reject the interdepartmental/COO segment on the merits + pre-commit the falsifier before strategy conversations. **Deductive — no new field data.**

**Context:** 2026-07-25→27 conversation batch via `/claude-conversations-to-cp` (5 files, 4 CP-relevant). The 2026-07-26 session "Internal feedback loops and cross-departmental communication" walked a buyer escalation — cofounder pair → COO/interdepartmental handoff protocol → acquirer in due diligence → citizens in an online assembly — and returned to founders. The founder then challenged the whole synthesis, and the challenge held: nothing was tested this week, so most of the proposed doc changes were logging dressed as strategy. **This entry records only what survived that challenge.** Scope was cut from 14 proposed edits to 2 doc changes plus cleanup.

**Decision:**
1. **The interdepartmental / Product↔Sales segment (H-SalesProductAlignment) is rejected on the merits, not merely parked.** Its filed rationale — *"sidesteps 'buyer = subject' friction of cofounder pairs"* — is false. It **reproduces** that friction: the COO buys, the two departments are the ones measured, so the people in the room did not choose to be there (a cofounder pair at least has buyer and subject coinciding by consent). And Sales is compensated on bookings while Product is compensated on roadmap/retention — an **interest conflict**, exactly the case where the protocol's own stated value shifts *"from preventing misalignment to honoring the disagreement"* ([lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §Unique Value Proposition — "Where the protocol's value shifts"). Verification surfaces the conflict cleanly and cannot resolve it.
2. **Its auto-firing revisit trigger is deleted.** The row read *"Track 1 week-2 gate returns zero signal → this becomes next pitch test."* Track 1 has returned zero signal, so as written the doc instructed future-Slava to adopt a segment that fails the reasoning in (1). Replaced with a non-firing condition: **never a cold entry** — revisit only if an existing founder-segment client grows into the interdepartmental case and refers inward.
3. **Pre-commit the falsifier before any conversation that could relocate the buyer, wedge, or positioning** — with an AI, an advisor, or a peer. One line: *"I move off this only if [N attempts] produce [result]."* Recorded as an open item with a 4-week tracking window in [process-learnings.md](process-learnings.md); thresholds are `[FOUNDER DECISION]` with proposed defaults drawn from the [goals.md](goals.md) funnel walk-back.

**Falsifier (for 1):** a cross-department engagement produces a paid, durable outcome despite unfused compensation → reason (1b) is wrong and the segment is re-openable. **Falsifier (for 3):** over 4 weeks a written pre-commitment neither prevents a relocation nor correctly permits one → the rule is ceremony, drop it.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- **Recording the referral-ask failure as field evidence on H-BuildRightThing.** Proposed, then withdrawn on founder correction: it was one friend's opinion about one company he judged didn't need it — not a test of the ask, and n=1. The project's own rule (2026-07-07: "do not move the wedge on n=1") applies.
- **Promoting H-DisagreementDecomposition P1 → P0** as the commercial base. Withdrawn: it answers *does the mechanism work*, not *who pays*. It stays P1. Related pitch candidate — *"find out whether you actually disagree"* — was killed by the founder on the merits: a pair stuck on a decision experiences it as disagreement, so the offer is both unbelievable and mildly insulting.
- **Reframing the deliverable as a partnership/decision agreement** (from the same 2026-07-26 session). Rejected on a fact: the CPA is free to sign on the platform, so "sell a document" is incoherent. What is sellable is verification + installation; the agreement is the residue, not the purchase.
- **Eleven further doc edits** (statable refusal · clash-not-gap · strategic-ambiguity bound · slogan reachability caveat · pricing conditionality · citizen-assembly and interdepartmental rejection rows in lean-canvas · theory-of-change precision · H-NormFlip skill-vs-norm · Min-under-adversarial-conditions · dev-lead cross-ref). All defensible, none load-bearing in a week with no tests. Deferred deliberately, not lost — they are in the a55 spec and the session thread.

**Consequences:** Content filed: **a55** "The Refutation That Never Ran" (new **ARC-6** added to `content/story-arcs.md`). **a56** "The Buyer Wants It Over" was filed and then **deleted** — its central move was the rejected sell-a-document framing. **a54** enriched with the self-concealment unfalsifiability beat (*the thesis predicts its own absence of confirming testimony, so "nobody names it" cannot distinguish right-and-invisible from wrong*); the transcript-audit test was written and then removed on founder judgment that the transcripts hold nothing. **Open, unresolved:** the March 2026 pair — a free session after which they asked for a de-risking session *and* a partner contract — remains the only recorded conversion intent in the project's history, and the thread stops there. **Pre-existing drift flagged, not fixed:** [progress.md](progress.md) §Bets and kills lists H-FounderWince as "Active"; [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) has it Dormant since 2026-07-20.

**References:** [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) §Parked H-SalesProductAlignment · [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §Unique Value Proposition "Where the protocol's value shifts" · [process-learnings.md](process-learnings.md) "An objection is a conjecture, not a refutation" · [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-07 [product] (n=1 rule) · 2026-07-24 [product] (one-motion collapse) · `content/articles/a55_the-refutation-that-never-ran.md`.

## 2026-07-24 [product]: Understanding Ledger — v1 is completion counts + progress; defer the asymmetric-effort view. **UNTESTED.**

**Context:** From the 2026-07-21 "Illusion of shared understanding" conversation, which built out the previously-bare "Clarity Ledger" concept (deferred in the P1010 spec, [definitions.md](definitions.md) "Clarity Organization" L2). The conversation designed a rich dyadic ledger; this entry scopes what v1 actually shows.

**Decision:** The Ledger v1 shows **completion counts + progress only** — letters received, letters completed, letter completion progress (e.g. 3/7 steps), sessions completed. Design rule retained: ledger entries are **frozen events** (never overwritten); "how fresh is this understanding" is resolved at read-time, not stored as a mutable value. Lands as a later tab in P1010.

**Alternatives rejected:** The richer **asymmetric-effort view** (who-requested-whom, read/unread) — deferred, not built. It turns the ledger into a status/surveillance object with real privacy weight (it exposes who carries a relationship, who never sets a number), and `read` means *opened*, not *understood* — a delivery receipt that would lie in exactly the way the system exists to prevent. Build the neutral count view first.

**Consequences:** Two `[FOUNDER DECISION]`s parked for a later version: (1) one importance score vs two — *importance-of-agreement* and *importance-of-being-understood* are separate axes the architecture keeps apart; (2) what is private-to-a-pair vs visible-to-a-group once N>2. Three ledger scales exist (dyadic / community / institutional-accounting-layer — the last is the H2 accounting-layer bet); v1 is dyadic-only. The "community Min" (what does lower-number-wins mean across a group?) is unsolved. Concept lineage: Lewis conversational scoreboard, Clark common ground, Stalnaker context set, NLP dialogue-state-tracking. **Follow-up:** the definitions.md "Clarity Organization"/ledger entry needs the v1 scope + frozen-event rule added (via `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`, not here).

**References:** [definitions.md](definitions.md) "Clarity Organization" · P1010 spec · 2026-07-23 [product] Clarity Organizations container.

## 2026-07-24 [product]: Collapse to one motion — the felt-pain wedge. Motion B is vision, not current action; sell a fixed-price done-with-you install (not a contingent catch); Bicchieri common-knowledge is why the pilot must be co-present. **UNTESTED.**

**Context:** Continuation of the 2026-07-23 clarity-organization session, stripped to first principles ("what do we actually *do*, and how do we close?"). The multi-motion framing collapsed, a delivery-risk hole in the recorded contingent POC surfaced, and a fabrication in my own prior reasoning was caught by the founder and is corrected below.

**Decision:**
1. **One motion, not two.** Motion B (champion room / integrity-referral / clarity-organization / "battle" webinar) is reclassified as **vision, not current action**. Referral cannot be the front door: it is second-degree, needs a seeded first-degree pool, and there are **0** champion-room members. The single live motion is the felt-pain wedge (H-BuildRightThing). This **narrows** the 2026-07-23 entry's "one funnel: integrity-referral is the front door" framing — referral is the *scaling engine* that switches on *after* the room has members, not the ignition.
2. **Sell a fixed-price install, not a contingent catch.** The recorded contingent POC ("pay only if within a month it surfaces a pre-nominated gap", wedge-flip 2026-07-20) puts delivery risk on the founder — do 15h, catch nothing, work for free. Since the free audit already buys belief, the guarantee is unnecessary. Sell the **installation of the system** (steps 1–4: build will · commit · install `/align` · test) at a fixed price. You sell an installed detector, not a guaranteed catch — a quiet week still succeeds because the system stays installed. Price value-anchored (one wrong feature ≫ €3k floor), not hourly. `[FOUNDER DECISION: exact price + session count]`.
3. **The offer is one object.** "Coaching" (ladischenski) vs "POC" is a false split — it is a single **done-with-you facilitated rollout of the method**: coaching = how it is delivered, POC = how it is priced. Skill-building (step 5) needs sustained practice-with-you → it is the **recurring tier** (~€99/mo, rung 3), sold separately, not crammed into the pilot.
4. **The funnel.** Source (early-stage product cos that are *hiring* — one list; the hire is the *clock*, not the target) → qualify (one question: "tell me about a recent high-stakes call where you weren't sure you and your co-founder meant the same thing"; heat = qualified) → **free audit** on a *past* disagreement (diagnose, surface the gap, they wince — **STOP**, no letter, no resolution) → close (past→future: "pay to catch the *next* one before you build on it") → **paid pilot** (fixed-price install) → recurring skill tier. Governing line: **diagnose free, treat paid** — the clarity letter is *treatment*, behind the paywall.
5. **Why the pilot must be co-present (Bicchieri).** "Build the will" is not a lecture on benefits. Will is a **conditional preference in an equilibrium of expectations**: prudential belief (installable individually) + normative expectation (others expect me to) + empirical expectation (others actually do). The recursion trap — my will waits on yours waits on mine — makes serial install impossible. Escape: flip everyone **at once** via **common knowledge in one room**. The commitment device (letter / pledge) manufactures the *normative* expectation; visible measurement sustains the *empirical* one afterward (async's real job, and only *after* install). This is what a neutral facilitator is *for* — the external agent who creates the common-knowledge moment the team can't create from inside.

**Correction (append-only — recorded here, not edited into the entry below):** the 2026-07-23 entry's falsifier line calls it "the **falsified** key-hire buying moment." That overreaches. Per the 2026-07-20 wedge-flip entry, key-hire was **superseded / flipped** (dormant-revivable), **not** payment-falsified — there is no evidence that "hiring didn't predict willingness to pay." Read "falsified key-hire buying moment" as "**superseded** key-hire buying moment." (The only genuinely falsified nearby claim is the honeymoon / illusion-peaks-early *timing* signal — unrelated to hiring or payment.)

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) run Motion A + Motion B in parallel now — B has no ignition (0 members; referral needs a seed). (b) contingent pay-per-catch pricing — delivery risk on the founder, and unnecessary once the free audit buys belief. (c) treat coaching and the pilot as separate products — same activity, two lenses.

**Consequences:** The active model is a **single funnel** ending in a fixed-price done-with-you install, with a recurring skill tier. **Hand-off needed** (not done here, per the KDD strategy-doc gate): run `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` to (a) reconcile `lean-canvas.md` on the contingent-POC → fixed-price-install shift + the funnel/page-lead, and (b) demote the org/champion/referral machinery from "one funnel front door" to explicit vision. The **P1010** org spec should move from `status: today` to someday/vision. The real **5 steps** remain `[FOUNDER DECISION]` — placeholders were used in the working session diagram until sourced from landing copy / definitions.

**References:** [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-23 [product] (org container — GTM framing narrowed here) · 2026-07-20 [product] (wedge flip — key-hire superseded, the term this entry corrects) · [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) (contingent POC → hand-off) · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-BuildRightThing · [features/p1010_clarity_organizations_community_container.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1010_clarity_organizations_community_container.md) (status → someday).

## 2026-07-23 [product]: Clarity Organizations as a community container (small spec) + integrity-referral seeding — additive to the active wedge, not an override. **UNTESTED.**

**Context:** A long design session on a "clarity community" feature. It converged on two separable things — a **feature** (a public organization container) and a **GTM refinement** (how to reach who'd populate it) — recorded here as one architecture. Reconciles with, and does not revive, the same-day org-level-opt-in-terms deferral ("The invitation is the entry" entry below) — see "Relationship".

**The feature (small, build now):** Two hardcoded Clarity Organizations — `/org/cm` (Chiang Mai nomad community) and `/org/champions` (interviewed high-integrity champions) — each with **About** (the terms), **Members** (roster, /pledgers format), **Events** (the existing calendar embed, optional per org), **Join** (single-party accept of the Clarity Organization Agreement — COA), **Manage/Leave**. Reuses PledgerCard, the accept-agreement pattern (stripped of counterparty/token), the agreement-certificate render, the ChiangMai calendar embed. **Deferred to followups:** user-facing org creation, discovery index (`/org`), private orgs + invite engine, the Clarity Ledger (documented-behavior visibility), badging/recognition. User-facing create waits until a champion asks — that ask is the platform-demand signal.

**The vision (document, don't build):** a Clarity Organization is a maturity ladder — **L1** accept the COA (join) · **L2** documented behavior visible to members (Ledger) · **L3** badged/verified (the existing 9-of-9 outcome-unit) · **L4** members pledged. "Community" and "company" are **types** of organization. Multi-tenant is the vision; two hardcoded orgs are v1. See [definitions.md](definitions.md) "Clarity Organization".

**The GTM (additive — nothing overrides the active wedge):** reach candidates by a two-pronged referral ask — "who is your highest-**integrity** person, and who is in the most **pain**?" — describe the pain, state the current hypothesis, and **let referrals overturn it**. Targeting is held as a testable hypothesis, not stage-locked; the seed–A active focus (H-BuildRightThing) and the paid-1:1 bridge are **unchanged**. Sharpens the documented "referrer = acquisition mechanism" and corroborates H-ChampionYield (still n=1, not promoted — no new field evidence this session). New deductive mechanism: **scale converts a high-integrity practitioner into a champion** — at small scale they verify by hand (no product need); at coordination scale, others' lack of will/skill forces them to *install* the protocol in others (= H-ChampionYield's buyer). The PM at the cross-team node is a candidate to test. One funnel: integrity-referral + interview is the front door → acute pain routes to the paid wedge (Motion A), no acute pain to the champion org (Motion B, seeding); champions are the distribution layer that refers both.

**Relationship to the org-level-opt-in-terms deferral (same day):** that deferral rejected replacing the **bilateral CPA** with **org-level terms in the paid funnel** (a click is a weaker pre-commitment than a will-at-the-breaking-point CPA; no prospect had raised n²). Honest correction (adversarial review bf7b92e4): this entry **partially revives** it — the deferral also rejected, as a standalone, *"building org-terms machinery now for a constraint no live prospect has raised,"* and the container is that machinery. Reason (a) (weak pre-commitment) genuinely does not bite (community-join carries no will-at-breaking-point weight); the build-now rejection **does**, and building anyway is a **conscious founder override**, justified by serving 3 already-interviewed people, not by the object being "different." The COA here is **community membership**; the CPA stays the bilateral paid-funnel instrument. **Guardrail:** community-join must not creep into "org-terms replace the CPA in the paid funnel" — that stays deferred until a prospect names n².

**Falsifiers:** *(budget-carving, H-ChampionYield)* a champion succeeds internally but no budget appears within ~N months → the free→paid bridge is broken (structural echo of the falsified key-hire "buying moment"). *(feature)* the 3 interviewed people + nomads are invited to the page and don't engage → the public-roster-sets-a-norm thesis is weak. **A join is enthusiasm, not proof** (adversarial review): the load-bearing metric is ≥1 member-originated second adoption, per H-ChampionYield's "traceable second pledge, not enthusiasm." *(targeting)* if "most pain" referrals point outside the build-right-thing hypothesis and convert better → the team-internal/seed–A hypothesis is overridden (record then).

**Known risk:** counterfactual attribution (the Ledger's "misses not caught") is epistemically hard; org-domain A/B needs decision volume small orgs lack early.

**References:** [decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-23 [product] (org-level opt-in deferral, below) · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-ChampionYield, H-BuildRightThing · [definitions.md](definitions.md) "Clarity Organization" · [goals.md](goals.md) (referral seeding arm)

## 2026-07-23 [process]: Repair the SINGLE-VALUE canary; do NOT extend it to `goals.md`. `/docs-strategy-update` now fixes `goals.md` in the same edit — **supersedes 2026-07-03 "read-not-written"**

**Context:** `docs/goals.md` drifts. It sits in neither of the two mechanisms that watch the strategy docs: it is not a gated home of `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`, and it is not in the `pre-commit-checks.sh` SINGLE-VALUE canary's doc list. Nine days after the 2026-07-20 wedge flip it still carried a stale copy of the page-lead and still framed a dormant hypothesis (H-FounderWince) as the active bet.

**Rejected — extending the SINGLE-VALUE canary to `goals.md` + `story-point-model.md`.** This was the obvious fix and it is **false coverage**. Three independent reviewers hand-traced `scripts/check-single-value-slots.py` against the real files and converged: (a) the prescribed marker placement exits **0**, not 2 — `goals.md`'s prose line ends the callout group before any lead is reached; (b) a second proposed marker sits in a section with no blockquote callouts and can never fire; (c) `story-point-model.md` has zero markers and zero dated callouts — a permanent no-op that prints a green tick; (d) **wrong failure mode** — the canary counts *co-existing* callouts (`>=2`), while `goals.md` fails by *destructive in-place rewrite*, where the count stays 1 and the exit stays 0. A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate: it trains dismissal.

**Decision — repair the gate that exists.** Four verified defects in shipped code, each with its failure path exercised (epistemic.md gate 7):
1. **Fail-open on a missing script.** If `check-single-value-slots.py` were absent, `python3` itself exits 2 — and the `rc -eq 2` branch printed the resulting traceback *formatted as a real reconciliation finding*. Now: a missing script is an **ERROR**, and rc=2 only counts as a finding when the output actually starts with `SINGLE-VALUE slot`.
2. **`PRIMARY` disarmed the winner.** It was in the reconciliation-token list, but it marks the *winning* lead. Following the documented "primary + `[FALLBACK]`" instruction dropped the counted set to 0, so the next untagged lead could only ever reach 1 — exit 0 forever. **The act of reconciling silenced the slot for all future conflicts.** Removed.
3. **Unanchored token match.** `[Dd]ormant` / `[Pp]arked` matched anywhere in a lead-in, so a copy-edit moving the word "dormant" into a lead silently discounted a genuine competing directive. Now anchored to a **closed bracketed prefix** at the start of the lead-in.

**Correction, same day — the bracket was briefly made optional, and that was wrong.** Requiring `[` turned `lean-canvas.md` §Channels red (its callout reconciles with an older unbracketed `**Dormant (…)**`), and the bracket was relaxed to `\[?` rather than touch the doc, justified as "retagging live positioning content to make a gate green would be worse." **Adversarial review refuted this** and it is recorded because the reasoning error is the reusable lesson, not the regex:
- The justification described an edit that was never required. Bracketing the lead-in changes the delimiter and nothing else — the callout still reads "This section describes the dormant cofounder/coach distribution path." Punctuating a token is not editing positioning. Verified: strict regex on the bracketed doc → exit 0.
- The relaxation **re-admitted the exact bypass the same commit claimed to close** — `\b` fires on a hyphen, so a lead-in opening `dormant-revivable …` was silenced again. That string is copy already present in the file the gate was relaxed for.
- **The bracket is what separates a tag from a sentence.** `[Dormant]` retires a lead; `Dormant no longer — revived as THE lead` promotes one. Without the bracket both reconcile, and the failure is **asymmetric**: missing a retirement tag fails closed (a spurious red), silencing a **revival** fails open — two live answers under one slot, exit 0. Revivals are the highest-stakes edit a single-valued slot receives. Four revival fixtures flipped exit 2 → exit 0 under the relaxed form.
- **Generalisable:** a gate loosened *in direct response to its own red result* is how gates become decorative. The red was a formatting violation, not a strategy conflict, so the proportionate response was to fix the formatting. `CHARTER.md` was ambiguous here (it bracketed only two of the six tokens and listed the rest bare) — that ambiguity is now closed rather than resolved in favour of the unenforceable reading.

Resolution: restored the required bracket, bracketed `lean-canvas.md`'s callout, amended `CHARTER.md` to prescribe brackets for all six tokens and to state why they are load-bearing.

5. **Every unrunnable state was a non-blocking WARN.** Also from review: a canary that cannot execute (syntax error, missing interpreter, zero files extracted) printed a yellow line and the commit succeeded — the same fail-open-into-green the missing-script guard was written to kill, one branch over. A canary that cannot run is now an **ERROR**, like a canary that is absent.
6. **`git show` failure lost the doc silently.** An unmerged path — precisely the commit where competing directives get merged — is in the index but not at stage 0, so extraction failed, the arg list emptied, and the script's own usage message surfaced as an ignorable warning while the staged doc went unscanned. Now an ERROR naming the unscanned files.
7. **`sed` on the temp path could abort the entire suite.** A `TMPDIR` containing `#` made `sed "s#$SV_TMP/##g"` fail under `set -e`, killing the run *after* a real finding was computed and before every later check — leaking the temp dir too. Replaced with bash substitution; `mktemp -d` failure is now guarded and reported.
8. **The script path was env-overridable.** `${SV_SCRIPT:-…}` had been added purely to let a test point at a fake path; it meant any parent process could set one variable and turn the gate green with a positive checkmark and no trace. Hardcoded.

**Known gap, stated not solved (`features/p1009`):** the canary recognises a competing lead only when the date sits inside the bold lead-in of a top-level `>` callout. Eight other shapes — date in the body, human-format date, nested `>>`, `> - ` bullet, placement after the group's closing prose — all return exit 0, each verified by execution. Two of them match formatting `lean-canvas.md` already uses. Widening the rule changes what gets flagged across all five docs and needs a before/after triage, so it is filed rather than patched. `CHARTER.md` now states the gap so the convention is not trusted beyond what it enforces.
4. **Read the working tree, not the index.** Now uses staged content via `git show ":$doc"`, matching the sibling Gate D/F block. `goals.md` and the strategy docs have automated writers and the main checkout's index is shared across sessions (2026-06-06 incident) — the canary could pass on bytes that were never committed.

**Supersedes commit `3e4a5fa7` (2026-07-03)**, which settled *"`goals.md` is read-not-written… hand off (never fix)."* **New evidence:** `decisions.md` records two explicit hand-offs — 2026-07-11 [product] (*"`goals.md` needs updating… no gated skill writes goals.md; do it directly"*) and 2026-07-20 [product] (*"Tactical POC mechanics + price → goals.md (hand-off; not this entry)"*) — and **neither produced the edit**: on 2026-07-23 `goals.md` still framed the hypothesis the 2026-07-20 entry had just demoted as the active bet. Detect-and-hand-off is a null operation when no other actor owns the file. `/docs-strategy-update` (v1.3.0) now reconciles `goals.md` **in the same edit** when a sync it just applied invalidates it — under Gates 1 and 3 only (no SINGLE-VALUE markers exist there, so Gate 8 does not apply). Free-standing tactical edits to `goals.md` remain outside the skill. Naming this as a supersession is deliberate: a future `git log -S` should find a link, not two live opposite settlements.

**Honest limit — this binds almost nothing.** `/docs-strategy-update` has **0 recorded invocations** in `.private/logs/skill-costs.log`. `/day` edits `goals.md` "silently (no confirmation needed)" and the kanban `PATCH /api/goals-strategic` endpoint rewrites it from a browser click. Both remain ungated. Nothing mechanical watches `goals.md` after this change; today's contradictions were fixed by hand.

**Side finding — `goals.md`'s consumers had been reading nothing.** Both the kanban `/api/goals-strategic` endpoint and `/day` parse `## Next Steps` / `## Dos` / `## Don'ts`; `goals.md` has had none of those headings for an unknown period. Both degraded silently to green — an empty Goals page reading "No goals", an empty WHAT'S NEXT block. Fixed by making the mismatch loud (a `structureNotFound` payload naming expected-vs-found headings, surfaced in `GoalsPage.tsx` and `/day`), **not** by picking a side: whether to restore the headings or reteach the parsers is filed as a bug, not decided here.

**Falsifier (inspectable, not event-counted):** at the next audit-mode run, if `goals.md` again carries a hypothesis-status or page-lead contradiction introduced by a strategy sync, the same-edit obligation is decorative — drop it and treat `goals.md` drift as an accepted cost. Checkable by reading two files.

**References:** `scripts/check-single-value-slots.py`; `scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh` §13e; `.claude/commands/slava/maintain/docs-strategy-update/SKILL.md` (v1.3.0, Step 0.2 + Step 6); `docs/CHARTER.md` §single-valued slots; `.claude/rules/epistemic.md` gate 7

## 2026-07-23 [product]: The invitation is the entry to the clarity letter — CPA becomes the object *under* verification, not the precondition. Org-level opt-in terms deferred. **UNTESTED.**

**Context:** Working the `/hiring` funnel, two premises were tested. (1) *"The buyer must be a founder, otherwise they can't credibly introduce the agreement."* Partly right, wrong mechanism — see the Alternatives below. (2) *"Stop pushing the CPA as the entry, because organizations are many-to-many"* — an n² objection to a bilateral pre-commitment, with the proposed replacement being an org-level opt-in to clarity terms.

**Decision:** **The invitation becomes the entry point, and it has no dead branch.** Both outcomes produce a letter and both produce verification:
- **Accept** → trigger the letter: *"we want to verify our understanding of what you just signed."*
- **Reject** → *"tell us why"* → verify we understood the refusal.

The refusal branch is arguably the richer one: a live disagreement is better test content than a nod. The CPA is retained but **re-positioned** — it is the artifact being read, verified and adopted, not a gate to pass before anything happens.

**This is not new — it is a second delivery surface for a move already documented.** [cofounder-program-facilitator-guide.md](cofounder-program-facilitator-guide.md) §"Branching on the CPA probe" already runs exactly this structure live: the seed letter *is* the CPA; both-agree → sign live; disagree → *"run the switch on the CPA divergence itself. That is the demo."* The new decision generalizes that facilitator branch from the room to the async invitation. It is also the self-priming property in [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §Solution: *"the instrument clears the beliefs that block the instrument."*

**Deferred, not adopted — org-level opt-in terms.** Two reasons: (a) **the mechanism it would dilute.** The CPA's job is *will at the breaking point* (`lean-canvas.md` Move 3 feeding Move 1) — a pre-commitment made while calm so it holds when it isn't. Terms clicked once during onboarding are a far weaker pre-commitment; solving n² this way trades away the thing that makes any single instance work. (b) **Many-to-many is not the current buyer.** Gate 3 (`.private/docs/business/discovery-questions.md`) requires a *specific live dyad* and caps the window at seed–A because "late = HR exists" — multi-party orgs are the disqualified end of the same gate. No prospect has yet named n² as a blocker.

**Alternatives rejected:** **Founder-only justified by "credibility to introduce the agreement"** — rejected as the *reason*, though the conclusion stands. An agreement between two people needs no org mandate; a VP hiring a director can say "before you start, let's both write what we think the job is and check," and credibility comes from being the counterparty, not from the title. A prospect breaks that argument in one sentence ("I have full authority over this hire"). The load-bearing reason is the one already recorded in `features/archive/2026-07/p989_pre_audit_qualification_gate.md`: a founder has an **unproven bet that isn't written down, can't be checked for months, and exists only in their head** — plus findability ("anybody hiring" is a category, not a segment). · **Dropping the CPA outright** — loses the will mechanism with nothing replacing it. · **Building org-terms machinery now** — future-proofing against a constraint no live prospect has raised.

**Consequences:** The reject branch needs a **one-click hard exit** by design. "Tell us why you refused" that keeps pulling is the unsubscribe-leads-to-a-survey pattern — coercive, and it burns exactly the trust the instrument sells. Revisit org-level terms when a prospect names n² as the actual blocker. Preserves the standing separation of artifacts (2026-06-25 entry: CPA bilateral/live, Clarity Pledge unilateral/public).

**Falsifier:** first three invitations sent — does the *reject* branch produce a letter anyone engages with? If refusals go silent (no stated why, no response to the verification bid), the no-dead-branch claim is false and the invitation is a one-sided gate after all.

**References:** [cofounder-program-facilitator-guide.md](cofounder-program-facilitator-guide.md) §"Branching on the CPA probe"; [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §Solution (5-move model, Move 1/Move 3); `.private/docs/business/discovery-questions.md` Gate 3; `features/archive/2026-07/p989_pre_audit_qualification_gate.md`

## 2026-07-22 [process]: CORRECTION to the entry below — the "decision alignment" reframe is an articulation of H-BuildRightThing, not a new pivot

**Context:** The entry immediately below ("Target decision *alignment*, not decision *quality*") was written after a multi-turn targeting analysis conducted **without reading `lean-canvas.md` or `hypotheses.md` first**. A Gate-3 pass during the subsequent `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` run found the conclusion already settled two days earlier.

**What was already in the docs (2026-07-20, H-BuildRightThing / lean-canvas §Customer Segments active focus):** (a) the target is a **growing seed–A team (2+ people)**, not a co-founder pair; (b) the segment is **"findable by the hiring / growth signal — a new hire is the *clock*, not the target"**; (c) the claim is **"calibration, not accuracy — we remove false confidence, we do NOT make you correct about the customer."** That third item is the same distinction the entry below re-derives as "columns, not rows." A fourth: `lean-canvas.md` §UVP fallback (2026-07-04) already carries *"when execution is cheap, the edge is problem **formulation** — the scarce skill."*

**Correction:** The entry below is **not a repositioning**. It restates an existing Active-P0 bet in different vocabulary. What is genuinely new from that session is narrower: (1) the 2×2 as a **communication artifact** — a way to explain calibration-not-accuracy to an audience, shipped as `/presi` slide 29; (2) the "load-bearing claim" generalisation (decision / assumption / problem-formulation are all claims that must be shared) as a mild widening of "verify they understood each other before agreeing"; (3) the two sibling entries below (RFC/ADR sourcing rejection, launch spike-vs-compounder), which have no prior. The pair-vs-team "tension" raised in that session was a **false alarm** — the docs moved to teams on 2026-07-20. No strategy-doc edit was made: Gate 3 dedup (concept present, same conclusion → cite, don't propose) and Gate 8 (`SINGLE-VALUE: page-lead` clean at exit 0; adding a competing lead is the FIX that gate blocks).

**Consequences:** Read the entry below as *articulation*, not pivot — do not treat it as evidence of a fresh direction change. **Process lesson (the reason this is `[process]`, not `[product]`):** a multi-turn strategy conversation is exactly the case CLAUDE.md's "check what already exists before building new" covers, and the check is cheapest at turn 1, not after the analysis is committed. Concretely: before any targeting / ICP / positioning discussion, read `lean-canvas.md` §Customer Segments + §UVP and the Active P0 hypotheses **first** — the strategy-doc gate catches this at write time, but by then the reasoning has already been produced and recorded. Cost here was one committed decisions.md entry overstating novelty and several turns of re-derivation.

## 2026-07-22 [product]: Target decision *alignment*, not decision *quality* — they are orthogonal axes (UNTESTED)

**Context:** A session that began as launch-channel research turned into a targeting reframe. The target moved alignment → decision-making → strategic decisions → and back to alignment-on-decisions. Two intermediate framings were tried and abandoned: (a) "help teams decide well," which collides with a crowded space (frameworks, strategy tools, decision records) and mis-locates the pain; (b) "strategic decisions" specifically, which broke the session's own targeting gates — strategic decisions are rare (a few per year) and involve the *fewest* stakeholders in a startup (2–3 founders), so a product attached to them has no usage loop, no cadence, and nothing to retain on.

**Decision:** Decision quality and decision alignment are **orthogonal axes, not points on one scale**. Everything the market builds improves the rows (quality of reasoning); CP is the columns (whether the people involved actually share the same understanding of what was decided).

| | Everyone truly understands | Nobody really understands |
|---|---|---|
| **Good decision** | Executes well | **Executes wrong, blames the plan** |
| **Bad decision** | Fails fast, learns, corrects | Fails slow, nobody can say why |

The top-right quadrant is what the main-landing hero already describes ("Your team agreed. And built the wrong feature.") — that is not a bad decision, it is a decision nobody shared. Two consequences follow. **(1) The operating unit is the assumption, not the strategic decision.** Strategy is set quarterly but its assumptions are contacted constantly — every user conversation, shipped feature, and metric that comes back wrong hits one. That gives strategic stakes at operational frequency, resolving the rare-event problem. **(2) CP is a verification layer, not a decision process.** It attaches to whatever the team already does (RFC, Slack thread, founder conversation) rather than replacing it — a materially lower adoption bar than "change how you decide."

**Falsifier:** *Teams record that they agreed and never verify that they understood the same thing — and when a decision goes wrong, the gap traces back to that missing step rather than to the decision's reasoning.* Testable in ~10 founder conversations. If failures trace primarily to reasoning quality, evidence, or timing rather than to divergent understanding, the columns framing is wrong and the row-improvers own the problem.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) decision *quality* as the target — crowded, and mis-locates the pain; (b) *strategic decisions* as the unit — breaks the frequency and stakeholder-count gates, and yields a product used once a quarter by two people; (c) the earlier bare "alignment" framing — true but vaguer; "alignment on a decision, at the moment it is declared settled" names an observable event.

**Consequences:** Status **UNTESTED** — recorded now under the record-under-uncertainty rule, not because it is validated. **Open founder decision, unresolved:** is the product used *at* the decision (rare, high-ceremony, weak retention) or *between* decisions, on the assumptions (frequent, lower per-session stakes, retains)? Pricing, cadence, ICP and retention model all hang on this and it was not settled. Sourcing implication: comprehension gaps only surface when someone says them out loud, so conversation-shaped sources (HN Algolia phrase search, practitioner subreddits, founder interviews) rank above any artifact-shaped source. Deck: `/presi` slide 29 renders the 2×2. **Follow-up strategy-doc edits deferred to `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`** — this entry does not write the gated docs.

**References:** [public/presi/index.html](../public/presi/index.html) slide 29 · [docs/hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-DisagreementDecomposition, H-PopperianIncrement (adjacent research claims — this entry is a positioning claim, not a research one)

## 2026-07-22 [product]: Public RFC/ADR repos rejected as a prospect-sourcing channel — adverse selection

**Context:** While looking for sources exposing the targeting gates (decision frequency, stakeholder count, disagreement behaviour), public RFC and ADR repositories looked ideal and were briefly proposed as the top source: count the RFCs (frequency), count the reviewers (stakeholders), read the objections (disagreement) — all three observable without asking anyone anything.

**Decision:** **Rejected as a sourcing channel.** A team publishing numbered ADRs with a superseding convention has already built a decision protocol — they are among the least likely buyers. The gates are observable precisely *because* the problem is solved. Compounding this: public RFC/ADR repos skew hard to open source, developer tooling and infrastructure, so it is also one narrow vertical. CP's actual ICP — high decision volume, many stakeholders, no protocol — is **invisible in public repos by construction**: the absence of an ADR folder is the qualifying signal, and absence is not searchable.

**Alternatives rejected:** using RFC/ADR repos as a lead list (this entry); treating observability of the gates as a proxy for fit — observability and need are inversely correlated here, which is the general trap this entry names.

**Consequences:** Retained for two other uses. **(1) Product input** — the `Rationale and alternatives` and `Unresolved questions` sections of public RFCs are the largest free corpus of what a well-run decision looks like when written down; read for protocol mechanics only, never for subject matter (these are *technical* decisions, CP targets product/strategic ones). **(2) Category evidence** — ADR templates ship in Notion, Confluence and Linear, so demand for decision logging is established, in one function, for the *reversible* decisions. That asymmetry is itself a finding: engineers built a documentation discipline for the decisions that needed it least. **Open, unverified:** whether any RFC/ADR in the corpus verifies *understanding* rather than merely recording agreement — expected to be near-zero, which would be evidence for the entry above. A reading guide with links and a reading protocol was produced outside the repo (not committed — it cites no CP-internal material). **General heuristic worth reusing:** when a signal is unusually easy to observe, check whether observability is caused by the problem already being solved.

**References:** [docs/decisions.md](decisions.md) 2026-07-22 [product] "Target decision *alignment*, not decision *quality*"

## 2026-07-22 [product]: Launch channels are either spikes or compounders — almost none are both (research-derived)

**Context:** Deep research (44 sources) on how teams launch products, run before the targeting reframe above. Relevant to CP's own launch planning; recorded so the model is not re-derived.

**Decision:** Sort launch channels by whether they produce a burst or accumulate. **Spikes** — Hacker News (5–30k visitors in 24h, ~24h half-life, 0.5–2% signup conversion), Product Hunt (only ~10% of submissions featured; featured products see 1–5k visitors and 10–150 signups; a 2026 #1-of-Day is ~800–2,200 signups), press, and accelerator demo days. **Compounders** — owned email, organic and AI search, community, and a recurring launch cadence; these produce no day-one signal at all. The correct mental model is that **spikes exist to accelerate compounders**: judged as customer acquisition an HN front page usually loses money; judged as *audience* acquisition it often wins. Two supporting findings. **(1) Launch cadence is a management tool before it is a marketing one** — Supabase's own account states Launch Week was built to recreate the pressure of a YC batch; teams that copy the format without the internal forcing function get seven days of silence. **(2) Launch metrics have been repriced as evidence** — a "#1 on Product Hunt" claim without an activation number now reads as a negative investor signal, and across 5,025 verified YC companies the era-adjusted odds ratio for Demo Day hype predicting unicorn outcomes is 1.04 (null).

**Alternatives rejected:** treating Product Hunt and Hacker News as substitutes — they trade off oppositely (HN gives volume with no residual; PH gives a permanent indexed asset with low volume); optimising a launch for day-one numbers — Day-7/Day-30 retention is the only output that should change a decision.

**Consequences:** For CP, never report a launch number without the retention number beside it. The channels worth investing in are the ones that **cannot be started this quarter** (community, analyst relations, owned list) — earned-entry channels have appreciated as attention has become scarcer. One genuinely new channel: AI answer engines, where a reported 47% of B2B buyers now do vendor research; launch content should be written to be *cited by a model* — fact-dense, dated, clearly attributed. **Evidence caveat:** a large share of the launch-tactics literature is published by vendors selling launch services, so channel-effectiveness figures are optimistic bounds; three figures (LinkedIn ROAS comparison, a 23x AI-referral conversion multiple, a creator-sponsorship return model) were single-sourced and should not be used as planning inputs. **Follow-up:** the spike/compounder model may belong in a gated strategy doc — deferred to `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`.

**References:** research report at `~/Documents/Product_Launch_Methods_Research_20260722/` (outside repo — contains no CP-internal material)

## 2026-07-21 [technical]: A section repeated on N pages should own its full `<section>` chrome and take no props — pages drop `<Component />` with no wrapper

**Context:** The founder-credibility block ("Built by someone who paid for the lesson", €398k) lived as hand-rolled markup on `/founder`, `/coach`, and the main landing. It "looked good on `/founder`" but was visibly different on the others — each page re-implemented the surrounding `<section>` padding, container width, and scroll-reveal, so they drifted. A separate but related trap: P1004 re-homed `/` to `build-right-thing-landing.tsx`, which carried its *own* copy of the old inline block — so "unify the component" silently missed the actual main page until a browser check caught it (`founder-photo.jpg` still rendering).

**Decision (P1005/P1006):** The shared component owns the **entire** section — `<section>` chrome, container, `Reveal`, and the clip/data constants — and takes **no props**. Every surface renders `<FounderCredibility />` with no wrapper of its own; markup is byte-identical by construction. This is stronger than the prop-driven "renders byte-identically" pattern (P987 HardTruthChat): take-nothing removes the per-page wrapper as a drift surface entirely. A one-class change (`items-center` → `items-start`, P1007) then propagates to all four pages from one edit.

**Alternatives rejected:** (1) props for per-page variation — reintroduces the divergence surface the change was fixing; (2) a shared *inner* component with each page supplying its own `<section>` wrapper — the wrapper is exactly what drifted, so it must be owned by the component. (3) Trusting "all pages import the component" without a browser check — a re-homed route (P1004) can hold a stale inline copy the grep for the import name won't surface.

**Consequences:** For any block that must look identical across ≥2 pages, default to a take-nothing component owning its full section. When "unifying" a repeated block, browser-verify every route that renders it — an import-name grep misses a route holding an inline copy. Blast radius of a style tweak becomes one line.

**References:** [src/app/components/landing/founder-credibility.tsx](../src/app/components/landing/founder-credibility.tsx) · [features/done/2026-06-10/p1006_main_landing_unify_credibility.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/p1006_main_landing_unify_credibility.md)
