## 2026-07-14 [product]: `/align` scope refinement — two layers; solo use is legitimate for layer 1, only layer 2 needs a counterparty

**Context:** The "only for counterparties" scope (entry below) was too strong. The founder wants to run `/align` **solo** — surface his own high-stakes decisions, see the points/stories/anti-points, keep the log — and build the *habit* first, which makes involving a coach (the counterparty) easy later.

**Decision:** `/align` has **two separable layers**: **(1) detection + decomposition** (surface the decision, make point/story/anti-point legible) — has **real solo value** as a self-awareness / what-to-falsify log, no counterparty needed; **(2) comprehension verification** (the min-gate, two-sided rating) — **needs a counterparty** (a self-rating can't self-certify). "Only for counterparties" applies to **layer 2**, not the whole tool. Solo runs are exploratory practice: run layers 1, self-rate honestly but **labelled a self-signal, not "verified."**

**Use ≠ build (holds the freeze).** *Using* the already-hardened skill manually is zero-build and freeze-compatible. *Wiring it into `/weekly` + a persistent decision store* is **build** — still frozen. The lean order: run it manually as a habit → if the habit proves valuable over weeks → that demonstrated need is what **pulls** the wiring/store build (honoring the freeze's "let a real need pull it"). Guards the founder's known scope-expansion-under-uncertainty pattern.

**Falsifier:** if solo runs produce no durable self-awareness value after a few weeks of the habit, layer 1's standalone value is overclaimed and `/align` really is counterparty-only.

**References:** decisions.md 2026-07-14 [product] (`/align` counterparty scope; build freeze) · [story-point-model.md](story-point-model.md) "counterparty condition" · [align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md)

## 2026-07-14 [product]: Freeze further alignment-tooling build — no customer is pulling the requirements; revisit when one is

**Context:** After a session hardening `/align` and the story/point model, the founder tested the honest question: *can I use this myself now?* Answer: not really. An alignment-between-people tool **can't be dogfooded solo**, and the one near-term internal counterparty (a co-builder being brought on) **doesn't need the async Clarity Letter** — a founder + one close report just talk and trigger the protocol verbally (she knows it). The async letter only earns its keep as *faster data-gathering / decision-prep*, which needs front-loaded preparation that isn't worth it before a customer exists. Continuing to build (the letter product, the `/align` expansion, the decision-graph vision below) would be **building on speculative requirements with no puller** — the exact anti-pattern the lean mission avoids.

**Decision:** **Freeze further alignment-tooling build.** Priority shifts to **acquiring a coaching/consulting customer** in the alignment space (the active GTM — founder + active key hire), whose real needs then *pull* the tool's requirements. Keep what's cheap and already done (the `/align` skill hardening this session — useful for the founder's own self-awareness / what-to-falsify). Come back to the build when a customer's needs drive the design.

**Parked (revisit trigger = a customer, or N people with decisions in the system):**
- **The decision-graph vision.** Founders "lock" high-stakes decisions into the system (even solo ones); agents scan the database of everyone's locked decisions, detect **conflicts / divergence / synergies**, surface the **counterparties** automatically, and — on confirmation — drive **letter prep → send → answer**. Strong fit for a manager whose one decision influences many people (broadcast a high-stakes decision, collect positions, verify comprehension). Needs multiple people with decisions in the system first, so it is a later-stage build, not what unblocks now.

**Alternatives rejected:** keep building the letter flow / decision-graph on inferred requirements (no customer pulling → speculative); force `/align` to be a solo dogfood tool (structurally can't — an alignment tool needs a counterparty, 2026-07-14 [product] scope entry below); treat the co-builder as the dogfood via async letters (she doesn't need them — verbal protocol trigger suffices for one close report).

**Falsifier:** if the co-builder relationship or an early customer surfaces a concrete letter/decision-graph need *before* you'd otherwise build it, the freeze was slightly too early for that one piece — unfreeze just that piece, pulled by the real need. And if a coaching customer, once acquired, does **not** pull any alignment-tooling requirement, the tool's product-market fit is weaker than assumed (H-FounderWince / H-ProtocolTransfers territory).

**References:** decisions.md 2026-07-14 [product] (`/align` counterparty scope) · [goals.md](goals.md) §Active (coaching bridge = the customer motion) · plan `~/.claude/plans/serene-jumping-blossom.md`

## 2026-07-14 [product]: `/align` (Clarity Flash) is for alignment *with a counterparty* — surface stakeholders, gate on the align-target first (UNTESTED)

**Context:** During the first real `/align` runs, the founder surfaced the scoping crux the skill was missing: filing a story + point + min-rating is a **two-party comprehension act**, so it only earns its cost when there is **someone whose comprehension matters**. A high-stakes decision with *no counterparty to align with* is just self-analysis — which an agent does more cheaply without the comprehension apparatus. This also explained why a live clawback/runway candidate felt off: high-stakes, but a prepared *wait-state* gated on an adversary (the trustee) and a contractor (the lawyer) — no align-target, so not an alignment case.

**Decision (UNTESTED):** `/align`'s domain is **high-stakes decisions where a counterparty's alignment matters**; no-counterparty cases route to **plain analysis**, not the story/point/min loop. Three concrete skill changes (shipped to `align.md` this session):
- **Stakeholders are first-class in detection.** The Stage-1 card gains `stakeholders` (everyone involved + relation: partner / contractor-or-peer / adversary / future-recipient) and `align-target` (whose comprehension matters, or NONE). Channel follows relation: a **Clarity Letter** for a partner, a **call/ask** for a contractor (e.g. a lawyer you won't onboard), **none** for an adversary.
- **Gate 0 — the align-target gate runs FIRST**, before the stake gate. "Who is this for?" is the cheapest filter and can retire a case before any stake quantification. `NONE` → "solo analysis, `/align` is the wrong tool — want plain analysis?" and stop.
- **Angle transparency.** A story affords multiple points; *which* to decompose around depends on which risk matters. Step 3 surfaces **2-3 candidate point/anti-point angles, each labeled with the risk it targets**, and the founder picks the crux — the selection is a founder call, not a silent one.

**Alternatives rejected:** keep detection stake-first (lets no-counterparty cases consume the full loop before their pointlessness surfaces); treat every high-stakes *thing* as alignable (conflates a *state you wait on* with a *decision with a counterparty* — the clawback mis-aim); pick the decomposition angle silently (hides the highest-leverage choice — "aligning on the agent's crux, not yours").

**Consequences:** `align.md` Stage 1 restructured (stakeholder fields + Gate 0 + angle transparency); `story-point-model.md` gains the "counterparty condition" scope section. Also captured earlier this session: 3-way stake choice, first-person story recovery, internal 2a harvest, the answered-check gate + widened harvest corpus. **Falsifier:** if founders get durable value from `/align` on decisions with genuinely no counterparty (now or future), the counterparty condition is too strict and the no-counterparty→plain-analysis route is wrong.

**References:** [align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md) · [story-point-model.md](story-point-model.md) "counterparty condition" · plan `~/.claude/plans/serene-jumping-blossom.md`
## 2026-07-15 [process]: the against-argument carries the same evidentiary burden as the for-argument — it is the only claim nothing downstream catches

**Context:** Four times in one session the assistant asserted something it had not read or tested, and was wrong every time: `/founder` was "a 539-line dev snapshot nobody reviewed for prod" (it was verbatim the page already live at `/`); the site-wide canonical fix "needs its own spec" for blast radius (it was ~10 lines); `/founder`'s hero differed from `/`'s in its `min-h-screen`/padding classes (the class strings were byte-identical — the real cause was a layout wrapper); and React 19 "extracts `<link>` so Helmet's canonical never reached the DOM" (a probe showed it renders — there were *two* canonicals). The four split 2/2 in a way that is the actual finding. **Incidents 3 and 4 were caught by machinery** — a grep before editing, and a code review that forced a probe. **Incidents 1 and 2 needed the founder**, and both were arguments *against* doing work.

**Decision:** Append to CLAUDE.md's "Architecture & Implementation Style" (`9a1855c2`, net-zero lines): *"The against-argument carries the same evidentiary burden as the for-argument — and it is the only one nothing downstream catches, because if it lands, no code runs and no test fires. 'Blast radius', 'needs its own spec', 'nobody reviewed that' are claims: read the file and cite the lines, or don't make the claim."* Wording came from `/slava:maintain:claude-md`, which **rejected the original draft** ("an argument against building that rests on unread code is not an argument") as duplicating "Falsify Before You Rely" and as naming the symptom rather than the mechanism.

**Why no existing rule fired:** the gate's audit is the load-bearing part. "Falsify Before You Rely" scopes to *tool* claims — "this needs its own spec" is not one. The "argue against building before arguing for it" instruction triggers *"before building"* — definitionally absent when the proposal is *not* to build. **Every verification rule in CLAUDE.md triggers on the agent DOING something.** A recommendation to do nothing is self-executing: it consumes no test, no review, no runtime. That asymmetry — not effort-avoidance, which asserts an unfalsifiable motive — is the root cause.

**Alternatives rejected:** A 9th gate in `.claude/rules/epistemic.md` (its eight gates all answer *"how do I establish a fact"*; this answers *"which claims need establishing at all"*, and would sit orphaned from the instruction that generates against-building arguments). SKIP as redundant (rejected: the nominally-covering rules evade by their own literal text — shown above).

**Consequences:** Incident 4 is deliberately **not** covered by this clause — it was a wrong technical claim, not an argument against work, and belongs to the rule that already caught it. A clause that appeared to catch all four would be laundering scope.

**Falsifier:** A future session talks the founder out of work using invented risk *despite* this clause being loaded → the clause is decoration and the constraint must be mechanical, not textual.

**References:** [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) "Architecture & Implementation Style", `.claude/rules/epistemic.md`

## 2026-07-15 [technical]: three prod bugs were invisible at desktop width by construction — the front door was unbookable on phones

**Context:** A blind visual-QA subagent (screenshots + checklist only, no diff, no intent) reviewed `/`, `/founder`, `/intro` at 375/320/desktop and surfaced three **pre-existing, live-in-prod** bugs that every prior check had missed. All three had shipped; none were introduced by P987.

**The bugs, and why desktop hid them:**
1. **`/intro` was unbookable on a phone** (`43da4052`) — the destination of the site's primary CTA rendered only the struck-through past week, with no selectable date. One flat `minHeight: 580px` served every width, but Google's embed stacks the picker vertically below ~520px (month grid → day nav → slots) and needs ~880px there, while laying out horizontally above. **The phone needs *more* height than the desktop — the opposite of what a single floor can express.**
2. **The TEMPLATE watermark never rendered below ~520px** (`30a9a62c`) — `IntersectionObserver` `threshold: 0.6` is a ratio *of the observed element*, and the stamp is ~867px wide at its pre-landing `scale(2.7)`; the greatest achievable ratio at 375px is 0.43 (measured live at 0.433). A deadlock: the stamp had to fire to shrink to the ~336px that would satisfy the threshold. The demo agreement therefore shipped to phones with **no visual "this is a sample" marker**.
3. **The pledger `+N` badge** was wrong (`b8e8a2a2` — it subtracted `AVATAR_ROW_LIMIT_DESKTOP` (8) while `getFeaturedProfiles()` caps at `MAX_FEATURED_PROFILES` (6), so the desktop limit is unreachable and the count was permanently short by 2) *and* unreadable (`14202b1d` — it painted under the last avatar, reading "685" not "+685").

**Decision:** Fix all three on the P987 branch rather than defer, each with a regression test whose failure path was exercised first. Derive counts from what is **drawn**, not from a limit. Make scroll triggers **viewport-relative** (`threshold: 0` + negative `rootMargin`), never a ratio of an element that may exceed the viewport.

**The unifying root cause:** bugs 1 and 2 are *viewport-conditional by construction* — each hinges on a comparison between an element's size and the viewport's, and each resolves correctly when the viewport is large. Desktop is not a weaker test of these; it is a test that **cannot fail**. `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md` already mandates 375/320/desktop — the rule was right and the shipping sessions did not follow it.

**Consequences:** Any `threshold` > 0 on an element whose rendered width can exceed a phone viewport is suspect — grep for `threshold:` when auditing. Any single `minHeight`/`maxHeight` serving a third-party embed across breakpoints is suspect, because embeds reflow. The `/intro` fix is verified **by rendering only**: the embed is cross-origin, so whether the slots that appear *after* picking a date fit inside 1000px is **unverified** and needs one real booking on a real phone.

**Falsifier:** A real phone booking fails or the slots clip → 1000px is still too short and the height must be measured against the embed's post-selection layout, not its month grid.

**References:** [social-proof.tsx](../src/app/components/landing/social-proof.tsx), [template-stamp.tsx](../src/app/components/agreements/template-stamp.tsx), [intro-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/intro-page.tsx), `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md`

## 2026-07-15 [process]: a visual-QA capture that skips the reveals photographs a blank page — the method nearly discredited a QA run that was finding real bugs

**Context:** The first visual-QA round returned two CRITICALs: "`/intro` renders no calendar at desktop" and "~70% of home and founder page bodies render empty". **Both were artifacts of the capture, not the page.** The screenshot script jumped straight to `window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)` — a single hop that never intersects the middle sections, so their framer-motion `whileInView`/`once: true` reveals never fired and they photographed at `opacity: 0`. The tell was in the report itself: the FAQ and references *did* render, because the one hop landed them in view. Separately, `fullPage` capture blanks cross-origin iframes, which is why `/intro` looked empty at desktop while rendering perfectly in a viewport capture. Cost: a full re-capture, and a near-dismissal of a run that had *also* surfaced three real bugs.

**Decision:** A visual-QA capture is not evidence unless (a) the page was scrolled **stepwise** (~250–350px steps) so every `IntersectionObserver` reveal fires, (b) zero low-opacity content is confirmed **programmatically** before the shot (`[...document.querySelectorAll('section *')].filter(e => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(e).opacity) < 0.9 && e.innerText.trim())` must be empty), and (c) any page embedding a cross-origin iframe is captured **per-viewport**, never `fullPage`. Capture mobile at DPR 1 — DPR 2 on a tall page overshoots the stitch and silently repeats content, which is how the FAQ/references/footer went uncaptured at both mobile widths while the report read as complete.

**Alternatives rejected:** Trusting the agent's "probably a reveal artifact" instinct — it explicitly refused to, and was right to: *"Either the pages are broken or the evidence is."* An agent that downgrades findings because the evidence *might* be bad is useless; the fix belongs in the capture, not the reviewer's confidence.

**Consequences:** The blind-subagent rule in `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md` works and should not be softened — the agent's honest refusal to sign off is what forced the re-capture that found the real bugs. **Proposed:** `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md` should carry the stepwise-scroll + opacity-check + no-fullPage-for-iframes preconditions; that edit is **blocked pending `/slava:maintain:claude-md`** per `.claude/rules/rules.md` and is not made here. Second, unrelated friction worth naming: **four of five background subagents did not deliver their reports at all** until told explicitly to call `SendMessage` with `to: "main"` — prompts saying "report your findings" are satisfied by writing text the spawner cannot see. Background-agent prompts must name the delivery mechanism.

**Falsifier:** A stepwise-scrolled, opacity-verified capture still photographs a section blank → the cause is not reveal timing and the blank is real.

**References:** `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md`, [features/uat/p987.md](../features/done/2026-06-10/uat/p987.md)

## 2026-07-15 [product]: `/program` (the €950 co-founder offer) is parked — unlisted and unlinked by design, not broken

**Context:** P987 pulled `/program` (`OffersPage`) out of the top nav and footer and added `noindex`, keeping the route reachable by direct URL with the price intact ("unlisted, not stripped"). The net effect is that no new visitor can reach the €950 offer: nothing links to it, not even `/founder`, the page that now carries the co-founder audience. A code review of the branch flagged this as a suspected accident — "two separately-sensible changes combining into full invisibility" — which is the point of this entry: it was **one deliberate decision**, specified and executed, and it still read as a bug to a fresh reader. Feature specs get archived to `features/done/`; the alarm would keep re-firing.

**Decision:** Keep it parked. The co-founder offer is dormant Posture-1 (2026-07-01 pivot) while the key-hire wedge is tested. Unlisted-but-reachable is the deliberate middle: the offer stays sellable to anyone the founder sends the link to directly (the only channel it has today), stays out of the front door that now argues a different wedge, and stays out of the index so it cannot compete with `/` for the same searcher. Deleting it would destroy a revivable fallback; re-linking it would put a co-founder program in the nav of a key-hire page.

**Alternatives rejected:** Link it from `/founder` (superficially tidy — `/founder` is the co-founder audience — but it re-opens a paid funnel that is deliberately dormant, and `/founder` exists to preserve the page, not to sell the program). Restore the nav link + drop `noindex` (puts the dormant offer back in front of the key-hire audience). Leave it unrecorded (what produced the false alarm).

**Consequences:** The €950 offer is invisible to organic traffic and reachable only via a link the founder sends. If it ever needs to sell itself again, both halves must be undone together — the nav link AND the `noindex` — since either alone leaves it effectively invisible. `UAT-10` in `e2e/p987-verify.spec.ts` pins the parked state (no nav link + reachable + noindex + price kept); it is the executable record of this decision and should fail loudly if someone "fixes" one half.

**Falsifier:** A co-founder pair asks for the program via a channel other than a direct link from the founder → the offer is being sought organically and the parking is costing real revenue, not just hypothetical revenue.

**References:** `features/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md` (Solution #3, Done-When, Non-Goals "do NOT delete OffersPage"), [offers-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/offers-page.tsx)

## 2026-07-15 [product]: the five moves drop "Prevent common pitfalls" — the key-hire front door leads with alignment, not with conflict

**Context:** P987's copy refresh changed the `HowPlatformWorks` five moves (shared by `/` and `/coach`) without recording why. Three edits rode in on one commit: "Align expectations" → "Secure mutual commitment" (and "in your partnership" → "with the people you work with"), a new "Surface what needs clarity" move, and the **deletion of "Prevent common pitfalls" — "Guard against memory failures and gaslighting."** The deletion was the one nobody decided; it surfaced only when the founder said the moves didn't match what was discussed and asked to see the diff. The moves are a conceptual argument ported from the `/presi` deck, not a feature list, so dropping one drops a claim about what the product does.

**Decision:** Keep the drop, deliberately. "Gaslighting" names an adversarial frame — it presumes bad faith by someone in the relationship. That fits the co-founder-split origin story, where the reader has already been through a fight, but it misreads the key-hire buyer, who does not believe anything is wrong yet (the whole wedge is that misalignment is *invisible and mutual*, not that someone is lying). Leading a cold key-hire visitor with gaslighting-protection answers a question they have not asked and frames their hire as an adversary. The remaining four keep the argument intact. Also confirmed: "Secure mutual commitment" over the original "Align expectations", because the page now spends "align" on the whole promise (alignment audit, "how you align with your team") — reusing it for one of five moves would make that move read as the entire product.

**Alternatives rejected:** Restore as a sixth move (adds a conflict frame to a page whose thesis is that no conflict is visible yet). Restore and drop "Surface what needs clarity" (the agent-flagging move is the only one naming the actual mechanism). Restore with softer wording (the frame, not the word, is the mismatch — rewording keeps the misfit).

**Consequences:** `/coach` shares this component and inherits the drop — coaches lose the gaslighting-protection claim too, which is untested for that audience. The memory-failure/gaslighting capability still exists in the product; it is no longer claimed on the front door. If the key-hire wedge is later abandoned, revisit — this drop is downstream of the wedge, not of the product.

**Falsifier:** Audit conversations surface memory-failure/gaslighting as a top-two stated pain for key-hire buyers → the move was load-bearing and should return.

## 2026-07-15 [technical]: the React 19 / helmet workaround covered `<meta>` but missed `<link>` — every page canonicalised to the site root for ~3 months

**Context:** The 2026-04-12 entry below ("React 19 strips `<meta>` from react-helmet-async") rewrote `seo.tsx` to set `<meta>` imperatively via `useEffect`, and recorded that "Helmet is kept only for `<title>` and `<script type=ld+json>`". That enumeration was wrong by omission: `<link rel="canonical">` was also inside `<Helmet>`. That same fix also "removed duplicate static OG tags from `index.html`" — but left the static `<link rel="canonical" href="https://claritypledge.com/">` there. The two halves combined into a silent site-wide bug: **every route carried TWO competing canonicals** — the static root tag plus the route's own — and crawlers discard both, so `/coach`, `/manifesto`, `/pledgers`, `/about` could not rank independently. Found while shipping `/founder` (P987).

**Mechanism (measured, not inferred — probe: React 19.2.1 + react-helmet-async 2.0.5, jsdom; a first version of this entry asserted the opposite from inference and a code review caught it):** React 19 hoists `<link>` to `<head>` **itself**. A `<link rel="canonical">` inside `<Helmet>` therefore **does** reach the DOM — the failure is not that it vanishes, it is that **React, not Helmet, owns it**, so Helmet never dedupes or replaces it and it is appended *alongside* the static tag. This differs from `<meta property>`, where the symptom is a tag that never updates. Same root (React 19 owns hoisted metadata, Helmet loses control of it), opposite surface symptom: meta silently doesn't change, link silently duplicates. Do not reason from the meta symptom to the link symptom — that inference is exactly what produced the wrong first draft of this entry.

**Decision:** Move canonical onto the same imperative path as the meta tags (`setCanonical()` in `seo.tsx`'s existing `useEffect`), update the existing tag in place rather than appending (two canonicals are worse than one wrong one — crawlers discard both), and reset to the site root on unmount so a route without its own `<SEO>` degrades to the root rather than inheriting the previous route's URL. Removed the dead `<link rel="canonical">` from `<Helmet>` with a comment saying why it must not come back.

**Alternatives rejected:** Filing a separate spec and deferring (the founder pushed back and was right — the fix follows a pattern already proven in the same file, and the prior state was maximally broken, so the change could only improve it). Deleting the static `index.html` canonical (it is the correct pre-hydration default for crawlers).

**Consequences:** The general lesson is about **partial fixes to a class of bug.** The 2026-04-12 fix was correct and incomplete, and its own decision entry recorded the incomplete enumeration as if it were exhaustive — so the gap was invisible to anyone reading the log. When a root cause is "the framework hoists element type X out of this library", the fix must enumerate *every* element type the library renders, not the ones the current bug report mentions. It failed silently because the broken code reads as correct: `<link rel="canonical" href={fullUrl} />` looks right. The tell was available all along — `og:url` was correct (imperative path) while `canonical` was wrong (Helmet path) on the same page. A canary now covers it, and its failure path was exercised (3/3 fail with canonical restored to Helmet). Fixed in `85ba952f`.

**References:** [seo.tsx](../src/app/components/seo.tsx), [seo-canonical.test.tsx](../src/tests/seo-canonical.test.tsx), 2026-04-12 entry below

## 2026-07-15 [product]: the co-founder offer was still being sold with no reachable page — `/founder` promoted out of the DEV-only `/tree` snapshot

**Context:** P987 reframed `/` from the co-founder pitch to the key-hire wedge and snapshotted the old page to `/tree/old-landing-2`, which is `import.meta.env.DEV`-gated. That was correct as revival insurance and wrong as a resting state: the co-founder offer is **still live**, so the snapshot left a sellable offer with no page anywhere in production.

**Decision:** Promote the snapshot to a real `/founder` route with a "For co-founders" nav entry alongside `/coach`. The site now has **three** public audience landings with three different offers: `/` (alignment audit), `/coach` (Clarity Letter), `/founder` (co-founder program, behind the webinar funnel). Fixed its inherited `url="/"` → `url="/founder"`.

**Alternatives rejected:** Deferring to a separate spec — the assistant recommended this on blast-radius grounds and was **overruled correctly**. The recommendation rested on an unverified claim ("a 539-line dev snapshot nobody reviewed for prod") that a file read refuted: it is verbatim the page that was live at `/` until P987, i.e. the most battle-tested page in the repo. Stripping the webinar CTA from `/founder` — rejected: `old-landing-2`'s `WebinarCta` is now the *only* place that funnel's code lives, since P987 deleted it from `/`, and it is live correct behaviour for that audience.

**Consequences:** The webinar funnel (P937/P951) is **parked, not deleted** — it runs on `/founder` and nowhere else. When webinars resume, `/founder` is the reference implementation to copy back. "Snapshot to `/tree` for revival" is the right move for a *retired* offer and the wrong one for a *dormant-but-still-sold* offer; the discriminator is whether anyone can still buy it. Shipped in `92488331`.

**References:** [p987 spec](../features/done/2026-06-10/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md), [App.tsx](../src/App.tsx)

## 2026-07-15 [technical]: a two-way toggle cannot express three audiences — it strands whichever page it sits on

**Context:** P916 built the audience switcher as a toggle: `onCoachPage ? "For founders"→"/" : "For coaches"→"/coach"`. Correct for two landings. P987 added a third (`/founder`), and the toggle silently stranded it — on `/founder` it rendered "For coaches" and offered **no way back to `/`** at all except the logo. Two more symptoms shared the cause: the list was duplicated across three surfaces (desktop header, desktop dropdown, mobile menu), so a guard added to one drifted from the others (the mobile menu self-linked "For co-founders" *on* `/founder`), and the desktop dropdown had never carried audience links at all — on any surface where the header collapses to the hamburger, `/coach` was unreachable.

**Decision:** One exported `AUDIENCE_LINKS` list in `nav-links.ts`, read by all three surfaces, each filtering out its own pathname — "show the audiences you are NOT on". The self-link filter replaces the toggle. It lives in `nav-links.ts` rather than a component file because exporting a constant from a component breaks fast refresh (`react-refresh/only-export-components`).

**Alternatives rejected:** A three-way conditional (same class of bug at four audiences). Guarding each surface separately (that *is* the drift).

**Consequences:** Same shape as the nav-CTA fix in the same commit: `LoggedOutPrimaryCta`'s docstring promised "every public page mirrors the main landing's action", which stopped being well-defined the moment there were three landings — it now mirrors *the page you are on*. **The general rule: an N-way UI switcher written as a boolean toggle is a latent bug that fires when N grows, and a list duplicated per surface will drift — not might.** Neither symptom was caught by tests; both were caught by rendering the three pages and reading the links. Shipped in `11735261`.

**References:** [nav-links.ts](../src/app/components/layout/nav-links.ts), [navigation-menu-items.tsx](../src/app/components/layout/navigation-menu-items.tsx), [simple-navigation.tsx](../src/app/components/layout/simple-navigation.tsx)

## 2026-07-15 [product]: a CTA's promise must survive the click — the copy explaining the audit lived only in a meta tag

**Context:** `/` promised "Book your free alignment audit" and broke that promise twice. (1) `/intro`, the CTA's destination, was a bare Google Calendar iframe with **no copy at all** — the word "audit" appeared nowhere, so the promise died at the moment of highest intent. (2) The hero microcopy read "A live 1:1 session. Free. Starts with a 15-minute call." — naming neither what the audit *is* nor that the 15 minutes is a qualifying gate. The copy that did both already existed and was live *only in the SEO `description` meta tag*: no human had ever read it. The page's own FAQ #1 answers "What are you actually selling me?" with "A paid engagement, eventually. That's the honest answer" — so the hero was the least honest surface on a page selling honesty.

**Decision:** Pull the meta-tag substance onto the page; name the audit on `/intro`; hoist the microcopy to one `AUDIT_MICROCOPY` constant and render it under **every** CTA including the bottom one, since it carries the 15-minute disclosure and a visitor converting at the foot of the page was getting the button without it. Keep "Book" in the CTA (a verb, not a label) and "free" in the CTA only — repeating it in the sentence below is redundant.

**Alternatives rejected:** Changing the CTA to "Book a 15-min intro" — honest about the click but sells nothing; nobody wants an intro call, they want the audit, and it puts funnel mechanics on the button. Stating the gate ("to see if it's worth both our time") — recommended by the assistant, **declined by the founder**; the gate is therefore still unstated on `/` and FAQ #1 carries the transparency alone.

**Consequences:** Two checks worth keeping: **(a) does the destination repeat the promise the button made?** — a scent break at the click is invisible to every test we run; **(b) is the best copy on the page actually on the page?** — SEO metadata is a plausible hiding place for the clearest sentence a team has written. One residual is not code-fixable: the Google Calendar appointment schedule is named "15-min Intro Call" in Google Calendar config, so the widget still says "Intro Call" under a heading that says "audit". Shipped in `92488331` + `11735261`.

**References:** [program-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/program-page.tsx), [intro-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/intro-page.tsx)

## 2026-07-15 [product]: front-door wedge word "de-risk" → "keep"; the free audit is free-by-application (no price anchor)

**Context:** P987 shipped the hero as *"De-risk misalignment with your next key hire."* Two problems surfaced while reviewing it. (1) **Grammar the founder's ear caught first:** "de-risk" takes an *asset* as its object, not a hazard — you de-risk a hire, not a misalignment; "de-risk misalignment" is de-risking the risk. (2) **Provenance:** `hypotheses.md:75` sources the key-hire trigger phrase *"de-risk this hire"* to an interview analysis, but the underlying interview transcript (in `.private/`) contains **zero** instances of "de-risk" from the interviewee — the risk frame is introduced by the interviewer and **deflected twice** by the founder interviewee ("not a big risk for me personally" / "the risk is smaller there"). That is precisely the failure `H-GenerativeFraming` already logged in April: *"de-risk (defensive, invites 'we're fine')"*, and the 2026-03-23 frame-resistance risk (*"buying a de-risking package = admitting we might break"*). The founder then settled provenance directly: **"de-risk is definitely coming from me"** — it is our word, not a customer's.

**Decision:** (1) Hero → **"Keep the hire you can't afford to lose."** The interviewee's own unprompted verb for key staff was *keep*. (2) `next` → `this` throughout: a *planned* hire is `hypotheses.md:75`'s documented **disqualifying** state (*"a dream, not a dyad, so the reveal had nothing to bite on"*) — the prior hero pointed at the state the evidence says does not convert. (3) The free audit is **free, by application** — no price anchor.

**Alternatives rejected:** *"Prevent misalignment"* — grammatical but over-promises (the product surfaces, it does not prevent). *"Avoid compounding misalignment"* — "avoid" is defensive, the same "we're fine" invitation that sank "de-risk"; the word *compounding* was salvaged into the stakes bridge sentence instead. **Plural** ("the key hires you can't afford to lose") — turns one live dyad into a retention programme, the systemic framing the state layer says does not convert. *"Retain" / "increase retention"* — dashboard language; a rate, not a person. **"€250 value, free"** — a price that exists nowhere (the canvas prices a live 1:1 diagnostic at ~$99), and value-anchoring a freebie is webinar register aimed at a buyer whose entire objection is *"what's the catch"*; it also undercuts the FAQ's disarming-honesty strategy — trust is the product, and a fake anchor spends it. **€250 as an actual price** — contradicts the same-day two-step model (free audit → challenge letter carrying the offer → separate closing call). A prior session reached "free, by application" independently.

**Consequences:** Shipped in `6c5e12b0`. `lean-canvas.md:77` still prices the live 1:1 diagnostic at ~$99 while the founder said "99 we can delete" — a live strategy-doc contradiction, hand off to `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update`. `hypotheses.md:75` cites a transcript filename that does not exist (the real file is under a different name in `.private/`) — needs fixing. **Evidence status: UNTESTED, and weaker than it looks** — the assistant misattributed one supporting quote to the interviewee (it was the founder's); the attribution of the *"keen on keeping them"* quote was asked twice and never confirmed, so the shipped headline rests on a quote of unverified provenance. This is a better bet than "de-risk", not a proven one. **Falsifier:** if founders with a live key hire pull no harder on "keep" than on "de-risk", the wedge word is not the constraint and the state layer is.

**References:** features/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-FounderWince (2026-07-10 state-layer), H-GenerativeFraming · [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §UVP · decisions.md 2026-07-14 [product] (key-hire §UVP page-lead)

## 2026-07-15 [product]: the `/align` capability is advertised on `/` before it is wired — a founder-owned unfreeze of the 2026-07-14 build freeze

**Context:** The founder asked to replace the "Prevent common pitfalls" move on `/` with *"AI identifies misalignment risks"* — i.e. `/align` surfacing high-stakes matters that deserve shared clarity. The skill exists and is hardened; the bridge to call it is unbuilt. The build freeze logged 24 hours earlier (*"freeze further alignment-tooling build — no customer pulls it yet"*) names its own unfreeze trigger: **customer-pulled, triggered by the first real audit** — and `decisions.md` 2026-07-14 states the freeze *"guards the founder's known scope-expansion-under-uncertainty pattern."*

**Decision:** Advertise it. The founder's frame — recorded because it is the load-bearing reasoning and it is **not** the assistant's: *"we don't need to build it — we advertise what the value is and check if people want it; if they do we build the missing thing… it doesn't commit me to building it, it's part of validation."* The founder owns the build and overruled the hold. Logged here at the assistant's request so the freeze does not read as silently violated to whoever reads the log next.

**Alternatives rejected:** The assistant's hold, twice. First on freeze grounds — advertising a capability commits you to it, which pulls the build forward, which is what the freeze exists to stop. Then, after conceding the validation argument (domain context the assistant lacked), on **attribution** grounds: a fake door needs a *door* — a click, a waitlist, a distinct CTA — something that produces a countable signal. The page has one CTA, so a booking cannot be attributed to this step; it is a claim with no read-out, and the freeze's own designated trigger (a founder asking for it unprompted in a real audit) is a strictly stronger signal. **This objection was overruled, not refuted** — recorded because it predicts what will fail.

**Consequences:** **Not implemented** — `how-platform-works.tsx` is untouched and is genuinely shared by `/`, `/coach`, and `/tree/old-landing-2`, so this change has cross-page blast radius. The two companion changes in the same batch are also unbuilt: rename "Align expectations" → "Secure mutual commitment" (the body copy already says *"Commit to a minimum principle"*, and "alignment" is being promoted to the product-level word, so using it as one of five moves dilutes it), and delete "Prevent common pitfalls" (its body accuses the hire of gaslighting, on a page whose thesis is that both people mean well). **Evidence status: UNTESTED and, per the unrefuted objection, unfalsifiable as specified** — one CTA means no attributable signal. **Falsifier:** none available until the step gets its own door.

**References:** features/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md · decisions.md 2026-07-14 [product] (build freeze; `/align` scope; "use ≠ build") · [align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md)

## 2026-07-15 [technical]: `/coach` never consumed the shared `HardTruthChat` — a false docstring propagated into a spec non-goal and an architecture decision

**Context:** `hard-truth-chat.tsx`'s docstring claimed it was *"Used on `/` … and `/coach`"*. P987 turned that into a hard non-goal — *"Do NOT edit the shared HardTruthChat component — props only (protect `/coach`)"* — and a Done-When line certifying *"`/coach` chat unchanged (verified — no props passed by coach-partnership-page)"*. The assistant then designed two successive architectures around the constraint (first "prop-only", then additive props "so `/coach` renders byte-identically").

**Decision:** Restructure the shared component freely behind a `variant` prop defaulting to existing behaviour. Verified by grep + file read: `coach-partnership-page.tsx` defines its **own local** `function HardTruthChat()` and never imports the shared one. The only real consumer needing preservation is `/tree/old-landing-2`, which passes no `variant` and is therefore unaffected by the default.

**Alternatives rejected:** The props-only constraint itself — it protected nothing. The Done-When line was verified-true in the way "the door is locked" is true about a wall: no props are passed by `/coach` because `/coach` is not a caller.

**Consequences:** Four artifacts were built on a fiction — the docstring, the spec non-goal, a Done-When line, and two rounds of the assistant's own design. **The propagation path is the lesson: a stale docstring became a spec constraint became an architecture decision, and nothing in the pipeline re-checked the original claim.** Docstrings asserting cross-page consumers are load-bearing and should be grepped, not trusted. Fixed in `6c5e12b0`. The same class recurred twice more the same day, which is what makes it a pattern rather than a slip: once on a *statistic* taken from a secondary source without reading the cited original, and once on this log itself — the 2026-07-15 [technical] canonical entry above asserted a React 19 mechanism reasoned from a sibling symptom, and a code review's probe refuted it. Common root: asserting from a proxy (docstring, secondary source, analogous symptom) instead of the artifact.

**References:** `src/app/components/landing/hard-truth-chat.tsx` · `src/app/pages/coach-partnership-page.tsx` · features/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md

## 2026-07-15 [product]: the cp landing's job is a cold-outreach credibility surface, not an inbound funnel; Gallup 200% clears the calculator's stat blocker

**Context:** A prior session had blocked the risk-calculator idea with *"we have run zero audits — building a polished funnel widget to optimize a conversion step we've never observed is optimizing blind."* The founder corrected the premise: **five audits have been run** (none with the key-hire segment — that is why they read as "wrong audience", not "no data"), and named the page's actual job: *"to reach them we improve the landing so when we reach out in cold to them they have something to see before they respond to us."*

**Decision:** (1) The landing is a **credibility surface for outbound**, not an inbound conversion funnel. This changes the calculator's justification: it is not optimizing an unobserved conversion step, it is giving a cold prospect something to *do* that makes the stakes theirs. (2) The replacement-cost stat is **Gallup's role-specific figure — ~200% of salary for leaders and managers** — not the generic one-half-to-two-times range, because a key hire *is* a leader; it is the source's own words for our exact population. Placed as the second beat in `#stakes` after the Leadership IQ 46%, bridged by **"Small gaps compound."** — the bridge the spec mandated in two places and had built in zero.

**Alternatives rejected:** **200% in the hero** (founder's instinct) — the H1 already carries the stakes qualitatively ("the hire you can't afford to lose"); the number is the same claim with arithmetic, so in the hero it is redundant while pushing the CTA down, and the scroll cue already promises the stakes are next ("Why it matters") — putting them above it makes the cue lie. **Leading with 200% before 46%** — 46% attacks *"my hire is fine"* (the deflection the interviewee gave verbatim, and the objection an independent FAQ pass ranked most dangerous); 200% attacks *"so what"*. Lead with cost alone and the "we're fine" founder reads it and thinks *"sure, but they're not leaving"* — the cost only bites once the probability lands. **Adding ref [8] without a body citation** — would have shipped an orphaned reference in the same commit that fixes one.

**Consequences:** Resolves the **`[STAT PENDING — 2x annual salary]`** hard precondition that was blocking the calculator spec. The calculator remains a **separate spec, not filed**; the founder's stated shape is calculator-on-the-landing (not gated behind the CTA) with the CTA staying a 15-minute call — which reads as the lead-magnet side of the warm-primer-vs-lead-magnet fork, but was never confirmed as an answer to it. **Evidence status:** the 200% is evidence-backed (source verified in-session); the cold-outreach-surface claim is UNTESTED. **Falsifier:** cold prospects who visit the page before replying convert no better than those who do not.

**References:** [Gallup — This Fixable Problem Costs U.S. Businesses $1 Trillion](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/247391/fixable-problem-costs-businesses-trillion.aspx) · features/p987_cp_front_door_realignment.md · [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) H-FounderWince

## 2026-07-14 [product]: active market focus moves solo-AI-builder → seed–A founder with an active key hire; §UVP page-lead promotes the key-hire wedge over the mission slogan

**Context:** The 2026-07-01 market-focus shift chose "solo founders / solo AI builders" on a *reachability* argument (single-person funnel, no two-sided coordination). H-FounderWince's own evidence then evolved past it: the 2026-07-10 state-layer refinement (n=5, Founder-J) found the ICP-5 filter is necessary-not-sufficient and that buying needs a **live dyad** — sharpest trigger an **active key hire** — reached via **champion/referrer**, explicitly not a single-person funnel. P987 (2026-07-14, post-challenge) then built the cp front door to lead with exactly that wedge ("De-risk misalignment with your next key hire"). The market-focus header and the §UVP page-lead had not caught up: the header still said "solo builder / single-person funnel," and the §UVP lead was the 2026-07-13 mission slogan.

**Decision:** (1) **Active market focus** (lean-canvas §Customer Segments, `SINGLE-VALUE: active-market-focus`) moves to **seed–A founder with an active key hire** — unit = the founder + the person they're betting on; reach = champion/referrer. (3) H-FounderWince keeps its ID; only its one-line summary + section header are sharpened to surface the key-hire trigger.

**Alternatives rejected:** keep "solo builder" as the focus and treat key-hire as only an entry trigger (leaves the canvas contradicting the homepage P987 just shipped); broaden to "any live high-stakes dyad" (dilutes the sharp key-hire copy P987 locked); rename H-FounderWince → H-KeyHireWince (churns cross-doc refs; the bet is unchanged, only its sharpest trigger); delete the solo-builder framing outright (it's a revivable fallback under the reversal-lock/bloat gates).

**Consequences:** Supersedes the "mission hero on /" consequence of the 2026-07-13 [product] "cp untouched" entry (the hero is now the key-hire line, not the mission slogan). goals.md §Active + its H-FounderWince pointer name "solo AI builders" — needs a matching direct edit (goals.md is outside the docs-strategy-update charter). definitions.md "Founder (ICP)" is untouched — it defines the acquisition *unit* (individual vs pair) and correctly defers *which focus* to the strategy docs; the champion/referrer reach is a channel, not a change to the unit. **Falsifier:** if founders who fail the state layer (no live key-hire dyad) pull just as hard as those who pass, the key-hire narrowing doesn't filter → revert to the dormant solo-builder focus (H-FounderWince 2026-07-10 falsifier).

## 2026-07-14 [process]: story/point model gets a dedicated home (`docs/story-point-model.md`) — glossary can't hold an untested model, and every consumer needs the full one

**Context:** Fixing the story/point definitions so `/align` reads *one* correct source exposed that the model was smeared across 5 homes that had drifted (`definitions.md` §"Stories vs Points", `sifter-definitions.md`, `sifter-point.md`, `sifter-story.md`, hardcoded refs in `align.md`), and the *best* synthesis (two orthogonal axes + edge-case reasoning) lived in none of them. The obvious move — enrich `definitions.md` — collided with two facts: (1) `definitions.md` is a **strict glossary** (`docs-strategy-update` Gate 1 forbids status/untested content), and (2) `decisions.md` 2026-07-13 [product] already parked the two-axis model with an explicit *"migrate to definitions.md only after the backtest."* Meanwhile every **consumer** of the concept (`/align`, the sifters) needs the *full* model — definition **+** edge cases **+** the reasoning that fixes the boundaries — to function; a glossary entry stripped of that is useless to them.

**Decision:** Create a **dedicated full-model doc** — `docs/story-point-model.md` — as the single home for the story/point/position model: the stable definitional frame, the two axes, point types (mechanism/stance), all edge cases *with their reasoning*, and the operational scoring mechanism labeled **current-best / UNTESTED**. Everything else **points** at it: `definitions.md` keeps a crisp plain-meaning entry for Story/Point + a pointer; `sifter-definitions.md` / `sifter-point.md` / `sifter-story.md` / `align.md` drop their inline definitions → pointer (their *process* sections stay); `CHARTER.md` gets a routing line (a dedicated concept-model doc, home for the story/point model). This **does not reverse** the 2026-07-13 "wait for the backtest" note — that note protected the *glossary* from an unproven model; a dedicated doc *can* carry the UNTESTED label, so the honesty the note guarded is preserved, and the model no longer masquerades as settled fact.

**Root cause of the scatter (the second half of this entry):** the concept **evolved faster than the doc**, AND the maintainer skills have a **skill-tree blind spot** — `/kdd` and `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` scope their dedup/consolidation to `docs/` and **never scan `.claude/commands/**`**, which is exactly where the competing definitions accumulated (three sifter files + `align.md`). Enforcement (extend the maintainers to scan skill files for inline concept redefinitions) is deferred to the repo-wide spec, not built here.

**Tentative (UNTESTED, not enshrined as definitional):** *context-depth* as a third axis (comprehension cost ≈ dependency-neighbourhood / graph in-degree) — flagged because it may reduce to "predicted comprehension gap," which the 0–10 already measures. *Arbiter* has **two distinct senses** kept separate: (a) *shared-arbiter availability* = the epistemic sense that grounds point-ness/falsifiability (who or what can adjudicate the claim); (b) *letter-routing arbiter* = the product-topology sense (Slava as initial recipient, later real stakeholders) — **not** a story/point axis. Do not fold (b) into the model.

**Alternatives rejected:** force the full model into `definitions.md` (breaks Gate 1; reverses a same-day decision on reasoning alone; makes the glossary dishonest); leave everything in `decisions.md` with only pointers (makes the append-only *log* the concept SSOT — backwards from CHARTER rule 2); the A-split — stable frame → glossary, untested mechanism → log (optimizes doc purity but forces every consumer to stitch two files and to *know* to).

**Consequences:** 5 definitional homes → 1 + pointers. `/align` (Phase 3) points its form-contract at the new file. The 2026-07-13 [product] working-model entry stands as the dated origin; the new file is the maintained current model and references it. **Falsifier:** if a consumer skill still needs to read a *second* doc to apply story/point correctly (the new file is missing a boundary it relies on), the "one full home" claim failed — the file is under-scoped, re-widen it.

**References:** `docs/story-point-model.md` (new) · [definitions.md](definitions.md) §Story, §"Stories vs Points" · [CHARTER.md](CHARTER.md) · decisions.md 2026-07-13 [product] "point/story working model" · `.claude/commands/slava/content/sifter-{definitions,point,story}.md` · [align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md) · plan `~/.claude/plans/serene-jumping-blossom.md`

## 2026-07-13 [process]: A skill's gate REPORT can self-attest even when its sub-gates are script-backed — fold every agent-run gate into the aggregator

**Context:** First target of a signal-first skill-improvement pass (repair-ranked from git log + KDDs). `/ship` was the hottest (4 repairs). Its gate report (`✓ all gates passed`) was **agent-composed**: it mixed mechanical results from `ship-gates.sh` (gates 2.5/2.7) with two gates the agent ran by hand — 3.5 pre-deploy checklist and 3.65 deferrals. An agent under context pressure could print the `✓` summary having skipped an agent-run gate. This is the scriptify meta-lesson (2026-07-01 [process], line 468: "a skill's safety gate should be a grep/exit-code the agent runs, never a checkbox it ticks") applied one level up — at the **report** layer, not the individual gate.

**Decision:** Fold the two agent-run gates into `ship-gates.sh` so the whole gate report is the script's **verbatim stdout** with one exit code; `/ship` relays it and never re-types `✓` lines. Two nuances the work surfaced:
- **Gate 3.5 (pre-deploy checklist):** mechanizes cleanly as hard-FAIL on any unticked markdown task-list item (`[-*+] [ ]`) under a `pre-?deploy checklist` heading, tracking section depth so sub-headings don't end it. The ticked box IS the auditable acknowledgement, replacing a self-attestable verbal y/n.
- **Gate 3.65 (deferrals):** does NOT mechanize as a hard gate — natural-language deferral-detection has irreducible false positives (e.g. "out of scope for older browsers"), and the old commit-log credit was inert on the branch path (the feature's own pN credited every deferral). Downgraded to **WARN**: always runs, always in the report, human judges. A gate that can't be mechanically decided should surface, not block.

**Verification discipline:** every gate FAIL path was exercised end-to-end (non-zero exit pasted) before commit — epistemic gate 7. An adversarial reviewer on the diff found **3 shippable false-negatives in the first fix** (sub-heading reset the section scan, only `-` bullets detected, heading-variant misses) — all closed and re-tested. Gate-logic changes without a red-team would have regressed silently.

**Alternatives rejected:** hard-FAIL for 3.65 too (blocks legit merges on innocent prose); leave both gates agent-run (the self-attest hole); rewrite all ~120 skills (signal-first says fix only repair-ranked, gate-bearing skills).

**Consequences:** Reusable lens for the rest of the pass — "is any gate the agent self-reports rather than a script emitting?" is the single thing a recurring `/weekly` audit should hunt across gate-bearing skills (`/day`, publish-run, canaries). Not every check survives mechanization; the WARN-vs-FAIL split is the discriminator. `/day` is the next repair-ranked target (2 format-assumption self-heals) — not yet audited.

**References:** [ship-gates.sh](../scripts/ship-gates.sh) · [ship.md](../.claude/commands/slava/build/ship.md) · commit `915919cb` · scriptify precedent (2026-07-01 [process])

## 2026-07-13 [process]: /align brought to minimum-executable bar — built live via its own feedback loop

**Context:** `/align` could not be run *for real* — an earlier "run" was hallucinated (hand-written output shaped like an alignment unit, no real point-identification, no user turns). Per the plan (`~/.claude/plans/once-i-guess-we-misty-quiche.md`), we brought it to a "runnable for real" bar, then ran it on a real high-stakes point mined from `claude-conversations`, improving the skill each turn from what the run exposed (7 commits, v1.0.0 → v1.7.0 on `align.md`).

**Decision (what the minimum-executable `/align` now is):**
- **Anti-hallucination rests on two unforgeable anchors, not on the skill claiming a sub-process ran.** (1) *Detection anchor:* every candidate cites a **verbatim `evidence` quote + source** — no citable quote ⟹ it's an invention, drop it (caught a real case where a distilled `content` welded on words the user never said). (2) *Loop anchor:* the position cannot emit until the user answers open questions AND types the 0–10 rating on **separate transcript turns** — a single model cannot forge a real user turn.
- **Stage 1 detection = classified, quantified cards.** Fields: `type` (decision/assumption/hypothesis/problem-statement/reasoning) · `stake` · `content` · `source` (readable relative date + corpus) · `evidence` (verbatim) · `reasoning` (plain prose).
- **Stakes are a magnitude in time AND money, not 0–100 points.** Time lost = money lost — convert via the user's worth, state the assumption if unknown. (Superseded the four-factor 0–100 score built one turn earlier; factors demoted to sizing lenses.)
- **Loop order is load-bearing:** detect → **user confirms/corrects the quantified stake (1→2 gate, agent halts)** → enrich (harvest already-answered material from the corpus, user's own quoted words) → open questions (residual gaps only, *after* enrichment) → user rating (min).
- **Contradictions/confusion** raise the stake estimate AND become enrichment open questions — never a detection-blocker.

**Alternatives rejected:** reusing `sifter-story`'s point-seeded (generative-persuasive) mode for recovery — it manufactures a justification for the point, the exact rubber-stamp `/align` blocks; baking in the untested orthogonal-degrees (point-ness/story-ness) model — ran against shipped definitions instead; treating "invoked the sifter, not hand-written" as a realness criterion — unverifiable, dropped.

**Consequences:** `/align` is now runnable for real (a run only counts with user-confirmed point + stake, user-answered questions, user-typed rating). Deferred and NOT built: the decomposer (story-ness/point-ness axes — explicitly NOT required for open questions), the blind backtest for detection evidence. A CANDIDATE-1 run (coaching-pivot decision, stake ~3–6 months ≈ €18–36k) is mid-loop at the enrichment→questions stage.

**References:** [align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md)

## 2026-07-13 [process]: docs-strategy-update let competing single-valued directives accumulate — two failures (never-ran + design blind spot), fix = Gate 8 + /kdd bypass close + pre-commit canary

**Context:** A `/challenge-prd` pass on P987 (CP front-door redo) tripped over a real doc defect: `lean-canvas.md` §UVP carries **three competing "lead the page with X" directives** — 2026-07-04 "Get to PMF faster", 2026-07-11 "divergent-AI hook", 2026-07-13 mission slogan — none marking the others superseded, so the homepage spec inherited an unresolved positioning contradiction. Investigation asked *why the anti-drift skill (`docs-strategy-update`) didn't catch it.*

**Decision (root cause — two independent failures, both confirmed against artifacts):**
- **(1) The gate never ran.** `.private/logs/skill-costs.log` (50 entries, months) shows **zero** `docs-strategy-update` runs; the drift commits (`74bc4b37`, `67dba0b6`) edited `lean-canvas.md` via `/kdd`/manual. Root cause: **`/kdd` contradicts itself** — its line-33 "Strategy-doc gate" says route strategy edits through `docs-strategy-update`, but lines 99–103 + 143–147 instruct `/kdd` to write `hypotheses.md`/`lean-canvas.md` directly (and step 4.4 commits them). Prose rule vs prose instruction, no enforcement → bypass.
- **(2) Design blind spot.** Even had it run, all three leads PASS the 7 gates: each `UNTESTED`-labeled (Gate 1), falsifier-carrying (Gate 5), non-negating (Gate 3's negation-grep misses), and additive-rewrite-shaped (Gate 4 explicitly protects "additive UNTESTED updates"). The skill cannot distinguish a **bet-list** (accumulate — correct for `hypotheses.md`) from a **single-valued slot** (one current answer — the page hero); the accumulate-everything philosophy leaked into a one-answer field.

**Fix (planned, not yet built):** (a) add **Gate 8 — single-valued-slot reconciliation**, deterministic via an explicit `<!-- SINGLE-VALUE: <slot> -->` marker on one-answer sections; (b) resolve the `/kdd` self-contradiction so strategy-doc content routes through the gate; (c) a deterministic pre-commit canary mirroring Gate 8 (defense-in-depth, WARN). Plus the mandatory failure-path proof (exercise Gate 8 + canary against the live §UVP drift before trusting them — epistemic.md Gate 7).

**Alternatives rejected:** keyword-heuristic Gate 8 (non-deterministic, noisy) — chose marker-based. Hard-BLOCK pre-commit (stops legitimate quick fixes) — chose WARN. `/falsify` to review the plan (5-phase overkill for a bounded process-rule change) — chose `/slava:think:adversarial-review` on the written plan artifact.

**Consequences:** Plan lives at `~/.claude/plans/on-go-joyful-unicorn.md` (outside the repo). Skill edits execute in a fresh session after adversarial-review of the plan; then an audit-mode run reconciles §UVP to one lead (a founder decision), unblocking P987. This entry is decision-capture only — no skill files changed yet.

**Falsifier:** if Gate 8 + the canary ship and a competing-directive drift still lands in a strategy doc undetected (or the `/kdd` path still writes strategy docs directly), the fix missed the root cause and the bypass/blind-spot diagnosis is wrong.

**References:** `.claude/commands/slava/maintain/docs-strategy-update/SKILL.md` · `.claude/commands/slava/maintain/kdd/SKILL.md` · [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md) §UVP · `~/.claude/plans/on-go-joyful-unicorn.md`

## 2026-07-13 [process]: Validating /align — a hand-written skill "run" is indistinguishable from a real one; only genuine user turns anchor it

**Context:** A long session designing how to prove `/align`'s load-bearing claim (surface a real comprehension gap instead of confidently rubber-stamping). Two false starts worth recording so a future session doesn't repeat them.

**Decision:**
- **The hallucination anchor.** Mid-session an agent produced a live `/align` "run" that was entirely hand-written — an alignment-unit-shaped output with no real sub-process, no definitions used, no questions actually asked. Root cause (surfaced by a critic): a skill is prompt text executed by the same model in the same context, so *"invoked the sifter, not hand-written"* is **unverifiable** — a narrated fake is indistinguishable from a real call. The **only** unforgeable signal that a run actually happened is **genuine user input on a separate transcript turn** (user confirms the target point; user answers the open questions; user types the rating). Verification of any interactive skill must key on that, never on the agent asserting a sub-process ran.
- **Test the whole loop, not an isolated stage.** Framing `/align` as 3 stages (detect-high-stakes → decompose → surface-vs-rubber-stamp) is an analytical lens, not canonical. A mid-session pivot to "test decomposition in isolation as the riskiest stage" was a too-fast social concession — reopened by a critic: the backtest's own confident-and-later-wrong cases **are** rubber-stamp failures by definition, so isolating decomposition walks away from the phenomenon the dataset captures. Test decompose→surface **together**, scored on two separate axes.
- **Backtest rigor (reinstated after a confounded shortcut):** ground-truth = the user's verbatim correction held out of the predictor; the user **freezes a gap-fingerprint before any unit runs**; a **separate arm-blind grader** scores; a **null baseline** the tool must beat. A "user-rates-their-own-accuracy" probe was rejected as a self-grading loop that cannot falsify (subject = grader, non-blind, N=1).

**Alternatives rejected:** blind backtest on dead transcripts as the FIRST validation (can't test the min-gate — needs a live user); a third adversarial review of the same spec (diminishing returns after reasoning-level + spec-level passes); trusting a narrated skill run as evidence.

**Consequences:** Near-term = bring `/align` to a minimum-executable bar (real Stage-1 point-identification with user confirmation; rigorous inline story recovery; run against shipped definitions; mandatory user turns for the questions AND the rating), then run it for real, then the two-axis blind backtest. Full spec + postponement ledger in the plan file. Postponed (downstream): high-stakes detection validation, decompose-as-scoring architecture, anti-point-in-sifter, the min-gate feedback loop, the blind backtest itself.

**References:** [align.md](.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md); plan `~/.claude/plans/once-i-guess-we-misty-quiche.md`

## 2026-07-13 [product]: point/story working model — orthogonal degrees; pointness = shared-arbiter availability (UNTESTED)

**Context:** The session pressure-tested the story/point distinction while designing `/align`. `docs/definitions.md` currently treats them as discrete TYPES. The refinement below emerged but is **unvalidated** — recorded per the record-under-uncertainty gate, and deliberately NOT written to `definitions.md` (that needs the `docs-strategy-update` gate, and the model is unproven).

**Decision (WORKING MODEL — UNTESTED):**
- Point and story are two **orthogonal degrees** an utterance scores on, not exclusive types: a thing can be high on both (run both loops), low on both (ignore), or high on one.
- **Pointness = degree of shared-arbiter availability** — raised by *arbiter-building* context, not mere volume (centuries of accumulated context can add no arbiter → an unfalsifiable claim stays low-pointness). Zero-pointness is an asymptote (the raw first-person quale), rarely reached.
- **Storyness is a property of the utterance-in-context, not the proposition** (a neutral factual claim is low-storyness; the same words from someone with lived stakes in them are high-storyness).
- The `/align` loop **decomposes** (recover claim + recover why), it never **classifies** (point XOR story) — so misclassification is off its path; but decomposition can still fail (a too-thin / wrong story IS the rubber-stamp).
- **Reuse caveat:** `sifter-story`'s point-seeded mode is generative-**persuasive** (builds a story that SUPPORTS the point). It must NOT be reused for `/align`'s why-recovery — it would manufacture a justification and launder it as the user's why, re-introducing the exact rubber-stamp `/align` exists to prevent. (Recovery is rigorous inline instead.)

**Alternatives rejected:** {story, point} as exclusive types (breaks on experience-avowals — high storyness, ~zero pointness; and on high-on-both claims); writing this into `definitions.md` now (unproven; needs the gate); "past prod/chat decompositions are invalid under the new definitions, discard them" (rejected — the 7-of-9-failing prod-point audit remains usable signal).

**Consequences:** Falsifier — a clean `/align` case that cannot be decomposed into (staked claim, recoverable why) without an exclusive point/story call. Migrate to `definitions.md` via `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` only after the backtest gives it evidence.

**References:** [definitions.md](docs/definitions.md); [sifter-story.md](.claude/commands/slava/content/sifter-story.md); plan `~/.claude/plans/once-i-guess-we-misty-quiche.md`

## 2026-07-13 [process]: Red-team the built implementation, not just the plan — an Opus critic on the shipped video scripts caught 3 FAILS two plan-level reviews missed

**Context:** The video-pipeline plan (`crispy-aurora`) went through **two** adversarial-review passes at the *plan* level and was declared "ready to build." After building the three skills, a single Opus critic reviewed the **implementation** (the actual `assemble.sh` / `beats.sh` / skill-step prose) against concrete failure inputs.

**Decision:** For orchestrator-style features, run a lean implementation-level adversarial pass **after building**, separate from any plan-level review — the two catch different bug classes. The plan reviews validated the *design*; only reading the built code surfaced three FAILS the design reviews structurally could not: (F) the orchestrated-mode **handshake was impossible** — `/video-edit-talk` minted its own `mktemp -d`, so the orchestrator's manifest could never land in it, orchestrated mode never fired, and the `.srt` got deleted (the exact transcript-loss class the plan set out to kill); (E) `beats.sh` **aborted the whole pass** when the last segment was shorter than the 4.5s card; (B) the `anchor_quote` re-location the plan *specified* was **never implemented**, while the docs still called timestamps "advisory." All three are gaps between described intent and running code — invisible to a plan review, obvious to a code review.

**Alternatives rejected:** trusting the two plan-level passes ("ready to build" was true of the plan, false of the code); the 5-phase `/falsify` pipeline (overweight — the repo's lean-default rule is one sharp critic with per-item SURVIVES/WEAK/FAILS verdicts, which is what ran).

**Consequences:** All six findings fixed and verified with edge tests (dup-id → exit 2; near-end beat → clamps + renders; handshake reversed so the orchestrator owns the dir). Generalizes: a skill that describes a handshake in prose is unproven until the built code is read — "the plan is sound" is not "the code is sound."

**References:** `.claude/commands/slava/util/video-edit-interview/` · `.claude/commands/slava/util/video-question-beats/assets/beats.sh` · epistemic gate 7 (exercise a gate's failure path).

## 2026-07-13 [technical]: Orchestrator OWNS the scratch dir; interview cut points are authoritative-from-SRT, not fuzzy-quote-relocated

**Context:** Two contract decisions surfaced while building + hardening `/video-edit-interview` (they were not settled by the plan). (1) The plan had each sub-skill isolate itself with its own `mktemp -d`, but an orchestrator needs to hand a shared project dir (with the manifest) to its trim sub-step. (2) The plan specified re-locating each cut by fuzzy-matching `anchor_quote` "nearest the advisory `src_start`" because the quote isn't unique — implying timestamps are unreliable.

**Decision:** (1) **The orchestrator owns the project dir.** Stage 1 does `mktemp -d`, writes `interview.manifest.json` into it, then invokes `/video-edit-talk` telling it to *use that dir* — the sub-skill mints its own dir only in standalone mode (detected by manifest presence). A sub-skill that unconditionally mktemps can never receive a caller's file; the ownership must sit with the caller. (2) **`src_start/src_end` are authoritative, copied verbatim from SRT segment boundaries** by the Opus selection pass (which has the real timestamped SRT); `anchor_quote` is downgraded to a human-readable **verification label**, not a re-location key. No fuzzy quote matcher is built — the SRT boundary *is* the cut; a recurring quote would only add ambiguity, and if quote and timestamp disagree that's a Stage-2 bug to fix, not something Stage 3 papers over.

**Alternatives rejected:** sub-skill detects orchestration then re-parents to a caller dir it discovers (fragile — no reliable discovery; the caller passing the path is deterministic); building a bash quote-search state machine that scans the SRT near `src_start` (real runtime complexity — SRT parsing, tie-breaking, occurrence-nearest logic — for marginal benefit when the SRT already provides exact numeric boundaries; argue-against-building wins).

**Consequences:** Cross-orchestrator pattern: any orchestrator→sub-skill file handoff must have the orchestrator create + own the shared dir, not hope the sub-skill adopts one. The interview manifest's timestamps are trusted numerically by `assemble.sh` — which shifts the accuracy burden onto Stage 2 emitting exact SRT boundaries (now stated as a hard contract in the skill).

**References:** `.claude/commands/slava/util/video-edit-interview/SKILL.md` (Stage 1 handshake, manifest schema) · `~/.claude/commands/slava/util/video-edit-talk.md` (step 0 orchestrated-vs-standalone).

## 2026-07-13 [process]: Video-editing pipeline splits talk vs interview; per-run scratch isolation (`mktemp -d`) + segment-identity manifest fix the transcript-loss class

**Context:** A ~71-min two-person interview edit ran ~1000 messages and landed poorly — meta-talk leaked into the cut (guest coaching the interviewer, "how much time do you have"), audio hard-cut at slide inserts, cuts landed mid-sentence, the branding skill was never wired in, and the transcript was lost + re-transcribed twice. Retrospective (session `29932534`) found the interview pipeline is structurally different from the linear-talk pipeline, but the generic `/video-edit-simple` skill was forced onto it. Transcript-loss root cause: intermediates written to shared `~/video-edits/` with generic names (`audio.wav`) that a concurrent process overwrote.

**Decision:** (1) Rename `/video-edit-simple` → `/video-edit-talk` (global, generic linear trim, brand-free). (2) Add cp-local `/video-edit-interview` orchestrator: trim → Opus 3-part selection sheet (aggressive meta-talk flags with coarse confidence + Pareto keep-set + reorder-for-viewer-interest, all human-approved before any cut) → cut+reorder → question beats → brand-pass. (3) Add cp-local `/video-question-beats`: lower-third question overlay, audio ducked (never hard-cut). (4) Deterministic scratch isolation via `mktemp -d` per run (NOT a `date` timestamp — same-second launches collide) + a stable **segment-identity manifest** (id / src range / `anchor_quote` / state / order / `out_start`) that every stage references instead of raw source timestamps. Two adversarial-review passes hardened the plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-enalbed-plan-crispy-aurora.md`.

**Alternatives rejected:** one skill with `--mode interview` (skills expose no flags; mixes global-generic with cp-specific logic); keying question beats by source timestamps (drifts after reorder — the manifest closes it); trusting the duration-assert as the overwrite guard (an external write arriving after the assert still slips through a shared name — `mktemp -d` is the real fix); the brand-pass card as a reusable lower-third (its card is full-frame/opaque webm — only its design tokens carry over).

**Consequences:** Build pending (three skills). The reasoning-heavy selection pass runs as an **Opus subagent with the transcript inlined** (mechanical stages stay Sonnet). Two founder decisions gate shipping: the question-beat card design, and the outro copy (see paired [product] entry). Multicam angle-sync is deferred — it's the dominant podcast-quality lever, so this plan fixes pipeline mechanics, not "podcast quality," and the framing should say so.

**References:** `~/.claude/plans/i-enalbed-plan-crispy-aurora.md` · `.claude/commands/slava/util/video-edit-simple.md` · `.claude/commands/slava/util/video-brand-pass/SKILL.md`

## 2026-07-13 [product]: Coaching offer is unpackaged case-by-case consulting NOW; the fixed-price ladder is the future PACKAGED state — de-price the structural docs (UNTESTED)

**Context:** Follow-through on the 2026-07-11 "unpackaged product with unproven transferability" read. Prices flex per customer / need / founder-confidence, which is the signature of the pre-productization stage: a fixed price requires a fixed package, and there is no package yet.

**Decision (UNTESTED):** The current active offering is **unproductized case-by-case coaching/consulting in the alignment problem space, priced per engagement** — no fixed price belongs in a structural doc while the product is unpackaged. ## 2026-07-11 [process]: `/align` blind backtest — scoped to *detection only*, and requires a null baseline to attribute the result

**Context:** Built `/slava:think:align` (previous entry) and designed its go/no-go blind backtest. Ran one hostile critic on the backtest *methodology itself* (not the skill) before executing, because a misleading go/no-go — false green ships a broken skill, false red kills a good one — is the most expensive error in the effort. Two critic findings were load-bearing. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/crystalline-mapping-galaxy.md` (not in-repo).

**Decision:** The blind backtest (feed only the pre-correction transcript slice to a separate agent, compare its ALIGNMENT UNIT to the actual correction) validates **detection only** — "does the loop surface the real gap vs rubber-stamp?" (Step 2). It **cannot** test the skill's actual spine, the mandatory `user_score` + `min()` gate (Step 3), because a dead transcript has no live user, so `min()` never binds. That half routes to the align plan's **separate live dry-run** where Slava supplies real ratings. **A GO on the backtest is necessary, not sufficient.** Second load-bearing fix: add a **null-baseline predictor** (same slices, generic fixed question, no `/align`) through the identical grader — `/align` must *beat null* by a margin, else its HITs are boilerplate a dumb agent also produces. Other folded fixes: blindness is *structural* (answer inlined-absent from the predictor's world, no cp checkout / no private-store access), not instructed; cut the slice **one human turn early** (the setup turn telegraphs the answer, and Slava can't feel the tell because he knows it — a blind leak-checker clears the tail instead); scan slices for **pre-existing assistant hedges** (echoing one HITs with zero skill contribution); the **gap fingerprint** is authored by the human and frozen before units, separating target-definition from the assembler who cuts + the grader who scores; **negative controls ≥ false-positives+corrections** because specificity (does it invent gaps?) is `/align`'s most-likely-broken property and was the least-tested.

**Alternatives rejected:** A *simulated-user* arm to exercise `min()` on transcripts — a sim that already holds the answer can't validate the one empirical question that needs a real human (does a low min trigger a real paraphrase, not a shrug). Absolute ⅔/½ thresholds at N≈8 without a baseline — noise; reframed as beating null. Trusting Slava's own boundary check to catch a leaky slice — he knows the answer.

**Consequences:** Run the backtest in a **fresh session** (assembler clean-room; kickoff prompt handed off). Sequence gates on Slava naming the bucket-A false-positives first. If GO (detection validated) → proceed to the live dry-run (§1) for the `min()` half before any CLAUDE.md codification. If NO-GO → the specific MISSes name what to fix in the loop. Artifacts private (`.private/backtests/align-v1/`). **`align.md` is written on `main` but uncommitted** — needs a separate skill-file commit (KDD does not commit skill files).

**References:** [.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md](../.claude/commands/slava/think/align.md); previous entry (align build, commit `3005c17c`).

## 2026-07-11 [process]: `/slava:think:align` — an AI alignment protocol whose spine is "no path to *verified* is completable by the AI alone" (`verified ⟺ min(ai_selfscore, user_score) ≥ 8`)
