(3) **"pairs vs solo" dissolves** into one product: train one individual via a practice agreement; partner-existence is a parameter; segment targeting is the coach's call. (4) **Objective function: maximize leverage-weighted paraphrasing worldwide** (rich/powerful weighted higher); cash-first as the proof gate, time/labor as a fallback price. (5) **Platform/practitioner split:** the coach keeps retention/relationship revenue; the founder keeps the license/method/club/data (Gottman-Institute shape). (6) **Parked phase-2+ flywheel:** certification/badger cascade, franchise, club, tooling co-invest, future-equity — multipliers on a base that is currently zero; build only after the first paid loop closes.

**Alternatives rejected:** Direct-to-founder acquisition (complex sale, one client at a time — the reason to route through coaches). Viral letter as growth engine (R₀≈0, empirically dead). Pairs-vs-solo as a customer-segment axis (one product, partner-existence is a parameter). "More customers" as the coach pitch (backwards — the coach brings the audience; lead with retention + measurability/proof-of-value).

**Falsifier (kill-condition):** If the first warm-coach co-delivered workshop produces **0 paid conversions** AND no coach will market it to their own audience after ~3 co-deliveries → the coach-distribution thesis is falsified; revert to direct-to-pair or test a different channel. Secondary read: if "verify before you commit" solo applicants vastly outnumber pairs, the prevention/matching market is the more alive one (a redirect, not a failure — impact-first learning-velocity frame).

**Consequences:** The four strategy docs need reconciliation — the coach-distribution layer and objective function were absent from all of them; the `/docs-strategy-update` gates flagged stale "Active"/"viral-as-proof", a theory-of-change "spreads NOT through coaches" contradiction, and phantom `#validated`/`#active-currently-testing` anchors. This entry is the Step-3 precondition for that sync (doc edits follow). Nothing here is validated — the application / first paid sale IS the demand test.

**References:** [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md), [theory-of-change.md](theory-of-change.md), [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md); P856 (cofounder coordination offer page); `/slava:maintain:docs-strategy-update` gate run (2026-06-02).

## 2026-06-02 [technical]: Email greeting personalization was incomplete — agreement *invitation* stayed hardcoded "Hi," despite the 2026-03-14 helper rollout; letter clone had diverged escaping

**Context:** The agreement invitation email (the most-sent email — fires on every invite) rendered a bare "Hi," with no recipient name. The 2026-03-14 [technical] entry claimed `send-agreement-emails` templates "all" use the `greeting()`/`firstName()` helpers — but `handleInvitation` was never wired in: it carried a literal `Hi,` even though an existing-user profile lookup already ran two lines below it (added for the P488 magic link, selecting only `id`). Separately `send-letter-emails` (cloned from `send-agreement-emails` per its file header) had diverged: `htmlEmail()` and `button()` interpolated the sender name into `<title>` and link attributes without escaping (the agreement function escapes both), and its greeting escaped the name once then reused it for both HTML and the `text/plain` body, leaking entities into plaintext.
**Decision:** (1) Invitation greeting resolves the partner name from their profile — reusing the lookup already present — or the creator's name on a self-invite, via the existing `greeting()` helper. (2) Letter falls back to a registered recipient's profile name when the sender typed none (guarded lookup, only when no name was provided). (3) Letter escaping moved to a module-scope `esc()` so `htmlEmail()`/`button()` can use it, and escaping now happens at the HTML boundary (`esc(greeting)`) with raw text for plaintext — matching `send-agreement-emails`. (4) Generic fallback for unknown recipients changed from "Hi," to "Hi there," (consistent with `request-letter-response-signin`).
**Alternatives rejected:** Adding a `partner_name` column to `clarity_agreements` to capture a typed name at invite time — a schema change for a case the fallback already handles honestly (brand-new email-only recipients have no name anywhere; `clarity_agreements` holds only `partner_email`, so "Hi there," is correct, not a bug).
**Consequences:** Verify edge-function copy claims against the actual handler, not a prior decision entry — the 2026-03-14 rollout silently missed one of four handlers. Cloned edge functions drift: the P684 plan to extract shared email helpers (CORS, template, Mailgun, escapeHtml) into `supabase/functions/_shared/` is still undone, and that drift produced the letter escaping gap. When cloning an email function, escape at the HTML boundary via a module-scope helper, not inside per-call variable construction. Found via adversarial code review of the greeting fix. On branch `fix/email-greeting-name`, deployed to test; prod deploy pending.
**References:** [send-agreement-emails/index.ts](../supabase/functions/send-agreement-emails/index.ts), [send-letter-emails/index.ts](../supabase/functions/send-letter-emails/index.ts); corrects 2026-03-14 [technical] (Event emails — name personalization); relates to P684 three-function split (`_shared` extraction).

## 2026-06-02 [process]: A claimed P-number can be taken by a co-tenant mid-session — collision surfaces at ship; recover by renumber (next-p-number.sh) + seed spec on main (P872, built as P870)

**Context:** This feature was claimed and built as P870 (`git-ops.sh claim p870`). During a long session a co-tenant created and committed a *different* `features/p870_*.md` to main, so p870 named two features. The clash surfaced only at `git-ops.sh ship p870`: `resolve_ship_spec` reads main's `features/`, found the co-tenant's spec (mine was on the branch), and the journal targeted the wrong feature. Hand-picking the next number ("p871") collided again — `next-p-number.sh` returned 872 because p871 already sat in `features/done/`.

**Decision:** (1) **P-numbers come from `./scripts/next-p-number.sh`, never manual** — it counts `done/`, which `ls`/`grep` miss (reconfirmed the hard way). (2) **Collision-at-ship recovery:** abort the in-progress cherry-pick (guarded — needs user OK), delete the stale `.ship-journal/pN.json` (else a co-tenant's pN ship would resume yours), renumber spec + decisions entry + branch (`git branch -m`), re-ship. (3) **`git-ops.sh ship` resolves the spec from MAIN** — a spec authored only on the branch must be seeded first (`git-ops.sh commit-to-main --files <spec>`; the die-message prints the exact command). This snag now recurs (P796/P866/P869/P872). (4) **`ship --resume` re-picks pending journal commits** — after resolving a cherry-pick conflict run `git cherry-pick --continue` to land it, then `--resume` (it detects "already applied"); or set the journal's `landed_sha` to skip Phase 1 deterministically.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Ship under the colliding number — closes the co-tenant's spec and creates a duplicate-P-number. (b) Manual `git merge --no-ff` instead of renumber+re-ship — bypasses the lock-serialized journaled path in a repo with 5 active co-tenants.

**Consequences:** The spec-on-main requirement is the single most-repeated ship snag. Durable prevention: when executing a detailed plan directly (no `/create-spec`), create the spec **on main** at the start (per features.md "Creation: always on main"), not on the branch — that also makes the P-number reservation visible to co-tenants sooner.

**References:** `scripts/git-ops.sh` (resolve_ship_spec), `scripts/next-p-number.sh`, `.claude/rules/features.md` (P-Number Assignment; Spec Location), [features/done/2026-04-22/p872_prototype_route_unification.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p872_prototype_route_unification.md)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: A "false-positive fix" to a secret scanner can silently remove a real backstop — widening the `services/` exclusion had a non-obvious security tail only adversarial review caught (P868)

**Context:** The Layer-2a grep secret backstop in `pre-commit-checks.sh` excluded every code dir *except* `services/`, so it false-positived on legitimate env-var *name* references (e.g. `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) in `services/transcribe` test code — the direct analog of the earlier `scripts/` exclusion (entry below). The obvious one-line fix is to add `services/` to the exclusion regex. But Layer-2a's exclusions for `src/`/`scripts/`/`api/` lean on the documented premise "gitleaks (Layer 1) covers these with proper rules" — and that premise is only as good as gitleaks' ruleset. `services/transcribe` reads `HF_TOKEN` (gated pyannote models, `config.py`), and gitleaks' default ruleset has **no HuggingFace `hf_` rule**. So excluding `services/` from the grep would have removed the *accidental* grep backstop for a hardcoded `hf_` token in the one tree most likely to contain one — and it would then have passed every layer.

**Decision:** Two-part change, the second only surfaced by `/finish` adversarial review: (1) add `services/` to the Layer-2a grep exclusion (`pre-commit-checks.sh:297`, comment line 296 updated to list `services/` as gitleaks-delegated); (2) add a `huggingface-access-token` rule to `.gitleaks.toml` (`regex hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{34,}` + placeholder allowlist) to restore the lost coverage at Layer 1 — which also closes the same pre-existing `hf_` blind spot that already existed for `src/`/`scripts/`/`api/`. Layer 2b (connection-string scan) is unaffected. The installed `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is a **symlink** to `scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh` (`install-hooks.sh` uses `ln -sf`), so editing the source IS the running hook — no reinstall, and no "diverged installed copy" (an early spec premise the review corrected).

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Ship the exclusion alone (the obvious fix) — leaves a real, narrow gap for the most-likely `services/` secret; the review's reframing of a "theoretical, out-of-scope" `hf_` allowlist note into a concrete blast-radius finding is why it's not shipped that way. (b) Narrow the `token\s*=` grep pattern instead of excluding the dir — risks missing real secrets (same rejection as the `scripts/` precedent). (c) Per-line `# gitleaks:allow` markers — papers over the design; the path exclusion is the correct, explicit mechanism.

**Consequences:** Same residual-risk rule as the `scripts/` precedent — a `services/` file that must hold a *real* secret belongs in `.private/`, never relied on the scanner. The transferable lesson: when widening a scanner's exclusion "to kill a false positive," ask what *true positives* that path was incidentally catching, and confirm the named backstop (here, gitleaks) actually has a rule for them — a green scanner after an exclusion change is not evidence the coverage moved. The sibling P868 entry below records the companion lesson (verify the new rule fires with a *random* token, not a famous example).

**References:** [features/done/2026-04-22/p868_precommit_scanner_services_exclusion.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p868_precommit_scanner_services_exclusion.md) · `scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh:297` · `.gitleaks.toml` (`huggingface-access-token` rule) · the `scripts/` Layer-2 grep exclusion [technical] entry below (the precedent this extends)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: Verify a secret-scanner detection rule with a realistic *random* token — scanners silently allowlist famous examples and low-entropy sequences (P868)

**Context:** Adding a `huggingface-access-token` rule to `.gitleaks.toml` (P868), the first verification used a sequential-alphabet token (`hf_ABCDEF…`); gitleaks returned "no leaks found", which read as a broken rule. It wasn't — gitleaks (like most scanners) deliberately filters obvious non-secrets: documented example keys (the AWS `AKIA…EXAMPLE` key, which also gave a false "no leaks" earlier in the same session) and low-entropy/sequential strings. A realistic random token (`hf_aB3xK9mP…`) fired the rule immediately. The regex matched in plain `grep`, but the running scanner's entropy/allowlist heuristics did not — config inspection is not verification.
**Decision:** When verifying a secret-detection rule, the positive test case must be a realistic high-entropy *random* value, plus a separate placeholder case to confirm the allowlist. Never use a famous example or a sequential/repeated string as the positive — a false negative is indistinguishable from a broken rule.
**Alternatives rejected:** Config-inspection only ("rule is present, regex matches in grep") — the regex matched but the tool still filtered the token; the running tool is the falsification target, not the pattern in isolation (epistemic gate: test the artifact, not the doc about it). Not an evasion concern — a real secret is high-entropy and is still caught; only fake test values get filtered.
**Consequences:** Future scanner-rule work (gitleaks rules, custom grep layers) verifies with a random token + a placeholder. Extends the existing "test against seeded fixture, not prose" principle.
**References:** [.gitleaks.toml](.gitleaks.toml), [P868 spec](../features/done/2026-04-22/p868_precommit_scanner_services_exclusion.md)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: Post-deploy prod-health gate — observe everything, allowlist the known-benign (inverts csp-smoke), and redact before any public surface (P866)

**Context:** A `406` on a `/letter` page reached prod unnoticed: it is not a CSP violation (so `csp-smoke` ignores it) and not a fatal React crash (so `app-boot-smoke`'s filter ignores it), and nothing loads a deployed page within minutes of a deploy to check the console. P866 generalizes the `csp-smoke` harness (the P864/P865 lineage's "fold a runtime gate onto the deployed artifact") into a console-error + HTTP≥400 gate over the public routes.

**Decision:** **Invert the filter.** Existing gates filter *what they observe* (CSP-only) to stay green; this gate observes *everything* (every console `error`, every HTTP response ≥400) and filters *what is known-benign* via a curated, commented allowlist — so a novel error fails by default. Key design points: (1) **one shared substrate** `e2e/helpers/prod-health.ts` (routes + stabilization poll + allowlist + `isAllowlisted` + `redactUrl`); `csp-smoke.spec.ts` refactored to import the routes + poll, so there is one source of truth, not two drifting copies. (2) **Two gates stay complementary on day one** — CSP violations surface via the `securitypolicyviolation` DOM event (csp-smoke's partition), which does NOT appear as a Playwright console `error`, so the console/HTTP gate legitimately does not catch the wasm-eval CSP block; folding CSP into prod-health is a deferred end-state once the allowlist is proven. (3) **Redaction is a security chokepoint** — captured URLs/console text can reach a public GitHub issue body, so `redactUrl` strips query strings (tokens live in `?token=`), `authorization`/`apikey` header values, and bare `key=value` secrets before any reporter or issue body; locked by a unit test. (4) **Alert-only day one** — the CI workflow uses `continue-on-error` + an `outcome`-gated find-or-append issue, so an unproven allowlist cannot post a scary red X. (5) **`/ship` post-push watch** — after the user's push, poll Vercel `readyState=READY` then smoke the prod alias inline, offering rollback / fix-forward / triage-as-benign, never auto-acting.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) A second parallel spec instead of a shared helper — two copies of the non-trivial stabilization poll drift (the P865 copies-rot lesson). (b) Test the `/letter` page that motivated it — needs a seeded prod row + token + elevated creds; cut entirely (public routes only, zero prod-data/secret surface). (c) A Vercel deploy webhook to auto-trigger — a new public relay + HMAC + secrets for a case the founder rarely hits; the `/ship` post-push loop + the existing cron cover the real flow. (d) Hard-block on day one — a broad gate with an unproven allowlist would be flaky; promote to blocking only after it is proven against real deploys.

**Consequences:** `npm run smoke:prod` (env `PROD_SMOKE_URL`) + a sibling alert-only cron `prod-health-smoke.yml`. The allowlist is the load-bearing artifact, reviewed like the P865 canary; `.supabase.co` is an intentional v1 host-level allow (narrowing is a future review — P866 does not chase the 406). First prod run found the public routes genuinely clean (a real filtered-green, proven by a synthetic catch-proof). When the allowlist is proven, fold csp-smoke's CSP assertion in — one prod-health gate, not two. Recovery gotchas hit while shipping (spec authored on a branch, never on main → seed-at-first-commit; stale same-P-number branch → `git branch -d`) are already documented in the 2026-04 P817 entry below.

**References:** [features/done/2026-04-22/p866_post_deploy_prod_smoke_gate.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p866_post_deploy_prod_smoke_gate.md) · `e2e/helpers/prod-health.ts` · `e2e/prod-health-smoke.spec.ts` · the 2026-06-01 P865 + P864 [technical] entries below (the runtime-gate lineage this folds into)

## 2026-06-01 [process]: Commit-comparison drift gates can't see an unpushed local main — a fix "merged to main" isn't live until pushed; only live-behavior gates catch the gap (P869)

**Context:** P869 — prod served a build predating the P865 CSP fix (`script-src` missing `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` → all WebAssembly blocked → HEIC uploads + LogRocket recorder dead). The fix WAS on local `main`, but local `main` had never been pushed: `origin/main` sat at the stale prod SHA (`2660787b`), 13 commits behind local. Vercel deploys `origin/main`, so "merged locally" ≠ "live." The scheduled `Check Deploy Drift` workflow compares deployed-prod against `origin/main` — both equal at the stale SHA — so it passed clean while the fix sat unshipped. (Flip side of P820, which deliberately pointed the manifest gate at `origin/main` to kill false-positive *branch* drift — the same choice that blinds it to an unpushed local HEAD.) What surfaced it was the P866 prod smoke gate, which loads the *deployed page* and fails on live CSP violations — a behavior check, not a commit comparison.

**Decision:** Treat "merged to local main" as **not live** until `git push` lands it on `origin/main` — the push is the deploy trigger, not the merge. To answer "is the fix actually live?" rely on **live-behavior gates** (P866 csp-smoke / prod-smoke, which load the deployed page), never on a commit-comparison gate's green. Push discipline is the only guard for the unpushed-local-HEAD blind spot.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Strengthen `Check Deploy Drift` to compare prod against *local* `main` — impossible; a server-side gate cannot observe an unpushed local HEAD. (b) Trust the drift gate's green as "prod is current" — it only proves prod == `origin/main`, never prod == your local work.

**Consequences:** When a shipped, tested fix appears "not live," check `git rev-list --count origin/main..main` *before* re-debugging code — an unpushed local main is the cheapest explanation and no gate flags it. The P866 smoke gate (loads deployed routes) is the authoritative "is it live" signal; a green commit-comparison gate is not. The fix itself required zero code — just a push.

**References:** [features/done/2026-04-22/p869_prod_stale_build_missing_wasm_csp.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p869_prod_stale_build_missing_wasm_csp.md) · P866 (prod smoke gate, the live-behavior catch) · P820 (manifest gate reads `origin/main`) · P865 (the CSP fix that wasn't live)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: Versioning load-bearing oath text — single-sourcing is necessary but NOT sufficient; build a verification skill (/upgrade-oath), not a re-sweep

**Context:** The 2026-05-31 v4-versioning decision (below) rejected "a mega skill to sweep the oath across all surfaces" in favor of single-sourcing the hardcoded React surfaces to the registry, claiming that "eliminates the drift class." Implementing P855 (pledge → v4) falsified the *sufficiency* half: single-sourcing the oath-*display* surfaces was necessary and done, but **prose descriptions** of the pledge (manifesto narrative quote, share-email invite bullets) can't be single-sourced — they paraphrase the oath in marketing copy — and silently stayed on v3 framing. Exact-string discovery greps missed them (paraphrased, not verbatim); AC#3 ("none on old text") was marked complete prematurely; `/finish` caught the gap.

**Decision:** Built **`/upgrade-oath`** (build namespace) — a discovery-based versioned-text bump with three mechanical gates: (1) no stale text on default-path surfaces; (2) every named block renders the new content (call-site completeness + content-freshness — catches the v3 hotfix class where THE EXCEPTION existed but wasn't invoked); (3) the version pointer (`CURRENT_PLEDGE_VERSION`) is the sole lever. Key concepts: **dispatched (renders a signer's *stored* version — grandfathered) vs default-path (renders *current*)** classification scopes every gate so grandfathering isn't false-flagged; **decision A** — app write-path + read-fallback resolve the pointer (`?? CURRENT`, not `|| N`), SQL column default stays as a backstop, so the pointer is the only rollback lever and no migration is needed. The skill single-sources where structurally possible AND verifies — it does not re-copy text. P855 owns the shared `VERIFIED_UNDERSTANDING_OATH` constant and ships *before* P857 (flipped from P857-first: the pledge already had versioning infra, making it the lower-risk surface to validate v4 publicly first).

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Pure single-sourcing, no skill (the 2026-05-31 stance) — necessary but insufficient; prose paraphrases drift and exact-string greps miss them. (b) A re-sweep skill that re-copies the oath everywhere — the original (correct) rejection stands; the skill *verifies* + single-sources, it doesn't propagate copies. (c) A migration to flip the SQL column default — unneeded; the app writes the pointer, default is a backstop, rollback stays a one-line pointer flip.

**Consequences:** `/upgrade-oath` is the path for future oath/agreement bumps; P857 extends it (agreement mode + `AGREEMENT_VERSIONS`). **Follow-up (Status: proposed):** strengthen the skill's discovery to (i) reconcile hits against the spec's explicitly-named surface list and (ii) flag *paraphrased* old framing, not just verbatim strings — the two gaps that let manifesto/share drift through. Deferred tech-debt: no automated test exercises the v4 render branches; `export-certificate` renders *current* (not the signer's pinned version) — pre-existing, out of scope.

**References:** [features/done/2026-04-22/p855_pledge_v4_number_first_upgrade.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p855_pledge_v4_number_first_upgrade.md) · `.claude/commands/slava/build/upgrade-oath.md` · `src/app/content/verified-understanding-oath.ts` · the 2026-05-31 [product] entry below (updates its sufficiency claim)

## 2026-06-01 [process]: Prototype routes unify under dev-gated `/tree` — route-gating controls reachability, NOT bundling (P872)

**Context:** Three conflicting conventions for prototype/harness routes coexisted and one leaked to prod: the `/tree/*` gallery (11 routes + a hub page) shipped **ungated** and was publicly reachable on the live domain; `/view` used `/_proto/{feature}`; P852 used a one-off `/_preview/letter-redesign`. Agents picked a prefix at random. While unifying everything under one dev-gated `/tree` prefix, the original plan's premise — that wrapping a lazy route in `{import.meta.env.DEV && …}` would strip its component chunk from the prod build for 8 of the 11 routes — was **falsified by the build**: all 8 own-module lazy chunks (`TreePage`, `landing-v2/3/4`, `design-audit`, `position-buttons`, `loading-demo`, `new-live`) still emit to `dist/assets`. A `lazy(() => import())` const is not tree-shaken (the call is not pure), so the dynamic import survives even when its only JSX use sits in a dead `false &&` branch. This re-confirms the 2026-04-14 "DEV guard only prevents rendering" entry (below); the plan had cited that entry yet claimed the opposite.

**Decision:** One prefix `/tree/*`, **dev-gated by default** via a single-line `{import.meta.env.DEV && <Route … />}` per route. The `/_proto` and `/_preview` route prefixes are retired (the `components/_proto/` *folder* stays — folder ≠ route prefix). Gating is understood precisely as a **reachability** control: in prod the route is unregistered (navigating there 404s) and its path string leaves the always-loaded index chunk — but the component code still deploys as a dead, never-fetched chunk. Removing code from the prod bundle requires **explicit import removal** (the only reliable strip; `/dev` step 9.6 does this for ephemeral `/view` demos). The persistent `/tree` gallery deliberately keeps its unreachable, mock-free, secret-free chunks. A genuinely prod-reachable route placed in the block stays ungated and carries `// PROD-REACHABLE: <reason>` on its route line. A narrow, warning-only `pre-commit-checks.sh` guard flags a `/tree|/_proto|/_preview` route added to `App.tsx` without a same-line gate.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Trust that route-gating strips the gallery chunks — falsified by the build; the chunks ship. (b) `lazy`/conditional-import tricks to force stripping — the 2026-04-14 entry found per-import bundler tricks unreliable, and a *persistent* gallery cannot delete its imports. (c) A separate dev-only build entry to fully strip the gallery — larger refactor; the residual (unreachable dead chunks, no secrets) does not justify it for landing-page experiments. (d) Keep three prefixes — the status quo that kept agents guessing.

**Consequences:** Adds the dev-gate requirement that the 2026-03-16 `/ux` "experiential forks in `/tree`" entry lacked. Reconciles with the 2026-04-14 entry: gating = prevents rendering/reachability; explicit removal = strips the bundle. Updated: `.claude/rules/src.md` (new Prototype Routes section), the `/view` + `/dev` skills (`/_proto` route refs → `/tree`; `/dev` step 9.6 changes the route-path pattern only, leaving the `_proto/` import-path pattern intact), and `pre-commit-checks.sh` (ungated-route guard). The ~5 docs that deep-link `/tree/*` as a live gallery (this file, p856, p562, p521, p847) are now dev-only-navigable — noted, not rewritten (append-only). Residual: the mechanical guard is heuristic (single-line, App.tsx diff only); the `src.md` convention is the backstop.

**References:** [src/App.tsx](../src/App.tsx) · [.claude/rules/src.md](../.claude/rules/src.md) · [scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh](../scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh) · `.claude/commands/slava/build/view.md` · `.claude/commands/slava/build/dev.md` · 2026-04-14 "DEV guard only prevents rendering" (below) · 2026-03-16 "/ux experiential forks in /tree" (below) · 2026-05-29 "Preview-first integration" (below — `/_preview` prefix superseded, the preview-first method stands)

## 2026-06-01 [product]: An onboarding demo that puppets a real component must replicate its interaction click-for-click — the intensity tutorial's 2-press demo misrepresented the real 3-click path (P867)

**Context:** P867 redesigned the P852 forced "intensity" tutorial — the looping modal that teaches readers they can refine a letter position (Slightly / default / Strongly) before committing. The demo puppets the *real* `PositionButtons` in controlled mode, but it compressed the interaction: a single press both selected Disagree AND opened the intensity menu. The real mechanic (P847 "Model C′") is **three** clicks: click selects the position (no menu) → click the *same* button again opens the intensity menu → click an intensity row. The founder watching the demo flagged it "feels misleading," and every copy attempt ("double-click", "click twice to select X") kept under-counting — because the demo itself was wrong, the copy had nothing honest to describe.

**Decision:** Rebuild the demo to the true 3-click sequence and let the copy name the real gesture: title `Double-click to pick "somewhat disagree"` (the "double-click" legitimately names the two same-button clicks that open the menu; the pick is the third, shown by the demo). Also: reframe the forced modal from an ambushing auto-animation into a directive ("Quick tip" tab + one instruction line, no question); switch the demo from the Agree to the **Disagree** path (calibrated disagreement is the higher-value intensity to teach); make the puppet cursor white-filled with a blue outline so it stays visible on the selected blue button (a brand-blue cursor vanished blue-on-blue at the key second click); tone-flip the click-ripple (white on the blue button, blue on the white menu row).

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Keep the 2-press demo — teaches a gesture that doesn't work; a "close enough" demo is worse than none. (b) "Double-click to select X" / "Triple-click" copy — both read as rapid same-spot clicks and mis-count against the real two-clicks-then-pick; "double-click" only works once it names the two *button* clicks and the demo shows the pick. (c) A separate "click" text cue at the cursor — added then removed; the ripple alone signals the press, the text was noise.

**Consequences:** Any tutorial/onboarding animation that puppets a real component must replicate its real interaction exactly — verify the click count against the component's *handler* (here `PositionButton.tsx` `handleGroupClick`, Model C′), not the spec's assumption about it. The intensity mechanic is canonically **3 clicks**: select → reopen-for-menu → pick. Verification was founder live-review of looping GIFs at desktop + 375px; the `.claude/rules/visual-qa.md` blind-QA subagent step was skipped in favor of direct iterative review.

**References:** [features/done/2026-04-22/p867_intensity_demo_disagree_click_affordance.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p867_intensity_demo_disagree_click_affordance.md), P847 (Model C′ position-button interaction), P852 (predecessor — forced tutorial)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: A CSP gate must detect via the securitypolicyviolation event and apply the allowlist to EVERY directive — reviewing the P865 fix found both gaps (P865 /finish)

**Context:** A post-ship code review (`/finish`) of the P865 CSP fix — the prevention layers themselves — surfaced two false-confidence gaps and one real latent bug. (1) The full-pool host rule was applied to `script-src` + `connect-src` but NOT `worker-src`, which stops inheriting `script-src` the moment it is declared (the exact P863 mechanism) — a rotated non-blob worker host would be blocked. (2) The runtime smoke gate detected violations by parsing `console.error` text and waited a fixed 5s: it missed violations that print no matching console line and raced LogRocket's deferred (~2s) load (a later "readiness" rewrite then hung on a vendor global the npm SDK does not expose). (3) Switching the gate to the `securitypolicyviolation` DOM event immediately caught a pre-existing site-wide WebAssembly block (`script-src blocked wasm-eval`) that broke HEIC photo uploads (heic2any) and degraded the LogRocket recorder — invisible to console-scraping.

**Decision:** Three rules. (1) **Apply a host-rotating vendor's allowlist to EVERY directive that governs it (script-src, worker-src, connect-src), and have the canary assert directive PARITY, not a hardcoded host subset.** worker-src now mirrors script-src's full LogRocket pool; the canary asserts `worker-src ⊇ script-src` LogRocket hosts. (2) **A runtime CSP gate detects via the `securitypolicyviolation` event (structural), not console text** — console parsing is locale/version-fragile and misses keyword violations like `wasm-eval`. Wait for the violation set to STABILIZE (min floor so SDKs init, max ceiling) — never a blind sleep or a fragile vendor-readiness global. (3) **Allow WebAssembly with `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, never `'unsafe-eval'`** — the scoped keyword permits WASM compilation only (sandboxed; no DOM/cookie access), not JS eval. Locked by canary so HEIC uploads cannot silently re-break.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Per-route WASM CSP exception — re-creates the route-fragmentation drift P865 warned about; one unified directive is more sustainable. (b) Filter `wasm-eval` out of the gate as "benign" — a gate green because we silenced a real violation is debt; fix the root cause so it is green because prod is clean. (c) `'unsafe-eval'` — allows JS eval, a large XSS surface; rejected for the scoped keyword.

**Consequences:** The P865 canary now also guards worker-src parity + `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. The smoke gate is structural + stabilization-polled (robust to load timing) and its cron failure opens a GitHub issue (an unwatched gate is no gate). The public CSP report proxy was hardened (body cap, content-type whitelist, fetch timeout). Meta-lesson: even the prevention layers had gaps — running a code-review pass on the fix itself is worth it, because "the gate looks green" is not "the gate catches the class."

**References:** [vercel.json](../vercel.json), [src/tests/p865-csp-logrocket-hosts.test.ts](../src/tests/p865-csp-logrocket-hosts.test.ts), [e2e/csp-smoke.spec.ts](../e2e/csp-smoke.spec.ts), P865 + P863 (entries above), P838 (securitypolicyviolation probe)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: navigateFallback bound to a non-precached index.html throws at SW startup — set `navigateFallback: null` (P864; corrects the 2026-05-15 "dead config / safe to keep")

**Context:** The 2026-05-15 entry (below) concluded `navigateFallback: '/index.html'` was "dead config — safe to keep" because the P838 NetworkFirst runtimeCaching route preempts it for navigation, and the non-precached inconsistency was "latent… if somehow reached." P864 proves that conclusion was incomplete: `vite-plugin-pwa` defaults `navigateFallback: 'index.html'`, which emits `registerRoute(new NavigationRoute(createHandlerBoundToURL("index.html")))`. `createHandlerBoundToURL` validates its URL against the precache **eagerly at registration**, so with `index.html` excluded from `globPatterns` (P838) the SW *startup* script throws `Uncaught (in promise) non-precached-url {"url":"index.html"}` in prod — independent of whether the navigation route is ever matched. Verified against the deployed artifact: `sw.js` contained `createHandlerBoundToURL("index.html")` with no matching precache entry. localhost never reproduces (dev server has no production SW) — same prod-only / static-checks-blind class as P805/P863/P865.

**Decision:** When `index.html` is excluded from the precache, set `navigateFallback: null`. Navigation is already served by the NetworkFirst `app-shell` runtimeCaching route (`request.mode === 'navigate'`), so the precache-bound NavigationRoute is both unreachable for routing AND actively throwing at startup — removing it is strictly correct and preserves P838's always-fresh-shell intent. **Invariant:** `navigateFallback` must reference a precached URL or be `null`; "dead/unreachable config" is not automatically inert — eager validators can still throw. Build-verified: post-fix `dist/sw.js` contains no `createHandlerBoundToURL` and no `NavigationRoute`; navigation still matches the NetworkFirst route. Static canary `src/tests/p864-sw-navigate-fallback.test.ts` parses `vite.config.ts` and fails if the fallback is bound to a non-precached URL.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Keep `navigateFallback` per the 2026-05-15 "safe to keep" — it throws in prod. (b) Re-add `index.html` to `globPatterns` — would satisfy the invariant but reverts P838's always-fresh-shell behavior. (c) Build a standalone runtime `/sw.js` gate now — duplicates P865's `csp-smoke` harness; deferred to fold there.

**Consequences:** Extends the CSP-triad lesson to the service worker: build config that is "dead" for routing can still throw at startup, and the durable catch for prod-only SW/CSP regressions is a **runtime gate on the deployed artifact** — deferred to fold into P865's `csp-smoke` harness (fetch deployed `/sw.js`, assert no `createHandlerBoundToURL` to a non-precached URL). The fresh-load "Page not found" on shared deep links is *plausibly* resolved by removing the startup throw (the SW script now executes fully and registers its NetworkFirst nav route), but this is **verified post-deploy** — if it persists for fresh visitors it belongs to the separate stale-SW class (2026-05-31 entry), not this fix. Two `[post-deploy]` ACs remain on P864.

**References:** [vite.config.ts](../vite.config.ts), [src/tests/p864-sw-navigate-fallback.test.ts](../src/tests/p864-sw-navigate-fallback.test.ts), 2026-05-15 entry (navigateFallback dead config — below), 2026-05-31 entry (stale SW first suspect), P865/P863 CSP-triad entries (below).

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: Deleting a profile cascades into shared content — safe user-delete protocol (reassign points, order the history trigger)

**Context:** Cleaning two founder test accounts from prod surfaced that deleting `auth.users`/`profiles` cascades well past user-owned rows into *shared content*. `points.first_validator_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting the account that first-validated a point deletes the point itself — and one test account was the first_validator of a real content point that lives in a sealed one-to-many letter a real user had already responded to. The cascade is additionally blocked by NO-ACTION FKs from the letter subsystem (`letter_point_responses.point_id`, `letter_story_snapshots.story_id`, `clarity_sessions.source_letter_id`) and by a trigger: deleting `point_positions` fires an INSERT into `point_position_history` whose `user_id` FK fails once the profile is already gone in the same cascade. Three `auth.users` DELETE attempts each 500'd on a different one of these — only the live run found them; static FK analysis and an adversarial-review subagent both missed at least one.

**Decision:** A user-deletion must never cascade-delete content. Safe-delete protocol (encoded in `/clean-test-users` v2): (1) **reassign `points.first_validator_id` to the founder** — points are shared/reusable content, never deleted by a user-cleanup (a separate point-graveyard skill retires points); (2) authored **stories are deletable** (their points survive via the `story_points` junction) *unless* frozen into a sealed letter, in which case reassign `author_id`; (3) **delete `point_position_history` + `point_positions` BEFORE the profile**, so the history-insert trigger runs while the profile still exists; (4) clear the letter-subsystem NO-ACTION refs first; (5) after deleting verifications, **recompute the counterparty's `ears_count`/`verification_session_count`** (those triggers only increment, never decrement).

**Alternatives rejected:** Delete the blocking point + the real user's response to force the cascade through — destroys shared content and real-user data, and would silently edit a sealed letter other recipients are still working through. Force past each FK error — the errors are the DB correctly refusing to orphan content.

**Consequences:** Any future account-deletion path (GDPR / account-closure, not just test cleanup) must follow the same protocol — profile deletion is **not** a leaf operation in this schema. The fail-loud loop (stop on first non-2xx, never force-continue) is what kept it safe — it caught three distinct blockers. Open follow-up (deferred): `points.first_validator_id ON DELETE CASCADE` makes shared content fragile to user deletion; a schema review could move it to `SET NULL`/RESTRICT.

**References:** [.claude/commands/slava/maintain/clean-test-users.md](../.claude/commands/slava/maintain/clean-test-users.md); supabase/migrations/20260204_stories_points_calibration.sql (first_validator + ears trigger), 20260403224331_p581_clarity_letters.sql (letter FK cluster), 20260220120000_story_point_history_cascade.sql (history trigger)

## 2026-06-01 [process]: clean-test-users rewritten allowlist-first — identification is a known set, not a heuristic problem

**Context:** `/clean-test-users` had grown to 421 lines around a heuristic classifier (domain/name/slug pattern matrix, surname false-positive guards, an adversarial-critic subagent gate, signal-split approval prompts). But the founder's test accounts are a *known fixed set* of namespaces (loaded from gitignored `.private/docs/founder-accounts.md`), so identification was never a guessing problem.

**Decision:** Replace heuristic identification with an **allowlist** of the founder's own namespaces (+ founder/fixture exclusions). An allowlist cannot mis-target a real user, which removes the entire false-positive-protection apparatus (heuristics, critic, signal-split). The one residual risk an allowlist can't remove — a real user on the *other side* of a shared row, or shared content the test account first-validated — is handled by a targeted Phase-2 counterparty/content scan, not fuzzy matching. Net 421 → ~130 lines.

**Alternatives rejected:** Keep the heuristic net "to be safe" — the safety it bought only exists because heuristic matching is dangerous; removing the guessing removes the risk it guards. Delete the skill and do it ad-hoc — the FK-ordered cascade cleanup (see the [technical] entry above) is genuinely fiddly and worth encoding once.

**Consequences:** Skill changes were validated live against the two real prod accounts, which is exactly what surfaced the cascade blockers now baked into Phase 4. Privacy: the founder's actual test addresses live only in gitignored `.private/docs/founder-accounts.md`; the public skill loads them, never hardcodes them. General pattern — when "identify the bad rows" is a known set, an allowlist + a narrow real-data-conflict scan beats a classifier + adversarial gate.

**References:** [.claude/commands/slava/maintain/clean-test-users.md](../.claude/commands/slava/maintain/clean-test-users.md), .private/reports/test-user-cleanup/2026-06-01.md

## 2026-06-01 [product]: Lean canvas re-cut to coordination-tooling positioning (prevention ⊂ coordination); promoted as pre-validation, not held (Clarity Foundry)

**Context:** The "Clarity Foundry" strategy session (2026-06-01, claude.ai) sharpened both the problem and the positioning. Processing it via `/claude-conversations-to-cp`, a proposer subagent recommended two `lean-canvas.md` edits; an adversarial critic recommended **HOLD** — capture in this log, promote to the canvas only after the first Foundry cohort runs (the session itself stamped every conclusion "hypothesis until run one"). The founder overrode the HOLD on a principle the critic's frame missed: **the lean canvas is a living current-clarity document** — it already carries dated "(…, untested)" entries (e.g. lines 173, 235) — so it should reflect current clarity *now*, explicitly marked pre-validation, rather than be withheld until validated. "It is our clarity now, not clarity after."

**Decision:**
1. **Positioning category re-cut: "preventive calibration" → "coordination tooling," settled deductively.** Preventing a cofounder split is one outcome of better coordination, so **prevention ⊂ coordination** — coordination is the superset (the whole distribution of friction/rework), prevention is the tail-case and the *entry wedge*. The category is settled by deduction, not by a run. Core-innovation line: most "alignment" tools conflate *"we don't understand"* with *"we don't agree"* and burn months treating one as the other; the protocol tells a team **which** gap blocks them right now.
2. **Problem re-cut from tail-risk to continuous cost.** Added the coordination-degradation framing (decision speed/coordination degrade when trust rests on affinity not verified understanding; can't tell misunderstandings from real disagreements) *above* the existing False Agreement framing (which becomes the tail special-case).
3. **Canvas-promotion policy:** converged-but-untested framings go into the canvas now, marked `(pre-validation — pre-Foundry-run)` with an explicit **promotion trigger**, rather than held in this log. This is the meta-decision: canvas = current clarity with dated markers, not a validated-only artifact.
4. **Guardrails kept from the critic (the parts that didn't depend on the wrong "validated-only" assumption):** the meaning/validity asymmetry is written **as a hypothesis, not fact**, preserving the in-session qualifier ("a meaning gap is reconcilable *in principle*, but you can't tell when you've reached it without verification; a validity disagreement may not reconcile at all"), and flagged against **Blocked H-MetaEpistemic**. The **lead-copy hook** (does the validity axis lead, or the bare meaning gap?) is left **OPEN as a landing-page A/B** — it cannot settle deductively, only by a live test.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- **Critic's full HOLD** (no canvas edit; capture only here until run one) — rejected: treats the canvas as validated-only, which contradicts how this canvas is used (dated-untested precedent). The defensible core of the critic (qualify the asymmetry, don't claim the category is run-settled) was kept instead.
- **Assert "coordination" as settled by evidence** — no; settled by *deduction* (prevention ⊂ coordination); copy/hook stays a live test.
- **Route the three-layer hierarchy (affective enables → cognitive verifies → validity outcome) to a17** — rejected: a17's three "types" are declarative/procedural/cognitive, a different taxonomy; conflating them would confuse readers. Routed to a9 (founder's tag; spec-logged, draft wording deferred) and echoed in a33.
- **Record the feedback-infrastructure alternative MVP in the canvas** (Future Segments / Alternative Approaches) — rejected as premature (single-utterance, founder explicitly unsure); captured as article a31 instead.

**Consequences:** `lean-canvas.md` §Problem (L29), §Customer Segments (L75), §UVP (L211) now carry the coordination framing as pre-validation. **Promotion trigger:** when the first Foundry cohort (P856) confirms the gap is felt as a recurring cost, promote out of pre-validation; until then the asymmetry claim stays gated by Blocked H-MetaEpistemic and the hook stays an open A/B. **Deferred (NOT in canvas):** the downstream-trust / "honesty about misalignment" signal is Problem-B design — held until B is built (it would contradict the session's "run one = inner loop only" decision); seeded as demand-narrative in article a34 (ties to Blocked H-InvestorDD). **Content filed this session:** a30 (illusion of understanding), a31 (feedback infrastructure), a32 (humiliation barrier — sibling to a27), a33 (CPA story), a34 (honesty-about-misalignment de-risking); a9 + a29 enriched (three-layer hierarchy; mini-Flip).

**References:** [lean-canvas.md](lean-canvas.md), [hypotheses.md](hypotheses.md) (H-MetaEpistemic Blocked; H-InvestorDD Blocked), [features/p856_foundry_offer_page_application_form.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p856_foundry_offer_page_application_form.md), [content/articles/a30_illusion-of-understanding-alignment-tools.md](../content/articles/a30_illusion-of-understanding-alignment-tools.md)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: CSP must allowlist a vendor's FULL host pool, and CSP violations need a runtime gate — static canaries only lock known hosts (P865)

**Context:** Third prod CSP break from the same Apr-4 enforce-flip lineage (P805 `connect-src`, P863 `worker-src`). The enforcing `script-src` listed one LogRocket CDN host (`cdn.lr-in-prod.com`); the SDK (v10) served `logger-1.min.js` from `cdn.lgrckt-in.com` and was blocked, silently stopping session replay for every browser user. Root: LogRocket *deliberately rotates* its bundle host across ~12 CDN families (`lgrckt-in.com`, `lrkt-in.com`, `lr-ingest.io`, …) to evade ad-blockers — so allowlisting the one host in today's error loses to the next rotation. Neither the prior fixes nor the P863 canary could catch this: they assert hosts we already know; they cannot discover a host the vendor rotates to.

**Decision:** Two rules. (1) **Allowlist the vendor's entire documented host pool, not the host in today's error.** P865 added all 12 LogRocket CDN hosts to `script-src` and all 13 wildcard origins to `connect-src` (per LogRocket's CSP docs). A single-host allowlist for a host-rotating vendor is a latent recurring bug. (2) **CSP violations are a runtime/deploy-time class that static checks structurally cannot catch — add a runtime gate.** The CSP lives in `vercel.json` response headers (Vite dev never applies them) and which host an SDK loads from is decided at runtime, so `tsc`/eslint/build/unit-tests are all blind. The durable catch is a browser that loads the *deployed* strict-CSP routes and fails on any CSP violation: `e2e/csp-smoke.spec.ts` + `npm run smoke:csp`, run post-deploy and on a 6-hour cron (`.github/workflows/csp-smoke.yml` — the vendor rotates independently of our deploys, so prod can break with no commit from us), plus a passive `report-uri`/`report-to` → Sentry sink (`api/csp-report.ts`, a same-origin proxy that keeps the DSN out of this public repo) for real-user violations between cron runs.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Add only `cdn.lgrckt-in.com` (the failing host) — loses to the next rotation; this is exactly the P805→P863→P865 whack-a-mole. (b) Static canary only — locks known hosts but cannot discover new ones; necessary but insufficient (kept as `src/tests/p865-csp-logrocket-hosts.test.ts`). (c) Self-host/proxy LogRocket through our own domain — avoids widening `script-src` to the vendor pool, but is larger infra for a vendor we already trust with full session replay; deferred, not warranted.

**Consequences:** "Static canary + runtime smoke gate + passive reporting" is now the standard CSP defense triad — the canary (build-time) locks known hosts, the smoke gate (deploy-time + cron) discovers unknown ones, the Sentry sink (real-user) backstops between runs. `vercel.json` was added to the pre-commit `BUILD_AFFECTING` set so a CSP-only edit still runs the canary locally. One operator step remains: set `SENTRY_CSP_REPORT_URL` in Vercel env to activate the passive sink (layers 1–3 work without it). Pattern generalizes: any host-rotating or multi-endpoint third party (ad-block-evading analytics, multi-region ingest) needs the full-pool rule + the runtime gate, not host-by-host patching.

**References:** [vercel.json](../vercel.json), [src/tests/p865-csp-logrocket-hosts.test.ts](../src/tests/p865-csp-logrocket-hosts.test.ts), [e2e/csp-smoke.spec.ts](../e2e/csp-smoke.spec.ts), [api/csp-report.ts](../api/csp-report.ts), P863 (entry below), P805 (features/done/2026-04-22/p805_csp_connect_src_missing_gcs.md)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: CSP enforce-flip audit must cover worker-src + blob: workers, not just script/connect-src (P863)

**Context:** The Apr-4 flip of the CSP header from Report-Only to enforcing (`c64dfd81`) has now produced two prod bugs from the same gap — an incomplete outbound/worker audit at flip time. P805: `connect-src` was missing `storage.googleapis.com` (every browser GCS upload blocked). P863: (1) no `worker-src` directive at all, so the session-replay `blob:` workers used by LogRocket and the Mixpanel recorder fell back to `script-src` (no `blob:`) and were blocked; (2) `cdn.mxpnl.com` was in `script-src` but missing from `connect-src`, so the Mixpanel recorder bundle fetch was blocked. Both silently broke analytics for every browser user with no user-facing error.

**Decision:** Extend the pre-enforce CSP audit (P805's "grep every non-`self` `fetch()` destination") to also cover **worker contexts**. Any third-party SDK doing session replay (LogRocket, Mixpanel session recorder) instantiates Web Workers from `blob:` URLs, which require an explicit `worker-src` listing `blob:`; an absent `worker-src` is not safe-by-default — it silently falls back to `script-src`. Second rule: when **adding a previously-absent CSP directive**, preserve the sources it inherited via fallback. `worker-src` was unset → workers were governed by `script-src` (three CDNs listed). Setting `worker-src 'self' blob:` alone would add `blob:` but silently *drop* those CDN origins from worker scope — a latent failure mode for any CDN-hosted (non-`blob:`) worker. P863 shipped `worker-src 'self' blob: <the same three CDNs>` (only-add-never-remove); those CDNs are already `script-src`-trusted, so the listing widens nothing.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) `worker-src 'self' blob:` only — drops the three CDN origins workers previously reached via the script-src fallback; rejected for the latent worker-load regression. (b) Add `blob:` to `script-src` instead of declaring `worker-src` — broader than needed (affects all script loads) and still wouldn't preserve the precise worker source set. (c) Loosen to a permissive policy — masks the audit gap and weakens the header.

**Consequences:** A static canary (`src/tests/p863-reproduce.test.ts`, sibling of the P805 canary) parses `vercel.json` and asserts `worker-src` lists `'self' blob:` + the CDN origins and that `connect-src` includes `cdn.mxpnl.com`; reverting the header fails the test. Standing rule for the next CSP enforce/tighten change: audit script-src AND connect-src AND worker-src against every third-party SDK, including the blob:-worker requirement of any session-replay tool. CSP behavior is prod-only (Vite dev does not emit `vercel.json` headers), so these fixes are unverifiable locally beyond the static canary — the two "zero violations in prod console" ACs are `[post-deploy]`. The Workbox `non-precached-url` console error seen in the same screenshot is a separate subsystem, tracked as P864.

**References:** [vercel.json](../vercel.json), [src/tests/p863-reproduce.test.ts](../src/tests/p863-reproduce.test.ts), P805 (features/done/2026-04-22/p805_csp_connect_src_missing_gcs.md)

## 2026-06-01 [technical]: Center-when-fits above a fixed bottom bar with `my-auto`, never `justify-center` (P860)

**Context:** `story-rate` (and any phase with content above a `position:fixed` bottom drawer) was top-aligned, leaving a dead gap between short content and the drawer. The fade + chevron scroll cues were gated on content overflow, so they vanished in exactly the short-content case. Centering with `flex flex-col justify-center` clips overflowing content above the scroll origin (the top becomes unreachable) — the long-standing reason `story-rate` stayed top-aligned.

**Decision:** For "center the content when it fits, top-align + scroll when it overflows" above a fixed bottom bar: wrap in `flex flex-col` with a viewport-minus-chrome `min-h` (e.g. `min-h-[calc(100dvh-56px)]`) and put `my-auto` on the single in-flow child. Auto margins are "safe centering" — positive free space splits top/bottom (centered); on overflow the margins resolve to 0 so content pins to flex-start and scrolls (no clip). Reserve the drawer via the already-measured `paddingBottom: drawerHeight+8` so the child centers in the band between the top chrome and the drawer. Pure CSS — no JS measurement, no flicker.

**Alternatives rejected:** `justify-center` (clips overflow, top unreachable); JS height-measurement toggle (flicker + dependency on overflow-gated state); detach-drawer / grow-image (founder reviewed all three, picked centering).

**Consequences:** Reusable for any fixed-bottom-CTA + variable-content screen. **Guard:** when an in-flow element (e.g. an auth-gate prompt) renders *instead of* the fixed drawer, disable the centered branch (`&& !authGateAtStoryRate`) — `my-auto` is inert in block flow, so the fallback top-aligns correctly. Centering distributes empty space, it does not eliminate it — sparse on ultra-short/no-image content, negligible once real content (a ≤50vh image) fills the band.

**References:** [letter-flow-content.tsx](../src/app/components/letters/letter-flow-content.tsx), P860 spec.

## 2026-06-01 [process]: Live-verify deep letter-flow phases via the `/letter/:docId/preview` route (P860)

**Context:** `/verify` of `story-rate` must reach it live on the real `LetterFlowContent`. The seeded reading-page route (`/letter/:id?token=`) stalls at the cover in the Playwright harness — the cover→reading `viewState` transition does not fire for seeded token deliveries — blocking reachability.

**Decision:** To live-verify any letter-flow phase, drive the **preview route** `/letter/:docId/preview` (`LetterPreviewPage` renders the real component, non-persisting, no token/consent cover gate). Seed a doc + story + point; a 1-point story is story-first (D36), so `story-rate` is the first phase after "Open the Letter". Assert layout geometry in the real DOM (e.g. card center within 20% of the band between top bar and drawer) rather than eyeballing a screenshot. `e2e/p860-verify.spec.ts` is the template.

**Consequences:** Future letter-phase visual verification reuses this route + assertion pattern instead of fighting the reading-page cover gate.

**References:** [e2e/p860-verify.spec.ts](../e2e/p860-verify.spec.ts), [letter-preview-page.tsx](../src/app/pages/letter-preview-page.tsx).

## 2026-05-31 [technical]: Hide a focusable-containing container with `inert`, not `aria-hidden` (P862)

**Context:** The letter engage phases (`point-engage`, `remaining-point-engage` in `letter-flow-content.tsx`) gated a post-selection tip row with `aria-hidden={selectedPosition === null}`. That row contains a focusable replay button, so when it hid while the button held focus, Chrome blocked it: "Blocked aria-hidden on an element because its descendant retained focus."

**Decision:** For any container that is conditionally hidden AND contains a focusable element, use the `inert` attribute (`inert={hidden}`), never `aria-hidden`. `inert` removes the subtree from both the a11y tree and the focus order, so a focused descendant is cleanly blurred — no aria-hidden/focus conflict. React 19 renders `inert={false}` as no attribute, so the element stays interactive when shown. Precedent already lived in `PositionButton.tsx`.

**Alternatives rejected:** (A) Keep `aria-hidden` + manually move focus before hiding — extra focus-management code, easy to miss an edge. (B) `display:none` — destroys the reserved `min-h` layout the engage block needs to avoid reflow. (C) Leave it — a real warning AT users hit.

**Consequences:** Pattern rule for `/architect`, `/finish`, `/spec-review`: hidden container with a focusable child → `inert`. Plain `aria-hidden` is still correct on hidden TEXT/icon nodes with no focusable descendant (e.g. the dev-only `<p>` at `letter-redesign-preview-page.tsx:781`, intentionally left). Regression test `src/tests/p862-engage-tip-inert.test.tsx` asserts both surfaces in both states (RED on aria-hidden, GREEN on inert).

**References:** [p862](../features/done/2026-04-22/p862_letter_engage_tip_inert_a11y.md)

## 2026-05-31 [technical]: "Fix deployed but issue remains" on the PWA = stale service worker first, not a failed deploy

**Context:** A CSP wall (Mixpanel / Supabase / Sentry / GCS all blocked under `connect-src 'self'`) persisted in the browser after a deploy that had already fixed the CSP header. The enforced policy matched no current source file.

**Decision:** When a deploy appears not to take effect on claritypledge.com, suspect a stale service worker before re-deploying. Verify deterministically: (1) `curl -sI` the prod URL — confirms the SERVER header is correct; (2) in-browser, register a `securitypolicyviolation` listener and `fetch()` an allowlisted third-party host — zero violations means the loaded document enforces the correct policy; (3) confirm the SW precache (`caches.open('workbox-precache-v2-…')`) does NOT contain `index.html` (P838 excludes it, serves it NetworkFirst). A cached navigation Response replays its OLD headers (including CSP) until the SW updates.

**Alternatives rejected:** (A) Re-deploy / "push again" — the deploy was already correct; wastes a cycle and hides the real cause. (B) Loosen the CSP — masks a non-problem and weakens security.

**Consequences:** Incognito windows register their OWN service worker, so the stale-SW symptom can appear in incognito while a normal window is clean. Fix for the affected window: close it fully (clears the SW) or Clear site data — no code change. The `securitypolicyviolation` probe beats console-scraping for verifying enforced CSP (console capture is timing-sensitive across reloads).

**References:** P838 (NetworkFirst app-shell, html excluded from precache)

## 2026-05-31 [process]: P861 — make the pre-commit type gate real by gating on the undeclared-identifier class only (strategy A of an A→C path), not a full baseline or cleanup

**Context:** The pre-commit "TypeScript ✓" was a no-op (decisions.md 2026-05-31 [process] — bare `tsc --noEmit` resolves the empty root solution tsconfig), which is how P859's `ReferenceError` shipped. Turning on a real gate is blocked by the volume of pre-existing errors. Assessment this session (`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`): **856 diagnostics across 152 files** — but split **550 in test files** vs **306 in non-test app code**, and ~**425 are strictNullChecks noise** (TS2532/18048/18047). The class that actually crashes at runtime (the P859 class — undeclared identifier, `TS2304`/`2552`/`2582`) was only **8 errors in shipping app code**. So preventing the next P859 does **not** require triaging 856 errors.

**Decision:** Gate now on the **cannot-find-name class only** (`TS2304`, `TS2552`, `TS2582`) in **non-test app code** — strategy **A** of an explicit **A→C** path. `scripts/typecheck-gate.sh` runs the real `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` and fails the commit if any gate-class error appears in non-test `src/`; `pre-commit-checks.sh` calls it in place of the no-op. Fixed the 8 existing app-code errors (7 `TS2304` + 1 `TS2552`, all missing imports / a `chunk` declared in `try` but read in `catch`) so the tree sits at zero gate-class errors. Regression guard: `scripts/test-typecheck-gate.sh` (proves the gate BLOCKS an undeclared identifier and ALLOWS clean code), wired to run whenever the gate or hook is staged — same canary-on-staging pattern as P783/P787. The same no-op existed on a second surface — CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) also ran bare `npx tsc --noEmit`; both surfaces now call the gate, so pre-commit and CI enforce the identical contract. **A→C:** incrementally clear the 425 null-safety + test-file errors, then broaden toward `tsc -b` (full strict, zero exceptions).

**Alternatives rejected:** (b) **Full baseline-ratchet** (snapshot all 856, fail only on new) — the baseline file is a permanent maintenance artifact that rots: line-number drift, merge churn, 856 errors frozen as "accepted forever." Least sustainable; a detour off the A→C arc that would later have to be dismantled. (c) **Fix-then-enforce** (clear all 856, then `tsc -b`) — best end state but its 152-file precondition is exactly the kind of cleanup that stalls, leaving the gate a no-op and prod unprotected meanwhile. A is a strict **subset** of C, so doing A first costs nothing toward C.

**Consequences / limitations (accepted):** (1) `tsc` has no per-file mode, so the gate typechecks the whole project — it reflects **working-tree** state, not the staged diff. With the app tree at zero gate-class errors this is attributable to the working change; a staged-diff-precise gate is the deferred Option B. (2) **Test files are excluded** — they carry pre-existing `TS2304`/`2582` from missing vitest globals (a separate cleanup on the C path); test type errors don't ship to prod. (3) **Type mismatches** (`TS2322`/`2345`, mostly strictness) are **not** gated yet — lower runtime severity than a guaranteed `ReferenceError`, far more numerous; closed later via A→C, not by freezing a baseline. (4) The gate runs the full app typecheck on every build-affecting commit (gated behind `BUILD_AFFECTING`). Implementation gotcha for future edits: `set -o pipefail` + `grep -q` (early pipe close) makes `printf | grep -q` report SIGPIPE failure even on a match — `typecheck-gate.sh` uses here-strings (`<<<`) and no pipefail to avoid it.

**References:** [features/p861_precommit_typecheck_noop.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p861_precommit_typecheck_noop.md); `scripts/typecheck-gate.sh`; `scripts/test-typecheck-gate.sh`; `scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh` (§1 TypeScript, §4.7b canary); `.github/workflows/test.yml` (CI uses the same gate); decisions.md 2026-05-31 [process] (the no-op root cause); P859 (the bug this prevents).

## 2026-05-31 [technical]: Pledge + Agreement v4 — share oath TEXT via one constant (not a merged registry); grandfather via stored data + additive column; two specs for independent reversibility

**Context:** The verified-understanding v4 oath is the same for the unilateral pledge and the bilateral Clarity Partner Agreement (decisions.md 2026-05-31 [product]). The pledge is versioned (`PLEDGE_VERSIONS`, current v3); the agreement had no version registry — its certificate renders a per-row `clarity_agreements.terms_text` (custom scope) **plus** a hardcoded bilateral oath. Question: ship the shared v4 oath to both without (a) breaking the one existing real agreement, (b) coupling two artifacts that are identical now but may diverge, or (c) an irreversible prod change.

**Decision:**
1. **Share the oath TEXT, not the registry.** One versioned `VERIFIED_UNDERSTANDING_OATH` constant (yourRight/myPromise/exception) referenced by both `PLEDGE_VERSIONS[4]` and `AGREEMENT_VERSIONS[4]`. Each registry composes that body with its own artifact-specific framing (pledge: "I commit to everyone…"; agreement: "Clarity Partner Agreement", two signatures). Edit the constant once → both update; either can later point at different text without touching the other.
2. **Grandfather via stored data + an additive column.** The agreement's scope is already per-row (`terms_text`, untouched). Only the hardcoded oath is versioned: add an additive `agreement_version` column, backfill the existing agreement → legacy, render the oath from `AGREEMENT_VERSIONS[row.version]`. Pledge signers grandfather via the existing `profiles.pledge_version` column. No existing row's data is mutated beyond gaining a version tag.
3. **Two specs, not one.** P857 (agreement, ships first, creates the constant) and P855 (pledge) stay separate so each deploys and rolls back independently via a config flip of the current-version pointer — not one all-or-nothing deploy.
4. **No measurement.** Dropped the P853 falsification apparatus — a promise-only certificate has no event source and the live population is ~1 agreement. v4 ships as provisional wording behind the flag; the flag is the only safety mechanism.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Merge into one `*_VERSIONS` registry / one shared version number — couples grandfathering (the agreement's legacy entry has no pledge equivalent) and forces lockstep versioning, blocking future divergence. (b) Merge P855+P857 into one spec/deploy — mixes a public/ToS pledge change with a prod DB migration; can't roll back one without the other (violates the reversibility requirement). (c) Keep the oath hardcoded and edit it in place — would silently re-render the existing agreement to v4 (its oath is in code, not pinned). (d) Build a "mega skill" to sweep the oath across all surfaces — automates a workaround; single-sourcing the hardcoded React surfaces to the registry eliminates the drift class instead (`full-article.md` had already drifted to v1 under the manual-sweep regime).

**Consequences:** Reusable pattern for any text shared across versioned artifacts — extract a shared constant, compose per-artifact framing around it, version each artifact's registry independently. Grandfathering is free wherever the artifact stores its instance data per-row (agreement `terms_text`, `profiles.pledge_version`); it needs an additive column only where the text lives in code. Deploy order is load-bearing for the agreement: migration + version-aware rendering must land **before** the v4 text. Open: I-vs-we pronoun framing for the agreement oath (current agreement says "we", locked v4 says "I") — decides whether the constant is literally shared or needs a bilateral variant.

**References:** [features/p855_pledge_v4_number_first_upgrade.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p855_pledge_v4_number_first_upgrade.md); [features/p857_clarity_agreement_versioning_verified_understanding.md](../features/done/2026-04-22/p857_clarity_agreement_versioning_verified_understanding.md); `src/app/content/pledge-text.tsx` (PLEDGE_VERSIONS); `supabase/migrations/20260224150000_p422_clarity_agreements.sql` (`terms_text`); decisions.md 2026-05-31 [product] (the v4 model); P853 archived.

## 2026-05-31 [process]: Pre-commit `tsc --noEmit` is a no-op — the type gate never checks app code (use `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json`)

**Context:** P859 was a `ReferenceError: currentUser is not defined` that shipped to prod — `LetterReadingFlow` referenced an undeclared identifier (`currentUser`, where only `user` is in scope). TypeScript flags it as `TS2304` six times, so a working type gate would have blocked the commit. It shipped because `pre-commit-checks.sh:74` runs bare `npx tsc --noEmit`, which resolves the root `tsconfig.json` — a Vite "solution" file with `"files": []` + project `references`. With no input files, `tsc` compiles nothing and exits 0. So the pre-commit "TypeScript ✓" is vacuous; app/source code is never typechecked at commit time. `vite build` (esbuild) also strips types without checking. The real app typecheck, `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`, reports ~1117 errors.

**Decision:** Treat bare `npx tsc --noEmit` (no `-p`) as NOT a typecheck in this repo. To actually typecheck app code, run `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` (or `tsc -b`). Any session verifying a fix that touches types must use the `-p tsconfig.app.json` form. Remediating the pre-commit gate itself is tracked as **P861** (needs a baseline/ratchet strategy for the ~1117 pre-existing errors before enforcement is possible).

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Flip pre-commit to `tsc -b` now — blocks every commit on 1117 pre-existing errors; needs a cleanup/ratchet plan first (P861). (b) Trust `vite build` to catch type errors — esbuild doesn't typecheck. (c) Assume `tsc --noEmit` works because it's the standard invocation — false for the split-tsconfig (project-references) layout Vite scaffolds.

**Consequences:** Until P861 lands, undeclared identifiers and type mismatches can ship silently — code review + unit tests are currently the only real type-safety net. The double-sibling shape that caused P859 (P852 added `readerProfileOwner` to both `LetterReadingFlow` and `LetterReadingFlowPublic`, fixed only the public one in `182713b7`) is exactly the class a working type gate catches for free.

**References:** P859 (this fix); P861 (gate remediation); `scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh:74`; `tsconfig.json` (`files: []` + references); `tsconfig.app.json`.

## 2026-05-31 [process]: Commit all worktree WIP before pushing a feature branch — uncommitted imports surface as Vercel preview ENOENT failures

**Context:** Mid-/ship for P852, the user surfaced a Vercel preview error from the earlier feature-branch push. The preview build failed with `Could not load .../intensity-tutorial-modal (imported by letter-flow-content.tsx): ENOENT`. Root cause: `letter-flow-content.tsx` on the pushed tip imported `intensity-tutorial-modal`, but `intensity-tutorial-modal.tsx` existed only as uncommitted WIP in the worktree. Local dev server kept working because the worktree had the file; the failure was invisible until Vercel built from a clean clone. The file was eventually committed during /ship's dirty-worktree gate — at which point it was too late to spare the broken preview.

**Decision:** Before any `git push` of a feature branch, audit `git status --short` for un-committed files whose absence would break the branch as published — specifically new `.tsx` / `.ts` imported by committed files, new assets referenced by committed source, new env vars read by committed code. The dev-server-vs-CI asymmetry hides these consistently. Treat "preview deploy on push" as the cheapest CI you have; don't push a tip the build can't satisfy.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Always run `npm run build` locally before push — catches it but is slow, gets skipped under time pressure. (b) Configure Vercel to ignore missing files — masks real bugs. (c) Treat dev-server success as proof of build success — the failure mode here. (d) Lean on /ship's dirty-worktree gate — it fires at ship time, not push-feature-branch time; by then a broken preview has already wasted a build slot and an attention beat.

**Consequences:** Adds a 10-second `git status` audit before push. Pattern generalizes: any "worktree has the file, repo doesn't" asymmetry across branches. Specific tripwire to watch: new files added by an agent in this session that aren't yet `git add`-ed, when the agent's preceding edits *imported* them in already-committed files.

**References:** P852 Vercel preview build from 2026-05-31 07:08 UTC (deployment `claritypledge-bqy25v9uf`, ENOENT on `intensity-tutorial-modal`); resolved by commit `0955c52c` (IntensityTutorialModal + Round-F polish + UAT file) during /ship.

## 2026-05-31 [technical]: Apply prod migrations via Supabase Management API when `.env.prod` is absent — `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` + manual `schema_migrations` INSERT

**Context:** /ship p852 surfaced deploy-manifest drift on prod: migration `20260530161011` undeployed. The canonical path `./scripts/migrate.sh --env prod` requires `.env.prod` with `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (the prod pooler URL *with password*) + `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`. The repo had `.env.local` with `PROD_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `PROD_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, and `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, but no prod DB URL. Creating `.env.prod` would require retrieving the prod DB password out-of-band — high friction for a single migration with the ship gate already blocked.

**Decision:** When the canonical CLI path is unavailable, prod migrations can apply via the Management API in three steps:
1. `POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/<prod-ref>/database/query` with `Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `{"query": "<migration SQL>"}` — runs as `postgres`, executes any SQL (DDL or DML).
2. After the body applies, `INSERT INTO supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version, name, statements) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (version) DO NOTHING` — records the migration so a future `supabase db push` from a fixed `.env.prod` doesn't see drift and won't re-attempt.
3. Verify with three queries against the same endpoint: `SELECT version FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version = '<ts>'`, `SELECT proconfig FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = '<fn>'`, `SELECT pg_get_functiondef(oid) LIKE '%public.<expected_table>%' FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = '<fn>'` — proves the function settings, body, and schema-qualified refs all landed.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) Skip the gate and ship without prod migration — the new code expects the new RPC shape; unmigrated prod would silently regress (cover avatar wouldn't render for public readers). (b) Block /ship to retrieve prod DB password — wastes the gate-cleared state, breaks the flow. (c) Apply only the body without recording in `schema_migrations` — next `supabase db push` would either re-run the SQL (idempotent for `CREATE OR REPLACE` but redundant) or see drift forever depending on history-diff sensitivity. (d) Use this as the *default* path — loses the CLI's transaction wrapping, retry semantics, and full history-diff features.

**Consequences:** Management API is a legitimate emergency path for SECURITY DEFINER functions and other DDL when CLI auth is unavailable. Generalizes: any prod read or write where the script wants `SUPABASE_DB_URL` but only `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is available works through this endpoint. The manual `schema_migrations` INSERT is load-bearing — without it, the canonical CLI path stays "broken" forever. Apply the same approach to test DB when the equivalent test pooler URL is unavailable.

**References:** P852 /ship session (this entry); P852 prod migration `20260530161011_p852_public_reading_sender_avatar.sql`; canonical path: `scripts/migrate.sh`; manifest checker: `scripts/check-deploy-manifest.sh`.

## 2026-05-31 [process]: When cherry-picking a KDD commit, resolve `decisions.md` conflicts by inserting at chronological position, not in-place

**Context:** /ship p852 cherry-picked 33 commits from a 4-day feature branch onto main. Three of them (`4436b9d4`, `581ffc18`, `4b645b79`) added KDD entries to `docs/decisions.md`. Each one hit a 3-way merge conflict because main had accumulated newer entries (other 2026-05-29 / 2026-05-31 entries from parallel work) at the top since the branch was cut. Naive resolution — keep both sides between the markers and delete the markers — would have placed older 2026-05-29 entries *below* newer 2026-05-31 entries from HEAD, violating the file's "newest at top" invariant in three different places.

**Decision:** When resolving a `decisions.md` cherry-pick conflict, the resolution is *not* "keep both sides between the markers." It is "insert the incoming entry at its chronological position in HEAD." Concretely:
1. Identify the incoming entry's date and surrounding HEAD entries' dates.
2. Place the incoming entry between the next-newer HEAD entry and the next-older one, regardless of where the conflict markers sit.
3. Multiple incoming entries on the same date go together, in their original branch order.

Same pattern applies to any append-newest-at-top log: `hypotheses.md`, `INDEX.md`, dated changelogs.

**Alternatives rejected:** (a) In-place marker removal — corrupts chronological order whenever HEAD has newer entries above the conflict area; was the default failure mode. (b) `cherry-pick -Xtheirs` / `-Xours` — wrong granularity (whole-hunk preference, not by-entry). (c) Defer KDD commits to a single fix-up at the end of the merge — loses per-commit authorship and timestamps. (d) Stop using `decisions.md` for per-branch KDD entries — it works well for everything except cross-branch merging, which is rare.

**Consequences:** Pattern is mechanical and well-defined; cost is ~30s extra per conflict (one extra Edit to move the entry). For long-running feature branches (P852 ran 4 days), expect every KDD commit on the branch to hit this conflict. A scripted resolver could mechanize it (parse incoming entry's date, find HEAD's anchor positions, rewrite); not worth building until 3+ shipping sessions hit it again.

**References:** P852 ship cherry-pick journal: 4436b9d4 → d2381b55, 581ffc18 → aec4642f, 4b645b79 → b7f0472b. Pattern observed 3× in one /ship.

## 2026-05-31 [technical]: SECURITY DEFINER functions must use `SET search_path = ''` + schema-qualified refs — especially when callable by `anon`

**Context:** P852 code review surfaced `SET search_path = public` on the new `get_letter_for_public_reading` RPC (callable by `anon`). The Supabase / PostgreSQL hardening guidance for SECURITY DEFINER functions is `SET search_path = ''` + fully-qualified references — closes a known class of search_path-related issues that `= public` leaves open. The pattern in P852 was inherited from an earlier P725 RPC.

**Decision:** All new SECURITY DEFINER functions use `SET search_path = ''` and qualify every table/type reference with its schema (`public.clarity_letters`, `public.profiles`, `auth.users`, etc.). Applies whether or not the function is granted to `anon` — anon-callable is the highest-stakes case, but authenticated-only SECURITY DEFINER functions have the same exposure surface for any user who can create objects in a search_path schema.
